items.statement: Aquapharm expansion of 38,000 MTPA on track for commissioning by March 2025
items.quote: Aquapharm Chemicals expansion project of 38,000 metric tons per annum are on track and likely to be commissioned by March '25.

items.statement: New specialty line for conductive polymers and batteries started at Palej; details in 3-4 weeks
items.quote: So, we have already started work on a new specialty line. It will come up in Palej. And here, we are planning to manufacture premium grades for conductive plastics and batteries.

items.statement: International sales volume up; Europe and North America share rose to ~35% of international volumes in Q3
items.quote: And in the last quarter, we have done close to about 35% of our volume in these geographies.

items.statement: Carbon Black EBITDA per ton INR 19,868 in Q3; margins supported by operating leverage and product mix
items.quote: EBITDA per ton in Carbon Black business stood at INR 19,868 per ton.

items.statement: Aquapharm EBITDA run rate expected to reach INR 80-90 crores per quarter by Q4 FY26
items.quote: But EBITDA, for sure, we are confident that we should be reaching somewhere around at least INR 80-90 crores, if not more (the quarterly run rate).

items.statement: Carbon Black pricing formula-based with variable cost pass-through; realization depends on crude prices
items.quote: Negotiations mostly happen on the volumes. Because our pricing is also dependent on the movement in crude prices. So, the level of realization would also depend on the behaviour of crude prices going forward.

items.statement: Specialty Carbon Black sales volume visibility of 63,000-64,000 tons for FY25, up from 57,000 tons in FY24
items.quote: Last year, we did a total sales volume of 57,000 tons around that. And this year, we have visibility of somewhere around 63,000-64,000 tons on a full year basis.

items.statement: Russian Carbon Black imports impacting domestic margins in smaller consumer segments; ~30,000 tons annually from Russia
items.quote: India is importing just around 100,000 tons every year and about 30% of that is from Russia. It is not significant. But even to whatever extent they are selling (1,500-2,000 tons on an average monthly), to that extent there is some impact which we have to bear.

items.statement: European customer inventory elevated but normalizing; destocking in December quarter due to balance sheet considerations
items.quote: Currently, the customers appear to have a little elevated level of inventory. But despite that, our volumes in Europe and North America are going up.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA to improve from ~4.5x to 3.3-3.4x by FY25 end and below 3x by FY26 end
items.quote: Last year, we had a debt-to-EBITDA of about roughly 4.5. By this year end, we should be somewhere around 3.3-3.4. And a year from now, we should be below 3 for sure.

items.statement: Finance cost quarterly run rate ~INR 120 crores; expect reduction of INR 5-7 crores per quarter going forward
items.quote: My sense is that borrowing cost should go down by at least 3-4% in absolute terms. So, currently, we have about INR 120 crores quarterly run rate. Maybe we can see INR5-7 crores kind of quarterly reduction going forward.

items.statement: Operating margin for 9 months of current fiscal at 36 bps of AUM; current quarter at 37 bps but not to be extrapolated due to mark-to-market AUM growth
items.quote: Our operating margin for 9 months of the current fiscal came in at 36 basis points of AUM and for the current quarter, it came at 37 b asis points. It would be optimal to not extrapolate this 37-basis point number, as it looks better due to sharp rise in AUM, material part of which is led by mark -to-market

items.statement: Equity yield 58 bps, debt yield 28 bps, liquid yield 12-13 bps for the quarter
items.quote: Yes. So, the yields for equity for this quarter were around 58 basis points, for debt 28 basis points and for liquid is between 12 and 13 basis points.

items.statement: Key risk: extended market downturn could impact AUM (mark-to-market) and flows, though systematic transactions provide resilience
items.quote: The risk to our business, of course, because if you look at our AUM, the growth consists of two things. One is the mark -to-market. Th e second is the flows. If markets don't do well, which is the last couple of weeks, it impacts our AUM. If this kind of market trend continues for an extended period, it may also have an impact on the

items.statement: Three funds live in GIFT City subsidiary with AUM exceeding USD 150mn; aim to launch two new products this quarter
items.quote: Three of our funds are now live in our GIFT subsidiary with AUM exceeding USD 150 million. We aim to have two new products going live this quarter.

items.statement: 95% of transactions now processed digitally vs 69% in FY20
items.quote: Interestingly, 95% of our transactions are now getting processed digitally, a significant increase from 69% in FY20.

items.statement: Commission rationalization effective Aug 1, 2024 was a one-time exercise; full quarter impact visible in Q3 yields
items.quote: That was effective from 1st of August. So, we did bit of rationalization. It was a one-time exercise, 1st of August 2024 onwards.

items.statement: Awaiting final SEBI regulations for new asset class; team building products to capture opportunity when regulations finalized
items.quote: We are awaiting the final set of regulations. We will have products in this space as and when we get the final set of regulations. The team is working on creating the right set of products, which will help us gain share in this space too.

items.statement: Operating expenses (ex-CSR, NFO costs) to grow 12-15% annually; Q3 lower due to fewer NFOs and lower CSR
items.quote: I think our request has always been that, see, on an annual basis, overall costs, employees as well as other expenses, should grow between 12% to 13% or 15%, give or take, depending on how markets are.

items.statement: Tax rate varies around 25% corporate rate due to deferred tax on mark-to-market gains moving between short-term and long-term rates
items.quote: I think 25% is the corporate tax rate. Only the issue is th at for mark-to- market gains, there are long-term, etcetera, you have a deferred tax at a different rate, right? So that would mean that sometimes it comes at 23, 24, etcetera

items.statement: Balanced Advantage Fund largest actively managed equity-oriented hybrid fund in India with AUM >INR90,000 cr; full product suite across hybrid categories
items.quote: Our balanced advantage fund is the largest actively managed equity-oriented fund in India, hybrid fund, and dynamically managed I mean, current AUM would be like in excess of INR90,000 crores.

items.statement: NFO switch commission: HDFC AMC always paid lower of two commissions on switches, even before SEBI Dec regulation
items.quote: we have always been very pr udent, Shreya, on this front. We have been very particular about this. And in all our NFOs, we have ensured that on the switch, we pay the lower of the

items.statement: Management estimates a combined revenue hit of around 18% from regulatory changes, with a safety buffer of 20% one-time hit on first-year customer revenue.
items.quote: So overall, it would be safe to say that hit appears to be overall, combined everything, true-to-label and all that areas combined together, it would be around 18%. And if you look at our customer base growth, that remains intact.

items.statement: Management expects to recover 75-80% of the lost ancillary transaction income over the long term as client behaviour normalizes.
items.quote: So you've got to look at it from this way that in the long term once things settle down and the behaviour normalizes, we should be able to ideally recover almost 75%, 80% of this cost that we've been talking about in the past also.

items.statement: Reported consolidated EBDAT margin was 42% in Q3 FY25, down 787 bps QoQ; adjusted for ancillary income loss, compression was 257 bps.
items.quote: Our Q3 FY 2025 reported consolidated EBDAT margin stood at 42%, while this was lower by 787 basis points quarter-on-quarter as compared to our reported Q2 margins.

items.statement: Management is comfortable with operating profit margins around 50% and expects margins to remain in the current range until regulations are fully implemented and client behaviour normalizes.
items.quote: Otherwise, if you think it is temporary revenue of a customer, in terms of first year revenue, is going to revert back to normal, we would be okay with this pricing because we are seeing overall OPM would be around 5 0%. That is what we would be comfortable with.

items.statement: Introduced flat fee brokerage of ₹20 or 0.1% (min ₹2) for cash delivery and interest charges on non-cash collateral exceeding ₹50,000 from mid-November 2024.
items.quote: On the delivery side, we introduced the pricing of ₹ 20, or 0.1% with a minimum charge of ₹ 2 on the cash delivery side.

items.statement: MTF interest rate revised to 14.99% in November 2024, reducing interest income by nearly ₹102 million during the quarter.
items.quote: The revised interest rate of 14.99% on MTF introduced in November 2024 reduced our interest income by nearly ₹ 102 million during the quarter.

items.statement: Client base growing at a healthy rate of 40-45%; added 2.1 million clients in Q3 with 88% from Tier 2/3+ cities.
items.quote: The good part is that customer inflow in this market remains very healthy. So we are growing at 40-45%, and that trend continues.

items.statement: Cumulatively disbursed ₹600 crores in personal loans via the credit distribution platform; live with 3 lenders, integrating 3 more.
items.quote: So far, we have cumulatively disbursed ₹ 600 crores in personal loans on the platform. We are also integrating with 3 more lenders in the final stages and will scale in a measured manner.

items.statement: Received regulatory approvals for Mutual Fund (AMC) and Portfolio Management Services (PMS); launched wealth management brand 'Ionic Wealth' with offices in 7 cities and ~140 professionals.
items.quote: I am happy to share, Q3 FY '25 saw significant milestones, including the beta launch of insurance journey within the SuperApp. The regulatory approvals for launching our Mutual Fund under the aegis of Angel One Asset Management Limited and Portfolio Management Services under Angel One Wealth Limited.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution hit nearly 9 lakh unique SIP registrations in December 2024, highest ever; over 2 million SIPs for two consecutive quarters, ranking second largest in incremental SIP registrations.
items.quote: In the mutual fund distribution business, we achieved a major milestone in December 2024 with nearly 9 lakh unique SIP registrations, our highest ever. For the past two consecutive quarters, we have recorded over 2 million SIPs, reinforcing our position as the second largest player in the incremental SIP registration.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization costs increased 4.2% sequentially to ₹267 million in Q3 as infrastructure assets were capitalized.
items.quote: Depreciation and amortization costs increased by 4.2% sequentially to ₹ 267 million in Q3 as we capitalized infra assets.

items.statement: Regulatory changes (True-to-label, F&O framework, monthly expiry grouping) estimated to cause 13-14% hit on total net income, plus additional 3-4% from expiry grouping.
items.quote: At Angel One, we estimate a short-term impact of 13% to 14% on total net income due to these changes for the period of implementation till client behaviour adjustment, apart from market-driven softer volumes as evident since October 2024. Additional regulatory update on grouping monthly expiry for each of the exchange, 2 exchanges to 1 day of the week, would bring an additional 3% to 4% decline.

items.statement: Credit distribution business faces short-term headwinds from lender caution due to industry-wide KYC frauds, over-leverage, and delinquencies; scaling in a measured manner.
items.quote: While some headwinds may persist over the next couple of quarters, we are very confident that we will emerge stronger and continue to accelerate growth given that there is minimal legacy that we have to live with in this new paradigm.

items.statement: Board approved reinstatement of dividend distribution at 35% of quarterly consolidated profit after tax.
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that the Board has approved reinstatement of dividend distribution of 35% of quarterly consolidated profit after tax.

items.statement: 9-month FY25 gross total revenues and PAT stood at ₹41.9 billion and nearly ₹10 billion, growing 43.4% and 27% YoY respectively; 9M PAT is 88.6% of full FY24 PAT.
items.quote: Our 9-month FY2025 reported gross total revenues and profit after tax stood at ₹ 41.9 billion and nearly ₹ 10 billion, representing a growth of 43.4% and 27%, respectively, over the corresponding year last year.

items.statement: Targeting sustained OPM of 50% over the long term; price hikes will be considered if this trajectory cannot be maintained.
items.quote: So what we look at that we are focusing on business model, which can give an OPM of 50% on a very sustained and long-term basis.

items.statement: Regulatory impact of 18-20% on net revenue expected to be offset by 40-45% customer growth within 2-3 quarters, returning to Q2 revenue levels.
items.quote: Hit of revenue in terms of 20%, market normalizing and growth rate of customer to the tune of 40%, in 2-3 quarters, we'll be back to these numbers. Pure math, not predictions. Not forward looking statement. Yes.

items.statement: Customer acquisition growth rate remains intact at 40-45%; new customers show higher spending in years 2 and 3 and buy more products.
items.quote: But if you look at growth of this base remain intact because customers that are coming to the market are coming at the same numbers. And not only they are coming at the same numbers, in fact, their spending in second year, third year is increasing. They are buying more products.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution is #2 in incremental SIPs; credit disbursed ~Rs 600 cr; insurance in beta; wealth licenses and team in place; all verticals contributing to top line.
items.quote: If you look at mutual fund, as I said already, we are number 2 in terms of incremental SIP. In terms of credit, we have disbursed around ₹ 600 crores. Insurance journey, we have just did a beta testing. Wealth, we just got licenses and team is in place.

items.statement: Credit, wealth, mutual fund, and insurance expected to contribute to bottom line faster; AMC will take longer as focus is on right retail products.
items.quote: So business like credit, wealth, mutual fund, insurance business would be fast to contribute to bottom line. AMC, because we want to build a very sustained, a very large business will take its own time because we want to sell just right product which is for retail.

items.statement: Major regulatory changes already implemented; no further major changes foreseen; focus now on customer adaptation to new reality.
items.quote: I think whatever like major kind of like regulatory changes, which they had in mind, have already been implemented. I don't see any major kind of this thing coming now.

items.statement: Majority of fixed costs for new verticals already taken; CEO joining next financial year; no major fixed expense changes expected.
items.quote: First of all, on expenses side, almost we have taken a majority of expenses, except for our CEO would be joining maybe in our next start of the financial year. So otherwise, I don't see any major kind of changes in terms of fixed expenses.

items.statement: IPL marketing spend decision pending; will depend on market response when season starts; last year's spend yielded good benefits.
items.quote: And IPL, again, expenses are always is based on responses that we get when season starts. So it's just too early to comment on IPL part. But definitely, we would like to continue with our visibility and expenses that we did last year, we saw a good benefit from that.

items.statement: SuperApp strategy differentiated by equity-first sticky customer base and relevant financial adjacencies; operating at money deployment endpoint vs payment platforms' money flow.
items.quote: The point here is that our hero product has been equity. And in an equity, a customer has exposure on a platform and he is investing money, he is investing stocks, he is holding them, and therefore his ability to stay on the platform is far more longer than comparing, say, to a platform which is a payment-driven platform.

items.statement: Insurance distribution combines digital (motor insurance launched on app) and physical (feet on street) channels; claims support integration with insurers/lenders building over next quarters.
items.quote: On the digital distribution piece, we have just launched motor insurance on the app with the insurers. So that will scale over time. But on the physical distribution piece, we already have feet on street, and we've been doing some business on the insurance side there as well.

items.statement: Mutual fund distributor base nearly doubled in last 9 months; targeting 2 million POSPs; cross-pollination expected between broking, MF distribution, and insurance channels.
items.quote: We have almost doubled our mutual fund distributor base in the last 9 months. Now another vector of growth for us would be that you may come in as a mutual fund distributor or you may come in as a point-of-sale partner.

items.statement: Trade payables declined QoQ from Rs 9,400 cr to Rs 6,500 cr due to weaker market sentiment; expected to improve as sentiment recovers.
items.quote: Yes. Nidhesh, this is in trend with the weaker sentiments in the market. And when people trade more, they bring more money when people trade less, they keep lesser money. So this is nothing to worry about. As the market sentiments improve, we will see an improvement in the trade payables as well.

items.statement: Wealth management licenses and team in place; pipeline building; numbers expected to pick up now that regulatory approvals are secured.
items.quote: Look, these licenses that are required to run this game almost towards the end of the last quarter. We already have a fairly interesting pipeline, but we can only -- we could have only started once the relevant regulatory approvals came in place. So I think now that they are all behind us, we expect the numbers to start picking up from here.

items.statement: Optimistic about sustaining growth momentum into Q4 supported by deal ramp-ups, reversal of most furloughs, and continued BFSI strength; however, could be impacted by short-term headwinds from AI-driven productivity.
items.quote: We are optimistic about sustaining growth momentum into the fourth quarter supported by the deal ramp ups, reversal of most furloughs and continued strength in the BFSI vertical; however, it could be impacted by short-term headwinds on account of AI-driven productivity.

items.statement: Expect to improve margins in Q4, but absorbing the full impact of wage hikes may take longer in the current growth environment.
items.quote: While we expect to improve margins in Q4, absorbing the full impact of wage hikes may take a bit longer in the current growth environment.

items.statement: Confident that FY26 will definitely be better than FY25 based on order inflow and pipeline.
items.quote: So, that's the confidence we have now. Calling out specifics is a little difficult because the clients are still going through budgeting sessions and we are kind of working with them and as Nachiket rightly called out, I mean, there is a pressure in terms of doing more for less. That's why there are consolidation initiatives that we are working on. And we have been very well placed in those initia

items.statement: Signed record TCV of $1.68 billion in Q3, up 29% quarter-over-quarter, including a new manufacturing logo worth over $50 million and two large BFS deals.
items.quote: Additionally, we signed a record TCV amounting to US$1.68 billion, up 29% quarter-over-quarter. These wins included a new logo in manufacturing vertical worth over US$50 million as well as two large deals in the BFS vertical.

items.statement: EBIT margin declined 170 bps sequentially to 13.8% due to ~220 bps wage hike impact, partially offset by 50 bps cost optimization.
items.quote: The EBIT margin for the quarter was 13.8%, down from 15.5% in Q2. The 170-basis points decline was mainly due to wage hikes, which we estimated would impact margins by approximately 200 basis points.

items.statement: Wage hike impact recovery normally takes 2 to 3 quarters; full absorption may take a couple more quarters.
items.quote: Absolutely. It holds good and normally takes 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Deal pipeline strong with record order inflow; continuing client focus on cost reduction and vendor consolidation supports pipeline; AI spend shifting from POCs to scaled projects.
items.quote: In terms of the business outlook, there has been a promising increase in deal activity and the deal pipeline in Q3 as evidenced by a record order inflow in the quarter. The continuing client focus on cost reduction and vendor consolidation is supporting a strong pipeline.

items.statement: Passing on AI-driven productivity benefits to top Hi-Tech client; impact began ~2 months into Q3 and will extend into Q4 with full quarter impact.
items.quote: The entire theme of doing more with less and the productivity benefits that we are talking about, I think you can probably say at least two months within this quarter, and which will also extend into the next quarter.

items.statement: AI strategy driving deal wins across three pillars: AI in Everything, Everything for AI, and AI for Everyone; engaged with majority of customer base on AI initiatives.
items.quote: From a customer penetration standpoint, we are now engaged with the majority of our customer base across verticals on AI initiatives, demonstrating growing trust in our ability to drive impactful AI-led transformations.

items.statement: Political and economic uncertainties persist entering calendar year 2025 with new US government and potential policy changes making spending trends hard to predict.
items.quote: As we enter calendar year '25 political and economic uncertainties persist. With a new government in the US and the possibility of policy changes, predicting spending trend with certainty is challenging.

items.statement: Depreciation has not yet stabilized; some office buildings still under construction, so depreciation will probably go up a bit more before stabilizing.
items.quote: So, I think suffice it to say that in answer to your question, the depreciation has not yet come to a stable state. It will probably go up a bit more before stabilizing.

items.statement: Utilization excluding trainees dropped to 85.4% from 87.7%; may inch up slightly in Q4 as bench capacity deployed, aiding margins.
items.quote: Our utilization, excluding the trainees dropped further to 85.4% compared to 87.7% last quarter. This aligns with our focus on strengthening the bench Q3FY25 Earnings call January 16, 2025 capacity, enabling us to support our growth ahead

items.statement: Onboarded 2,362 employees in Q3, total headcount 86,800; attrition stable at 14.3%; third consecutive quarter of employee additions.
items.quote: In Q3, we onboarded 2,362 employees, bringing the year to date count to 5,150 new hires, reflecting a 6.3% increase compared to the previous year's end headcount. At the end of the quarter, our total headcount stands at 86,800. Attrition remains stable at 14.3%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to PAT improved to 126.3% from 74.2%; free cash flow to PAT improved to 106.8% from 54.5%; cash and investments up ~500 crores QoQ to 12,488 crores.
items.quote: We had a significant improvement in our cash conversion metrics in Q3, the operating cash flow to PAT improved to 126.3% as against 74.2% in Q2. Furthermore, free cash flow to PAT has shown a strong improvement to 106.8% compared to 54.5% in Q2.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for Q3 was 26.2%; expect FY25 effective tax rate in same range.
items.quote: The effective tax rate for the quarter was 26.2% as compared to 25.8% in Q2. We expect the effective tax rate for FY'25 to be in the same range.

items.statement: DSO improved to 80 days from 81 days, progressing toward aspirational target of 75 days.
items.quote: Our efforts towards our aspirational DSO target of 75-days are continuing, and in line with this we close the total DSO for this quarter at 80-days compared to 81-days in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue guidance of -1% to +1% sequential growth in constant currency
items.quote: For the next quarter, we are guiding for a sequential growth of ( -1%) to (+1%) in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue guidance in dollar terms of $2.602 billion to $2.655 billion in constant currency
items.quote: Our guidance for Q4 is (-1%) to (+1%) and therefore the dollar terms will be $2.602 billion to $2.655 billion. This is in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Operating margin at 17.5%, a 12-quarter high, up 0.7% QoQ and 1.5% YoY after absorbing two months of wage revision
items.quote: Our operating margins came in at 17.5%, an expansion of 0.7% quarter -on-quarter and 1.5% year -on-year. This is a 12 -quarter high.

items.statement: Confident of holding margins in a narrow band around 17.5% for Q4 FY25
items.quote: As we move into Q4, we are confident of staying in the narrow band.

items.statement: Discretionary spending slowly returning, clients cautiously optimistic, significant growth expected in AI spending
items.quote: Our clients are cautiously optimistic, and discretionary spending is slowly coming back. While cost optimization remains key, we expect significant growth in AI spending.

items.statement: Americas demand strong and picking up, Europe and APMEA remain soft with pipeline healthy at same level over last year
items.quote: we see Americas very strong, and the demand continues to pick up. While if you look at our b ookings into 1 million to 4 million and 5 million to 10 million range has been very strong. However, in Europe while the economies are challenged, whether we all know what is happening in Germany, UK or France, actually this has put some pressure on some o f our clients and some of the companies out there

items.statement: Capco business order book grew 9% YoY and revenue grew 11% YoY with improved demand
items.quote: Our Capco business continues to see improved demand. Order book grew by 9% year -on-year and revenue grew 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Hiring engine kicked off with plans to hire 10,000-12,000 campus hires per quarter next fiscal plus lateral hiring
items.quote: We have called out that for the next fiscal, we will be going every quarter on campus and hiring about 10,000 to 12,000 people, over and above that, we'll have lateral hiring happening.

items.statement: Board approved increasing payout to 70% or above of net income cumulatively over three-year block effective FY26, declared interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to share with you that the Board of Directors approved. Increasing the payout percentage to 70% or above of the net income cumulatively on a block of three -year period. This is effective FY26. Along with this the board has also declared an interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation and volatility noted as watch item for Q4 margins, hedge books in place
items.quote: Yes, the rupee has been depreciating. We'll have to keep a watch on it. It has remained volatile in the last few weeks. A lot has to play in. There are also certain hedge books. There's also a certain amount of hedges that we carry.

items.statement: Depreciation reduction likely to sustain at current normalized level with no one-offs
items.quote: I don't think there are any one-offs. It's likely to sustain. You can model it at the same level.

items.statement: APMEA and Europe soft but pipeline rebuilding with new leadership and go-to-market changes
items.quote: in APMEA, specifically, each of the countries we have Wipro Limited January 17, 2025 Public identified set of accounts and we are also differentiating ourselves with consulting rate at AI, which is definitely a different value prop to this market. The pipeline is being rebuilt, and we see the pipeline growing and I think we should continue to execute, we should see momentum coming back in APMEA. I

items.statement: PAT growth for FY25 expected to exceed 30-35%
items.quote: This robust performance positions us well to exceed our predicted 30% to 35% PAT growth for FY '25, as already told you to earlier.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat presales crossed INR 110 crores
items.quote: Construction has progressed to about 22% and presales have crossed over INR 110 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue 90-95% from land sales, rest from project sales
items.quote: And in terms of the breakup of the sales, we will land and this year, around 90% to 95% of the sale is coming from the land in this quarter, and the rest is coming from the project sales.

items.statement: Ahmedabad demand not dipping, prices increasing year-on-year for premium apartments and office complexes
items.quote: Ahmedabad demand doesn't seem to be dipping. In fact, yes, for the last 1 quarter, probably that's been a little slower than ever before. But because of the developments which are happening continuously in this area, the demand hasn't slowed down or it hasn't dipped for sure.

items.statement: Godhavi Township monetization on schedule for Q2 FY26 launch
items.quote: We believe that the earlier plan where we had earlier announced that we shall be working on the monetization of this in Q2 FY '26 is on schedule.

items.statement: Million Minds SEZ Phase 1 completion expected by end of Q4 FY25, fit-out possession by April-May 2025
items.quote: Million Minds SEZ Phase I, this marquee commercial venture is almost 1 year ahead of schedule, with completion expected by end of Q4 FY '25, that is this year, is expected to give possession for fit out by April-May 2025.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 1 lease rentals expected upwards of INR 70 crores per annum from FY26
items.quote: Upwards of INR70 crores, correct, per annum.

items.statement: Godhavi Township plotted development sales potential ~INR 5,000 crores over 7-10 years on 450 acres
items.quote: See, we have already given that number on a basic plot to plot give, where if you develop the entire area on the basis plotting side, it gives us roughly around the sales potential of INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: High EBITDA and PAT margins due to historically low-cost land bank and significant land sale revenue
items.quote: However, in our case there are -- meaning, our margins, net margins and our EBITDA margins are high because of 2 factors. One, a lot of our revenue and profits are derived from sale of land and not from projects. And secondly, the land also, whatever we have sold is 1 which has historically acquired about 7, 8 years back and that is why historical cost of that land was very low.

items.statement: One Thaltej commercial project construction to start next quarter after plan approval
items.quote: No, it is -- it may not be starting this quarter because we -- the approval of the plans have been submitted and the approval may or may not come by this quarter, but surely in the next quarter.

items.statement: Jantri rate revision impact uncertain, developers in wait-and-watch mode before launching projects
items.quote: At this point, it is ver y difficult to say exactly because nothing is certain. There have been all various ways, various values , various news, which has been coming in. but nothing really concrete

items.statement: Dividend payout decision by Board in next 4 months, last year payout >20%
items.quote: Dividend decisions will be taken at the end of the year by the Board. Yes, I mean we had given the dividend last time, that was a good payout of more than 20%, and we hope to...

items.statement: Future revenue mix to shift from land sales to project sales (Godhavi, Million Minds rentals, One Thaltej) from FY26
items.quote: Next year onwards, the way the project developments are happening, majority of that revenue would be from the housing from lease rentals from Godhavi and the like and maybe from One Thaltej also in terms of the projects after the execution.

items.statement: One Thaltej commercial project sellable pricing in range of INR 6,000-7,000 per sq ft
items.quote: That is largely in the range of 6,000 to 7,000, 6,500 you can say, 7,000 are sellable area.

items.statement: Million Minds SEZ Phase 1 received leasing inquiries for ~30 floors vs 14-15 floors available
items.quote: Though they are about 14 floors -- 14 of 15 floors including the general utility one, kind of marketing, which has been done and it's been continuously been happening at various road shows in various cities, top tier cities, we have got inquiries for leasing out almost 30 floors.

items.statement: H2 like-for-like growth guidance of around 5% maintained for Q4
items.quote: At the start of -- in my last call, we had spoken that in H2, we will be close to a 5% like -for-like that was the guidance, and we stick t o that number for the coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Global SS Beauty full-year revenue expected at INR240-250 crores at distributor price
items.quote: For the full year, we expect the Global SS Beauty business to achieve circa INR240 crores to INR250 crores of revenue and these sales were at distributor price to our retailers.

items.statement: Capex and deposits of INR141 crores spent year-to-date, expect INR90 crores more in Q4
items.quote: We have spent INR141 crores as capex and deposits year-to-date and expect to spend further INR90 crores in Q4.

items.statement: INTUNE store count at 59 as of Dec 2024, targeting 85 by March 2025 and 90-100 in FY26
items.quote: We said we have opened 59 stores as of 31st December 2024. We are planning to open another 26 stores in Q4, taking us to 85 stores in FY25, which is March 31, 2025. Next year, we are planning anywhere between 90 to 100 stores.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 20% driven by higher revenue, gross margin improvement from lower obsolescence and optimized markdowns, and cost control
items.quote: Our EBITDA increased by 20% due to increased revenue, increased gross margins owing to lower obsolesce and optimized markdown in private brands and a strong control on costs.

items.statement: Like-for-like cost increase contained at near 2%
items.quote: At the like -for-like level, the cost has increased just by or near 2%, and that's a testimony of the controls which we are trying to maintain at the cost level.

items.statement: Wedding season starting expected to boost sales; first 15 days of January tracking better than Q3 average
items.quote: The wedding season will start from tomorrow post the new Hindu month. We expect the weddings to continue and I'm confident that our India Weds with Shoppers Stop campaign will further boost our sales a nd customers during the quarter.

items.statement: Premiumization share of revenue increased from 55% to 64% over 2 years; premium non-apparel share up from 64% to 72%
items.quote: Our premiumization as a share of total revenue was circa 55% 2 years back, and it has now reached 64%.

items.statement: Store openings delayed by regulatory restrictions in North due to pollution/smog
items.quote: Because of regulatory restrictions, especially in North, we were not able to open the stores as per the plan.

items.statement: Loan book target of Rs. 4,000 crores in FY26 and Rs. 6,000 crores in FY27
items.quote: With this momentum, we can assure that we continue to maintain our targets of achieving loan book of Rs. 4,000 crores and Rs. 6,000 crores in Financial Year 826 and 827 respectively.

items.statement: ROE target of 18%-20% and ROA of 4%-4.5% on Rs. 5,000 crore loan book over next 2-3 years
items.quote: On this loan book, we expect to generate ROE of 18%-20% with ROA of 4%-4.5%.

items.statement: Equity capital of Rs. 1,000 crores plus Rs. 340 crores preferential capital over next 15 months
items.quote: as we stand today, the equity capital of the company is around Rs. 1,000 crores plus Rs. 340 crores have to come in preferential capital form over the next 15

items.statement: Anchor MoUs aggregate to about Rs. 5,000 crores program size with 40 anchors
items.quote: Overall, our anchors are 40 now and we have total program size signed off close to more than about Rs. 5,000 crores now.

items.statement: Yield maintained at 13% with cost of borrowing at 8.5%, spread of 4%
items.quote: Importantly, we continue to maintain our yield of 13% and the cost of borrowing is about 8.5%. So, our solid spread of 4% is maintained.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to come down but spread maintained at minimum 4%
items.quote: We expect it to come down, but we will ensure that we continue to maintain a spread of at least 4% and upwards.

items.statement: Disbursement run-rate reached Rs. 5,000 crores monthly, quarterly disbursements Rs. 4,625 crores
items.quote: Month-on-month have we reached a run rate of about 5000, answer is yes, but this will be much higher when we do the next quarter.

items.statement: Retail finance business to start next fiscal year with 4-5 large APL Apollo distributors
items.quote: In the next fiscal year only, please.

items.statement: NPAs low due to anchor support, 35-day gross disbursement cycle, zero NPAs so far
items.quote: we have developed with 0 NPAs and the gross disbursement cy cle, which comes out to be 35 days

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs. 500 crores NCDs soon with rating already obtained
items.quote: NCD, yes and we have also got a rating done of Rs. 500 crore s of NCDs. And yes, we plan to raise NCDs very soon

items.statement: Credit rating of AA, A1+ received from both ICRA and CRISIL
items.quote: We have already received credit rating of AA, A1+ from both ICRA and CRISIL Ratings.

items.statement: 24x7 banking system launch delayed to February 1st due to bank integration
items.quote: So, it will happen on 1st of February. We are delayed by 30 o dd days because of integration underway with the banks

items.statement: Processing fee charged annually at 25-100 bps on sanction limits, not utilization
items.quote: We renew it annually one year, so every year we charge he custom er a processing fee of around 25 basis points to about 75 basis points to 1

items.statement: Internal leverage limit of 3:1 debt-to-equity to be maintained conservatively
items.quote: Yes, at present that is the limit that we have kept and easily we got eq uity base of about Rs. 1,500 crores in FY27 and leverage of about 3x Rs. 4,500 crores with a book of about Rs. 6,000 crores

items.statement: Confident about sustaining growth momentum into Q4 FY25 supported by deal ramp-ups, reversal of furloughs, and BFSI strength, though AI-driven productivity may cause short-term headwinds
items.quote: We are optimistic about sustaining growth momentum into the fourth quarter supported by the deal ramp ups, reversal of most furloughs and continued strength in the BFSI vertical; however, it could be impacted by short-term headwinds on account of AI-driven productivity.

items.statement: Expect FY26 to be better than FY25, with margin improvement dependent on growth returning to double digits
items.quote: the order inflow that we have and whatever we have in terms of pipeline as we go along, that also gives us the confidence to say that FY'26 will definitely be better than FY'25

items.statement: EBIT margin declined 170 bps to 13.8% in Q3 due to wage hikes (~220 bps impact), partially offset by 50 bps cost optimization; expect margin improvement in Q4 but full wage hike absorption may take 2-3 quarters
items.quote: EBIT margin declined by 170 basis points to 13.8% as compared to 15.5% in the previous quarter. The impact on account of wage hikes came in at about 220 basis points, and the hikes were effective from first October and given to all eligible employees across the company.

items.statement: Margin recovery will be gradual in single-digit growth environment; double-digit growth in FY26 would accelerate margin expansion toward 17-18% medium-term target
items.quote: We had also spoken about in the investor day interactions that one of the biggest levers for margin to be recovered, is growth. And as long as the growth Q3FY25 Earnings call January 16, 2025 is in single digits, the other levers, the pace at which they work versus the growth lever, their pace is different

items.statement: Record TCV of $1.68 billion in Q3, up 29% QoQ, driven by new large deals, vendor consolidation wins, and strong renewals in BFSI
items.quote: Additionally, we signed a record TCV amounting to US$1.68 billion, up 29% quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Deal pipeline strong with continuing client focus on cost reduction and vendor consolidation; AI spend shifting from POCs to scaled projects in data and infrastructure
items.quote: In terms of the business outlook, there has been a promising increase in deal activity and the deal pipeline in Q3 as evidenced by a record order inflow in the quarter. The continuing client focus on cost reduction and vendor consolidation is supporting a strong pipeline.

items.statement: Hi-Tech vertical declined 5.5% QoQ due to passing AI-driven productivity gains to top client; impact to continue for full quarter in Q4 before stabilizing
items.quote: The productivity gain that we pass to the client and especially the top client, I think that will at least one more quarter we have to bear that before it stabilizes.

items.statement: BFSI vertical grew 8% YoY and 4.2% QoQ in constant currency with healthy growth in both Banking and Insurance
items.quote: Q3 growth was led by BFSI vertical which grew 8% year-over-year and 4.2% quarter-over-quarter in constant currency. Both BFS and Insurance witnessed healthy growth.

items.statement: Manufacturing vertical grew 1% YoY and 9.1% QoQ in CC, includes pass-through revenue and a $50M+ deal win using AI platform
items.quote: The Manufacturing and Resources vertical grew 1% year-over-year and 9.1% quarter-over-quarter in constant currency. This quarter included some pass-through revenue. We also won a deal worth over US$50 million in which we will manage the customers' application stack, ERP and infrastructure using our AI platform.

items.statement: Political and economic uncertainties persist entering CY25 with new US government and potential policy changes making spending trends hard to predict
items.quote: As we enter calendar year '25 political and economic uncertainties persist. With a new government in the US and the possibility of policy changes, predicting spending trend with certainty is challenging.

items.statement: Depreciation not yet stable; will increase further as office buildings under construction get commissioned, partially offset by lease rental rationalization
items.quote: Some of our office buildings are still under construction. So, we will see some more additions to the capital stock. And consequently, maybe a bit higher depreciation. But at the same time, as the buildings get commissioned and we get into our own buildings, some of the lease rentals also may see some rationalization.

items.statement: Added 2,362 employees in Q3, total headcount 86,800; attrition stable at 14.3%; utilization ex-trainees at 85.4%
items.quote: In Q3, we onboarded 2,362 employees, bringing the year to date count to 5,150 new hires, reflecting a 6.3% increase compared to the previous year's end headcount. At the end of the quarter, our total headcount stands at 86,800. Attrition remains stable at 14.3%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to PAT improved to 126.3% in Q3 from 74.2% in Q2; free cash flow to PAT improved to 106.8% from 54.5%
items.quote: We had a significant improvement in our cash conversion metrics in Q3, the operating cash flow to PAT improved to 126.3% as against 74.2% in Q2. Furthermore, free cash flow to PAT has shown a strong improvement to 106.8% compared to 54.5% in Q2.

items.statement: Cash and investments up ~500 crores QoQ to 12,488 crores ($1.45B) despite interim dividend and variable payout
items.quote: Despite a significant cash outflow due to interim dividend payment and mid-year variable payout, I am pleased to report that our cash and investment balances are up by almost 500 crores quarter-on-quarter and stood at 12,488 crores. This corresponds to US$1.45 billion.

items.statement: DSO improved to 80 days from 81 days in Q2, progressing toward 75-day target
items.quote: Our efforts towards our aspirational DSO target of 75-days are continuing, and in line with this we close the total DSO for this quarter at 80-days compared to 81-days in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Wage hikes effective Oct 1 impacted all eligible employees; full margin absorption expected to take 2-3 quarters
items.quote: The impact on account of wage hikes came in at about 220 basis points, and the hikes were effective from first October and given to all eligible employees across the company.

items.statement: Expect full revenue potential from Saudi Aramco project of INR180 crores from 2 KTA plant targeted by FY28-29
items.quote: Yes, INR180 crores is the potential of revenue which we can generate out of 2 KTA plant.

items.statement: Target Saudi Aramco revenue of INR40 crores for FY25-26
items.quote: We are looking at anticipating net financial year to close to reach a revenue of INR40 crores.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin around 30% for next couple of months to 1-2 years, then increase beyond with new contracts
items.quote: Currently, for a couple of months or a year or 2, we can expect around 30% margin. And then when we have new contracts coming up, and then you will see that the margins also increased beyond that.

items.statement: Target working capital cycle of 150-160 days in 2 years (FY27-28)
items.quote: As a finance person and a CFO, I would like to see the working cycle of the company after 2 years to around 150, 160 days, at least.

items.statement: Site 5 Greenfield first phase expected fully operational by Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our Greenfield Project at Site 5 in Panoli is also progressing as planned with first phase to expect fully to be operational by quarter 3 of financial year 2026.

items.statement: Site 3+ and 3++ construction and commissioning to complete by end of FY25, stabilization over next 3-4 months, then full commercial production
items.quote: We will look to complete the construction and condition of the plant by the end of this financial year. We look to stabilize this plant over the next 3 to 4 months, and then we see the full commercial production happening.

items.statement: Plan 2x expansion of R&D infrastructure with new R&D wing starting very near future
items.quote: In fact, minus your -- in 2025, you plan to take a 2x expansion of the R&D infrastructure and create an entirely new R&D wing, which will be a 2x expansion of the R&D assets and that will start taking the whole and doing expiration for that in the very near future and the designs of made up and that will represent a significant expansion.

items.statement: Finalized orders on first 2 products for Baker Hughes in January 2025, gearing up for ramp-up in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have finalized orders on the first 2 products in January 2025, which will be supplied from our site. We are gearing up for a ramp-up in Q4, which should further solidify our position in this market segment.

items.statement: Anticipate multiple significant product launches for Baker Hughes and other companies at Site 4 in very near future
items.quote: We anticipate multiple significant product launches in Site 4 for Baker Hughes other companies to sequentially kick in now in the very near future.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out, expecting potential uptrend post Chinese New Year
items.quote: While we have observed that the prices are likely bottomed out, we are expecting a potential uptrend to emerge post Chinese New Year, which could positively impact our future quarters.

items.statement: Solar power plant saves over INR150 million annually in energy costs, 31 MW solar provides >80% electricity from renewables
items.quote: This initiative is expected to save us over INR150 million annually in energy costs. With 31-megawatt of solar power pants now under our belt, we stand as the only company in the spec chem space to source approximately more than 80% of our electricity from renewable sources.

items.statement: CRAMS revenue for 9M FY25 equals 95% of full FY24, working on 50+ research projects, significant influx of new inquiries in agro, non-pharma, oil & gas, sustainability
items.quote: The CRAMS business model has continued to grow with our 9 months CRAMS revenue, being equivalent to 95% of the entire fiscal year '24 already. We are currently working on over 50 research projects in our CRAMS business model across all the sectors with the majority of the projects being in the non-pharma and non-agro sectors.

items.statement: Site 5 product mix vision: 25% pharma, 25% agro, 25% material sciences, 25% oil & gas
items.quote: And so broadly speaking, the vision of the company ultimately is to have a mix of product mix of 25% pharma, 25% agro, 25% material sciences, and 25% oil and gas majorly and Site 5 is really our largest production site will reflect this proportionate ratio.

items.statement: Site 2 back to full capacity after GPCB revocation in Jan 2025, currently at 62% utilization, expect 70-72% this quarter, max 80-85% next year
items.quote: The capacity utilization at site 2, it is approximately 62%, which I told before some time also. And we expect that in end of March '25 when the entire facility is now operational, we expect it to be around 72%. And maybe next year when everything is going okay, we do not expect it to go more than 80%, 85% because we will give 15% always in hand for some kind of overall maintenance.

items.statement: Revised revenue growth guidance to 4.5%-5% in constant currency for FY25; operating margin guidance unchanged at 20%-22%
items.quote: Based overall on our strong performance in this quarte r and our view for the rest of this financial year, we are revising our revenue growth guidance to growth of 4.5% to 5% in constant currency. Our operating margin guidance remains unchanged at 20% to 22

items.statement: Large deal TCV at $2.5 bn with 63% net new, up 57% sequentially; large deal pipeline stronger in Q3
items.quote: Large deal TCV for the quarter was at $2.5 bn, 63% of this being net new, which is an increase of 57% in net new deal TCV. Our large deal pipeline has become stronger in Q3.

items.statement: Discretionary spending improving in US Financial Services, European Financial Services, and US Retail/CPG; Manufacturing double-digit growth but European automotive slow; Hi-Tech and Telecom remain soft
items.quote: We have seen a revival in European Fi nancial Services during Q3. We are seeing an External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 4 improvement in Retail and consum er product industry in the U.S. with discretionary pressures easing. Automotive sector in Europe continues to remain slow. Demand trends remain stable in other industries, with clients continuing to prioritize cost takeout over discretionary

items.statement: McCamish cybersecurity incident: eDiscovery complete, six class action suits filed in December, court ordered mediation process underway; no additional comments on business impact
items.quote: in December there were six different class action suits that were filed. The court has decided at the end of December to club or join all of them and allow for what is called a mediation process and that is the step that is underway today

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue guidance to 4.5% to 5% in constant currency; operating margin guidance remains 20% to 22%
items.quote: Driven by our performance and outlook for the rest of the year, we are revising our FY'25 revenue guidance to 4.5% to 5% in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Operating margin expanded to 21.3%, up 20 bps sequentially and 80 bps YoY
items.quote: Operating margins expanded to 21.3%, which is an increase of 20 bps sequentially and 80 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Realization increased 3.6% over 9 months from value-based selling, expanding YTD margins by 30 bps
items.quote: We are very pleased with the continued success of Project Maximus, which has resulted in benefits across various tracks. One such area is realizat ion, which has increased by 3.6% over 9 months, resulting from strong performance emanating fr om value-based selling track

items.statement: Financial Services US discretionary spend increasing; Europe revival; Retail US showing signs of recovery in discretionary spend
items.quote: Financial services in the U.S. continues to see discretionary spend increase in capital markets, mortgages, cards and payments, which led to another quarter of volume growth. We have also seen a revival in Europe leading to Q3 backed by some large deals.

items.statement: Manufacturing weak in European automotive but momentum in engineering, IoT, supply chain, cloud ERP, digital transformation
items.quote: Manufacturing continues to see weakness in the automotive in Europe. However, there is a continued momentum in areas such as engineering, IoT, s upply chain, cloud ERP and digital transformation

items.statement: Communication sector volatile with soft discretionary spending; EURS macro headwinds persist; Hi-Tech remains soft with clients reducing run cost
items.quote: Communication sector continues to face volatile macro environment, leading to growth challenges and rising opex pressure. Discretionary spending c ontinues to be soft and current year growth is driven mainly by recent large deal wins focused on efficiency and consolidation

items.statement: Free cash flow for quarter at $1.26 bn, up 51% QoQ and 90% YoY; 9-month FCF surpassed full year FY24 FCF
items.quote: For the quarter, our free cash flow s were at $1.26 bn, up 51% over last quarter and up 90% over the same period last year. FCF as a percentage of net profit for 9 months was 136

items.statement: Q4 guidance implies negative sequential growth due to third-party seasonality, lower working days, and furloughs
items.quote: Ankur, there are two parts, as you rightly said. O ne is, of course, the third-party seasonality, which is baked in Q4 guidance because Q3 was significant ly higher. And Q4 also has lower working days and calendar days

items.statement: Headcount grew by ~5,600 sequentially to 323,000; attrition low at 13.7%; utilization ex-trainees at 86%
items.quote: Headcount at the end of quarter stood at 323,000, growing sequentially by approximately 5,600. This is the second consecutive quarter of headcount addition. Attrition remains low at 13.7%.

items.statement: Third-party costs higher in Q3 with seasonality; not expected to change significantly in next few quarters
items.quote: So Yogesh, at this point in time, we do not expect this to change significantly but it is also a factor of the large deals or the megadeals that come in at ti mes, right

items.statement: Wage hikes rolling out in two phases from Jan 1 and Apr 1; India avg 6-8%, overseas low single digit; most employees get increase in Q4
items.quote: So Ashwin, as we have said earlier, our comp roll-out is going to happen in two phases. First phase starting 1st January and the second phase will star t from 1st April. The India wage increases would be, on an average, 6% to 8

items.statement: AI and GenAI creating broader opportunities; agents and small language models deployed in production; seeing growth potential
items.quote: So the way we are seeing it today is, the areas which can be addressed by agents. We are building about 100 new agents which expands the opportunity that we have to do this sort of work. So at this stage, it looks to us like this will give us over time more growth.

items.statement: Utilization comfort zone 83-85%; currently at 86% ex-trainees; not expected to change significantly
items.quote: Yes. So we have generally said 83%- 85% of utilization is a range that we are more comfortable with. 86% is a little bit above our comfort level but we do not expect it to change significantly either way.

items.statement: Small deal pipeline stable; large deal pipeline stronger; overall pipeline grown
items.quote: The smal l deal pipeline remained stable as compared to last quarter. As Salil said, our large deal pipeline has grown. So our overall pipeline, therefore, has become stronger

items.statement: Recruitment mix of freshers and laterals; FY25 target 15,000+ freshers; FY26 target 20,000+ freshers
items.quote: So I think recruitment is a combination of both freshers and laterals. Again, we have not broken up this number. But for the year, we will hire 15,000 pl us freshers in line with our original commentary. And for the next year we are expecting 20,000

items.statement: Committed to achieving 15% EBIT margin by FY27
items.quote: we are mak ing concerted efforts to improve our organization and to drive productivity gains and price optimization to achieve a 15% EBIT margin by FY27

items.statement: Committed to delivering higher than peer average growth by FY27
items.quote: I do feel confident that it will allow us to first catch up with, and then to deliver higher than peer average growth which we have committed to in FY27.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 net new deal wins of $745 million; LTM deal wins improved to $2.4 billion
items.quote: We report new deal wins of $745 million for Q3 FY25 on the back of several large and multi tower deals in the Telecom and Manufacturing sectors. On an LTM basis, our deal wins have improved to $2.4 billion in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBIT margin expanded 60 bps sequentially to 10.2% despite currency headwinds
items.quote: We have also reported EBIT margins of 10.2%, which is about a 60 basis points expansion from the last quarter despite the steep currency headwinds and the ongoing investments.

items.statement: Wage hike in Q4 FY25 expected to impact margins by 1%-1.5%
items.quote: So, from a wage hike perspective we have announced that to be in the current quarter Jan-Feb-March. So, that's the decision we have taken, I think that definitely will impact margins to the tune of 1% - 1.5%.

items.statement: Calendar year 2025 expected to be an incremental improvement over 2024, not a V-shaped recovery
items.quote: But I would say on the whole if you look at it from a calendar year perspective, 2023 was probably the worst, 2024 was an improvement over 2023 and we feel that 2025 will be an improvement over 2024. But it is an incremental improvement. It is not sort of a V shaped recovery but we do see that 2025 should be better than 2024.

items.statement: Onboarded 40+ new clients from must-have account list in current fiscal year, 12 in Q3; over two dozen now at $1M+ annual run rate
items.quote: I am really proud to announce that we have on boarded 40-plus new clients from a must-have account so far in the current fiscal year, of which 12 were onboarded in the December quarter itself. Over two dozen accounts from this must-have list have now crossed a revenue run rate above $1 million annually.

items.statement: Investing in GenAI capability build, training tools, partnerships, fresher induction, learning platforms, service line capabilities, and portfolio company integration
items.quote: We continue to consistently induct freshers to address long term pyramid change from an organization perspective, and also supplement that with a learning and development platform, both physical as well as from a software perspective. We also are investing in building service line capabilities in modernizing tools and platforms for delivery excellence.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by pricing excellence, cost optimization under Project Fortius, and efficient delivery
items.quote: We attribute this gain to efficient delivery, pricing excellence and cost optimization under project Fortius.

items.statement: Cross-currency headwinds impacted reported revenue; forex losses may persist if INR depreciates further
items.quote: If INR continues to depreciate against the US dollar, then from that aspect the hedges work the opposite way, and cross currencies are the bigger one. So, cross currencies while we have the hedging that flows in the other income but it's not given the steep decline that you see on a reported currency basis not enough to offset that.

items.statement: Telecom deal activity growing but largely consolidation and cost-focused, not incremental discretionary spend
items.quote: Yes. So, look I think again there are always headwinds and tailwinds. But yes, you know client deal activity in telecom is growing. But I would again stress that a lot of it remains sort of consolidation and cost focused rather than incremental discretionary spend at this time.

items.statement: Free cash flow of $199 million in Q3 FY25, 172% PAT conversion; DSO improved to 88 days
items.quote: When you look at the free cash flow, we had a robust free cash flow of $199 million, which translates to 172% of PAT conversion. Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter was $799 million, or in rupee terms, Rs. 6,841 crores. We look at the DSO including unbilled, we were at 88 days, which is a reduction of six days on a sequential basis and an improvement of three days on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for Q3 FY25 was 23.8%; YTD rate 26% within guided 26%-27% range
items.quote: When you look at the tax rate, the effective tax rate for the quarter was 23.8%, while low for the quarter, the YTD number is 26% as the range that we had mentioned for our expected ETR to be 26% to 27%.

items.statement: Hedge book at $2.1 billion; mark-to-market loss of $4.7 million for the quarter
items.quote: When you look at the total hedge book, we stood at $2.1 billion for the quarter, as against $2.3 billion last quarter. And b asis on our hedge accounting, the mark-to-market loss for the quarter was $4.7 million, out of which $0.7 million was taken to the P&L as gain, and the rest was carried as losses of $5.4 million towards balance sheet

items.statement: Analyst rating top quadrant positioning improved from 81% to 88%
items.quote: I am happy to announce that we have improved our position in analysts rating top quadrants from 81% to 88% for the same period this year.

items.statement: Flash Electronics expected to achieve revenue over INR 1,500 crores in FY25 with CAGR over 17% and EBITDA margin around 14% with ROCE over 22%
items.quote: Flash Electronics is expected to achieve revenue over INR 1,500 crores in FY25. And has been impressively delivering a CAGR of over 17% during the past years. The company is expected to deliver EBITDA margin of around 14% with a steady ROCE of over 22%.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY25 expected revenue about INR 1,590 crores with CAGR revenue of about 17% over last 5 years
items.quote: The FY25 expected revenue is about INR 1,590 crores with the CAGR revenue of about 17% over the last 5 years.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY24 revenue INR 1,340 crores, EBITDA INR 185 crores at around 14% margin, free cash flow INR 120 crores, ROCE 22% plus
items.quote: The FY24 highlights revenue were INR 1,340 crores, EBITDA reported was INR 185 crores at around 14% ma rgin, free cash flow has been INR 120 crores, and ROCE has been 22

items.statement: Flash Electronics EV revenue doubled from 13% to about 20% in first half of FY25, expects to double EV revenue by end of year
items.quote: I'm happy to share in first half of FY25, EV revenue now constitutes to about 20%, doubling from the last year. So, by end of this year, Flash Electronics expects to double its revenue coming from EV.

items.statement: Combined EV kit value in 2-wheeler segment expected to be INR 30,000 to INR 35,000, potentially up to INR 40,000 to INR 45,000 with premiumization
items.quote: The overall kit value in the EV segment, in the 2-wheeler segment, MCL offers products in the range of INR 12,000 to INR 15,000, and Flash Electronics will offer currently about INR 18,000 to INR 20,000, totalling our kit value of about INR 30,000 to INR 35,000, and this is expected to grow even higher.

items.statement: Transaction valued at enterprise value INR 31 billion and equity valuation INR 28 billion, Minda to acquire 49% stake for cash consideration INR 1,372 crores, closing likely by 31st January
items.quote: The transaction is valued at the enterprise value of INR 31 billion and equity valuation of INR 28 billion. Minda Corporation will acquire a 49% stake in Flash Electronics and this will be an all cash deal. The deal does not require any regulator y approval and closing is likely to be by 31st January within this month

items.statement: Post-investment, Minda Corporation balance sheet remains strong with net debt to equity below 0.6x and proforma net debt to proforma EBITDA less than 1.8x
items.quote: The impact on financials post the investment, Minda Corporation balance sheet continues to remain strong with net debt to equity below 0.6x and proforma net debt to proforma EBITDA less than 1.8x.

items.statement: Flash Electronics PAT expected to be in range of about INR 110 crores by end of FY26 when Minda Corporation accounting happens
items.quote: Which is more relevant for us, by end of FY26, which is where the accounting of Minda Corporation will happen, that is into the range of about INR 110 crores as PAT.

items.statement: Flash Electronics investing about INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores annually, expected to continue in same range from free cash accruals
