items.statement: Q4 expected to be in similar line as Q3 on top line growth and other metrics; confident of delivering double-digit growth guided for the year
items.quote: We are happy to say that we find that t he Q4 is also expected to be in similar line as Q3, whether it comes on a top line growth or other metrics. And we are confident of definitely delivering on the double-digit growth that we have promised and guided the market on from the previous year

items.statement: Target to open 25 hotels in current financial year, up to 30 hotels in following financial year
items.quote: And with 20 hotel openings so far, we are well on track to achieve our committed target of opening 25 hotels in the current financial year, which we have also guided would go up to 30 hotels as of the following financial year.

items.statement: Renewable energy target 50% by 2030, currently at 37%; 100% recycled water by 2030, currently at 48%
items.quote: We have given the guidance of 50% as a source for renewable energy by 2030, and we are already at 37% and 100% use of recycled water by then by 2030.

items.statement: Sea Rock construction expected to commence in second half of this year after receiving IOD and progressing on height approval
items.quote: We think that we have got very close so that construction could commence in the second half of this year.

items.statement: Signed 55 hotels and opened 20 hotels in April-December FY25; portfolio at 360 hotels with pipeline of 123 hotels as of 31st December 2024
items.quote: In the current financial year for the period April to December, we have signed 55 new hotels and opened 20 hotels. We have set a new growth benchmark with 85 signings and 40 openings i n the calendar year 2024, taking our portfolio to 360 hotels with an industry-leading pipeline of 123 hotels as on 31st December 2024

items.statement: Ginger EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 45%; expect Lean Luxe and New Ginger to perform at north of 50%
items.quote: Ginger's consolidated revenue grew 43% year-on-year to INR157 crores, while expanding EBITDA margin by 200 basis points to 45%. We have guided previously that we expect Lean Luxe and New Ginger's to keep performing at north of 50%.

items.statement: RevPAR growth driven by ARR increase rather than occupancy; pricing still below levels from 15-16 years ago on dollar per room night basis; currency tailwinds favorable
items.quote: I think the point number two is that even if you look at on a dollar per room night basis, we continue to be lower than even what we were 15 years back or 16 years back. I think that's a very important factor as you think about the economics of this sector.

items.statement: Demand continues to outpace supply; Q4 expected strong with Mahakumbh, Coldplay concerts, extended wedding season; Q1 FY26 also looking good with wedding season
items.quote: With large-scale events like Mahakumbh, conce rts like Cold Play and the extended wedding season in Q4, we remain confident of delivering all the metrics and the guidance that we have guided the market upon

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals still below pre-COVID levels; potential upside when they normalize to 110-120% of pre-COVID
items.quote: We are still at a lower end on the pre-COVID. Normally, it should in at least 120% of the pre-COVID level by now because -- we are talking about 2019, 2020 figures. And we're in 2024'-'25.

items.statement: Management fees grew 32% YoY to INR177 crores driven by 13% net unit growth, RevPAR increase, technical fees and new brand fee streams
items.quote: On the back of our capital-light growth strategy, our management fees in Q3 was INR177 crores, an increase of 32% over the same period last year. This was driven by 13% net unit growth in hotel rooms, increase in total revenue per available room, technical fees and new fee income streams such as brand fee.

items.statement: Tata Neu loyalty program reached 8 million members with 40% enterprise revenue contribution; enterprise NPS at 74 for YTD FY25 vs 72 last year
items.quote: Our collaboration with Tata Neu, loyalty platform has now 8 million members with loyalty-led contribution in revenue rising to 40% of our enterprise level revenue. The unwavering loyalty of our customers is visible in our increasing enterprise NPS scores, which stood at 74 for year-to-date, '24-'25, up from 72 in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Digital transformation progressing: new websites for Ginger and Vivanta to go live in H1 FY26; migrating to SAP for finance/HR and OPERA cloud PMS
items.quote: Progress is well underway on new websites for Ginger and Vivanta, which will go live in H1 '25-'26. And additionally, significant progress is being made in upgrading our core systems including the migration to SAP for finance and HR functions and industry-leading OPERA on cloud PMS.

items.statement: Export revenue projected at INR550-600 crores for FY25 driven by Q4 pickup
items.quote: For this financial year, we project export revenue to reach approximately INR550 crores to INR600 crores driven by pickup in demand in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Alloy wheel volumes expected to grow 35-40% in FY26
items.quote: And we have a hope of improving that number of current year performance of alloy volumes by 35% to 40% in next financial year.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckle revenue expected at INR14-15 crores in Q4 FY25, INR80 crores in FY26, INR105-115 crores in FY27
items.quote: Next year, it is going to be INR80 crores for financial year '25-'26. Next to next year on the same capacity without expansion -- if expansion happens, obviously, the turnover will change. But without expansion, INR105 crores to INR115 crores is visible with double-digit margin.

items.statement: Capex of INR150-160 crores each for FY26 and FY27 funded from internal accruals
items.quote: INR150 crores to INR160 crores will come into this financial year, which is '25-'26 and '26-'27 year, INR150 crores will be spent. All will be spent from internal accruals. No borrowings will be needed.

items.statement: Export order book visible at INR175-180 crores for Q4 FY25
items.quote: The order book is close to INR175 crores, INR180 crores. But because of the model mix that we are trying to see, I think INR155 crores to INR160 crores will be doable.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel stabilized at INR260, targeting INR275-280 in next 2 years
items.quote: And trajectory looks like that over the next 2 years, we are going to be at INR275 to INR280, is what the intent is with all exports, all alloy, all knuckles coming into action in '26-'27.

items.statement: Brownfield alloy wheel expansion targeting 25% ROCE, breakeven at 55-60% utilization for knuckles
items.quote: See, these are all brownfield projects. So obviously, these are going to be very aggressive in terms of the ROCEs. And I believe that, 25% for the brownfield? So for the brownfield projects, I think 25% is where we are trying to and it is fairly possible.

items.statement: Tractor segment achieved high sales growth in 9M FY25, expects 20%+ growth for full year
items.quote: And for the entire year, we expect that number to be at least 20% higher than what we did in last year. And this year probably will be the best year that we ever had in terms of tractor wheel sales.

items.statement: CV segment decline halved from expected 10-12% to ~5-6% based on Q4 order book
items.quote: I guess at the start, we have given a number of almost 10% to 12% odd of downtick on our CV number. But I guess we'll be somewhere around half of that looking at the kind of numbers that we have.

items.statement: Alloy wheel penetration to rise from 32% to 40% in 4-5 years, targeting 50% industry share
items.quote: Currently, alloy contribution is around 32%, right? And it will shift to around 40% in coming 4 to 5 years, right? And balance is from the steel wheel.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckle commercialization started at 2.5 lakh units/annum, doubling to 5 lakh in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our new aluminum knuckle segment commenced commercialization this quarter with an initial capacity of 2.5 lakh units per annum. This capacity is set to increase to 5 lakh units in the fourth quarter, enabling us to cater to our existing customers, including the two OEMs with whom we have established agreements as well as attract new customers.

items.statement: US election uncertainty caused inventory correction, but Trump tariffs on China expected to benefit India exports
items.quote: I think the Q4 is going to be the strongest quarter for exports, given that there is a transformation thing which is happening in the US. I think today is the ceremony, and we believe that very harsh measures on taxation can come on to various countries wh ere they are trying to import materials. And India can skip a lot of this salvage

items.statement: Total debt INR962 crores (INR406 crores long-term, balance short-term), no new borrowings planned
items.quote: The total debt is around INR962 crores, out of which around INR406 crores is of the long term and balance is the short-term debt.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckle realization at INR2,500-2,600 per unit, weight 4.2-4.5 kg
items.quote: It's around INR2,500 to INR2,600 per knuckle.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity expanding from 4.2M to 4.8-5.3M by Sep-Oct FY26, 90% utilization targeted
items.quote: This capacity will get further enhanced to 4.8 million sometime around September, October. There is some debottlenecking exercise that we are also doing, which probably will raise it further to 5.3 million.

items.statement: No specific FY26 revenue or margin guidance provided; focus on becoming top 3 global optical player, scaling connectivity attach rate, completing services demerger, and reducing debt
items.quote: We don't have any specific numbers to guide at this point about FY26.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected around Rs.120-130 crores, mainly maintenance and interconnect investment
items.quote: In fact, if you look at our capital spend for the year, it will probably be around Rs.120-130 crores maximum.

items.statement: Consolidated open order book stands at Rs.9050 crores as of Q3 FY25, diversified across segments
items.quote: Based on our strong new order book addition during the last quarter, despite of the significant order de scoping, our open order book stands at Rs.9050 crores as of Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Optical networking EBITDA margin at 12.9% in Q3 FY25; target 20% EBITDA margin requires 70-75% capacity utilization
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stands at Rs.119 crores at 12.9% of the revenues.

items.statement: Digital business achieved first EBITDA positive quarter at Rs.4 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are happy to share that STL digital business EBITDA stands at Rs.4 crores.

items.statement: Realizations down 20-30% from 2019 peak in US and Europe; expect improvement as demand recovers
items.quote: I would argue that depending on the market, we are probably between 20-30% down in realization.

items.statement: North America demand projected to grow from 70-80M to 120M+ fiber km annually; BEAD ramp expected H2 CY25, significant CY26
items.quote: To give you ballpark, this broadly should lead to demand in North America going from current base of 70-80 million fiber kilometers to north of 120 million kilometers annually.

items.statement: India data center GPU capacity expected to reach 5.2 lakh GPUs by 2026; BharatNet advanced purchase orders releasing soon
items.quote: In India, GPU based server capacity in AI driven data centers expected to reach 5.2 lakh GPUs by 2026.

items.statement: Data center and enterprise suite contributed 22% of optical networking revenue in Q3 FY25; connectivity attach rate sustained above 20% for three quarters
items.quote: We are proud to report that 22% of this quarter's revenues came from our data center and enterprise Suite products.

items.statement: Services demerger final NCLT hearing scheduled Jan 30, 2025; approval expected Q4 FY25, listing thereafter
items.quote: The final hearing date is scheduled on January 30, 2025, with NCLT Mumbai bench. The final approval is expected in Q4 FY25 after which resulting company is anticipated to be listed on a stock exchanges.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs.2195 crores; finance cost down Rs.50 crores YoY in 9M; quarterly interest cost expected to decline further from Q1 FY26
items.quote: The net debt of the business stands at Rs.2195 crores.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales volume target of 3.1-3.2 million tons and absolute EBITDA slightly better than FY24's INR1,192 crore
items.quote: So based on these factors, we are confident that we shall achieve 3.1 million to 3.2 million tons of sales volume for full year. And absolute EBITDA slightly better than last year because there was a lot of mix on the earnings front in the second quarter.

items.statement: FY26 sales volume target of 4 million tons and FY27 target of 5 million tons maintained
items.quote: Now that we are ready with 4.5 million ton s capacity going to 5 million tons over the next 12 months, so we do maintain our sales volume target of 4 million tons by FY '26 and 5 million tons by FY '27

items.statement: Residual capex of INR6 billion to reach 5 million tons capacity, funded from internal cash flows over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: The residual capex for these new plants and to reach 5 million tons is around INR6 billion, which will be funded from internal cash flows over the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Capacity to reach 5.5 million tons with additional capex for new plants in Siliguri, Gorakhpur, Ahmedabad, Malur and Dubai expansion
items.quote: Everything is there – Siliguri, Gorakhpur, Ahmedabad, Malur, 4 new plants and some capacity build up in Dubai, we are increasing it. So, all of that is there.

items.statement: Operating leverage benefit of INR400-500 per ton over next 1-2 years as capacity utilization rises from 3.3 to near 5 million tons
items.quote: So, there is INR400 to INR500 per ton operating leverage benefit, what we see over the next 1 to 2 years as we utilize near 100% levels.

items.statement: Value-added product mix improvement from Raipur and Dubai plants gives visibility for INR400-500 per ton EBITDA spread expansion
items.quote: Then value-added product mix improvement coming from our Raipur and Dubai plants. Again, it gives us visibility for INR400 to INR500 per ton expansion in our EBITDA spreads.

items.statement: Discounting of INR300-350 per ton currently; INR100-200 per ton pulled back in first 20 days of Q4
items.quote: So, Sneha till now whatever trends we see in the first 20 days of the quarter, ongoing quarter we see INR100 to INR200 per ton discounting pull off has been done by our sales team

items.statement: At 5 million tons capacity, general segment ~1.5 million tons, value-added ~3.5 million tons; general segment growing faster due to sponge iron to HR coil transition
items.quote: As far as t he mix is concerned, at 5 -million-ton capacity, the general segment is around 1.5 million tons and 3.5 million tons is the value-added product, okay

items.statement: Raw material supply disruption at Raipur from Tata Steel caused 5,000-10,000 ton volume loss in Q3; resolved from January
items.quote: If you look at the expanded capacity in Raipur, which is 1.2 million tons, the utilization rate is 55%, it would have been higher in Q3, but because of raw material situation like lack of raw material availability in Raipur from one of our steel suppliers, there was loss of volume.

items.statement: New products: 1000mm square launched this quarter, Galvalume next quarter, quarterly product innovation pipeline
items.quote: We have a new product of 1000 mm squa re in this quarter. In next quarter, we will have a new product of Galvalume. In Q1, Galvalume – quarter-on-quarter we will keep bringing a product for innovation

items.statement: Cold rolling capacity ~2 million tons currently, targeting ~1.65-1.7 million tons at 5.5 million tons total capacity; 30% of portfolio requires thinner gauges
items.quote: If we take 5.5, then we should have nearby 30% capacity of 1.65 million tons -- 1.7 million tons.

items.statement: Middle East sales at 16,000-17,000 tons/month; Dubai capacity expanding from 300,000 to 500,000 tons/month; service improvement driving destocking and order recovery
items.quote: We are going to the second round of phase of capex in Dubai. Our capacity was of 3 lakh tons there. We are extending from 3 lakhs tons to 5 lakhs tons per month.

items.statement: Un-executed order book stands at 3.4 GW peak as of 9M FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our un-executed order book stood at 3.4 gigawatt peak in the first nine months of financial year 2025.

items.statement: Expect 500-600 MW execution in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect next quarter, I mean this quarter to be of January to March, we should be doing 500 to 600 megawatt of execution, that's what we expect.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 19.96%; 9M FY25 at 16.5%; medium-term target 15%
items.quote: We have already guided in since 3 -odd quarters, we have been guiding that our margins must be in the range of 15%. However, we are pleased that they have turned out to be 19.96% this quarter. And for nine months ended, they are nearer to our internal calculations, which we keep saying that we should be under 15%. So 16.50% is for nine months.

items.statement: Will try to maintain 15% margin level in medium term
items.quote: Certainly, in the medium term, we will try to maintain that 15% margin level.

items.statement: Do not undertake projects that are not profitable; competitive intensity acknowledged but pricing power maintained
items.quote: But I want to admit that there is competitive intensity, is good for productivity of companies. But as such for pricing power, we don't undertake projects which are not profitable to us.

items.statement: Government commitment strong; India added 24.5 GW solar in 2024; targeting 40-50 GW renewable annually
items.quote: India is going for 40 to 50 gigawatt of renewable energy per annum. So you can say about 30% -odd percent, 30%,35% comes from government sites, which is like NTPC, SCCI and other PSUs have also started now entering like IOC, BPCL tenders.

items.statement: Pipeline geared towards utility-scale private IPP players; government business strong but private dominates order book
items.quote: But historically, if you witness Waaree Renewables book, it is more finding favor with utility scale IPP players, which are on the private side. And even the current order book is geared towards that. Our pipeline is also geared towards more towards larger private players as of now.

items.statement: Not looking to raise funded debt unless capex is undertaken for monetization
items.quote: We are not looking to raise any funded debt, but we are always scouting for non-fund-based limits because we need to give bank guarantees, et c, to our customers. So that's what we keep shopping for. But shopping for debt is not on the cards as of now, unless we do some capex, which we may like to monetize in some form.

items.statement: Board approved object clause amendment to enter data center EPC business; will bid across all data center types with prerequisites
items.quote: Right now, the Board has approved amending the object clause because we do want to foray into data center business. There are synergies. Data centers, you build EPC solar-generating power projects, now we will WAAREE/RTL Execution with Pace & build data centers also, another EPC model

items.statement: Annual execution capacity 3-3.5 GW under current circumstances
items.quote: In the current circumstances, we should be able to deliver between 3 to 3.5 gigawatt of business annually.

items.statement: No significant client-side delays experienced; macro demand strong with government commitment and capital inflows
items.quote: On the client side, projection delays, I can't comment something specific because we are always on time, and we have been delivering whatever is our commitment with customers. But from a customer side, we have not experienced any significant delays as such.

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 587 MW; expect 2-3x growth from April as projects go live
items.quote: As regards to O&M, we are sitting on right now 587 megawatts of O&M. And we have certain projects going live in March, which will get converted into O&M for us about 2x to 3x size of our current base from April onwards.

items.statement: Waaree Group has 350 MW electrolyzer award; will bid for EPC portion of green hydrogen projects when large-scale opportunities arise
items.quote: So Waaree Group already has a presence in hydrogen. They have been awarded 350 megawatt of electrolyzer. But as and when huge case opportunity comes up, which is likely to come up, we will definitely be bidding for EPC part of the hydrogen play as well.

items.statement: Opportunistic on solar parks; two subsidiaries set up for land/connectivity but no land bank currently
items.quote: Tomorrow, if there is an opportunity and we find it profitable to set up a solar park, we will definitely do that. Solar park essentially requires land, connectivity where the government sanctions it. So once we have that -- in fact, we have two subsidiaries we have set up for same opportunity

name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Management expects full-year ROE to be within 16-18% range for FY2025 and medium term

items.statement: Motor combined ratio target range maintained at 65-67% over medium to long term
items.quote: The range that we have spoken about running overall motor in that range of 65% to 67%, I think that's broadly the range that we believe we should continue to see as an outcome in terms of the portfolio experience.

items.statement: Retail Health loss ratio target range maintained at 65-70%
items.quote: On the Retail Indemnity book specifically, you had spoken about the fact that the range that we are comfortable on running the book is a loss ratio of around that range between 65% to 70%.

items.statement: Corporate Health loss ratio increased to 97.2% in Q3 FY2025 from 93.1% in Q3 FY2024
items.quote: So for Corporate Health, Q3 FY2024, that number was 93.1%, that number for Q3 FY2025 is at 97.2%.

items.statement: Retail Indemnity loss ratio improved to 65% in Q3 FY2025 from 66% in Q3 FY2024

items.quote: GDPI of the Commercial Lines was ₹ 14.63 billion in Q3 FY2025 as against ₹ 16.00 billion in Q3 FY2024, registering a de-growth of 8.6%.

items.statement: Motor GDPI grew 9.4% in Q3 FY2025 vs industry 7.6%; new and old business grew ~9.5% and 9.3% respectively
items.quote: GDPI of Motor was ₹ 31.09 billion in Q3 FY2025 as against ₹ 28.42 billion in Q3 FY2024, registering a growth of 9.4%.

items.statement: Retail Health grew 44.3% in Q3 FY2025 (19.1% on 1/n basis) vs industry 6.6%; gained market share to 3.2%
items.quote: Within Health, our Retail Health segment registered a growth at 44.3%. With 1/n accounting norm, the growth was at 19.1% as against industry growth of 6.6% during the same period.

items.statement: Fire segment pricing expected to improve in coming months after 22% de-growth due to pricing pressure
items.quote: We expect the pricing to improve in the Fire segment in the coming months.

items.statement: Third-party motor tariff hike expected for next financial year after 3-4 years without increase
items.quote: But we do believe, yes, it's been 3 to 4 years and there might be possibly a hike at least which we'll get for next financial year.

items.statement: Solvency ratio reduced ~30 bps to 2.36x at Dec 31, 2024 due to new inadmissibility norms; still above 1.5x regulatory minimum
items.quote: Due to this, there is a reduction of ~30 basis points in our solvency ratio as at December 31, 2024. Consequently, our solvency ratio was 2.36x as at December 31, 2024, which is higher than the minimum regulatory requirement of 1.5x.

items.statement: Health Benefit business growth impacted by subdued credit disbursement from financial institutions
items.quote: Further, subdued credit disbursement by financial institutions has resulted in a slower growth of Health Benefit business.

items.statement: 1/n accounting norm effective Oct 1, 2024 impacts health and other lines reporting but not economic value
items.quote: The premiums under long-term health and other line of business were recognized in the year of underwriting itself. This change has an impact on the reporting of health and other line of business for the industry in Q3 FY2025. However, this does not impact the economic value.

items.statement: Project Orion achieved milestone with Elevate retail indemnity product rolled out on new core platform Artemis
items.quote: We initiated transformation journey of our Health business and have now achieved a critical milestone by rolling out our flagship retail indemnity product "Elevate" on our new core platform.

items.statement: Targeting 18-20% APE growth and VNB growth upwards of 15% for the full year
items.quote: we basically said that we will try and get to 18% -20% APE growth and try and deliver a VNB growth of upwards of 15%.

items.statement: 9M VNB margin at 25.1%, down from 26.5% YoY due to product mix shift to ULIPs and surrender regulation impact
items.quote: Value of new business for the 9M period was Rs. 2,586 crores, reflecting a 14% YoY growth. New business margin for the 9-month period was 25.1%, with the compression mainly attributable to changes in product mix in line with macro trends.

items.statement: Q3 VNB margin at 26%, up sequentially from normalized Q2 base of 25.3-25.4% due to better ULIP margins from higher persistency and protection attachment
items.quote: the margins are expanded by about 60 bps if we were to look at it from that perspective. items.statement: Surrender regulation impact 10 bps for 9M and 30 bps for Q3 on VNB margin; annualized impact expected at 20-30 bps
items.quote: on an annualized basis , we expect the impact to be closer to what we reported for nine months. It's 10 bps because it's only been three months since the regulation has come in. But our endeavor will be to try and keep it as close to 20 -30 bps on an annualized basis going forward

items.quote: Individual APE in 9M was composed of ULIPs: 37%, non -par savings: 35%, participating policies: 18%, term: 6%, and annuities: 5%. Retail protection continues to grow well, with APE for nine months clocking a growth of 28%.

items.statement: Q3 growth slowed due to base effects, but seasonality in JFM expected to pick up run rate to meet annual guidance
items.quote: towards the end of the year, we always see seasonality coming in, and that seasonality does help in picking up the run rate. We do expect that to happen in JFM also , to be able to pick up what we have been guiding as our annual numbers.

items.statement: Bancassurance concentration risk: HDFC Bank counter share stable at ~65%; bancassurance is 35% of new business premium on received premium basis
items.quote: our bancassurance, if I were to look at from an overall business perspective at a company level, new business premium, it is only 35% and HDFC Bank is about 1/4th.

items.statement: Added ~65 new agency branches in 9MFY25; branch expansion to continue
items.quote: We also added a lot of agents in this year. We've also expanded by adding nearly 65* branches this year, that expansion of branches will also continue.

items.statement: No pricing changes made post surrender regulations; peers have revised non-par IRRs down, annuity prices down, term prices up
items.quote: we have not made any changes to our pricing, whether it's on protection or non-par savings or annuities, but we definitely have seen some downward revision in pricing from some of our peers.

items.statement: HDFC Pension AUM Rs 1.06 lakh crore, market share 43.2%; HDFC International maintains S&P BBB and AM Best B++ ratings

items.statement: Credit Life growth tepid due to MFI segment slowdown from lower disbursements; other Credit Life lines stable
items.quote: Credit protect growth has been tepid due to slower disbursements amongst specific part ners and the MFI sector, in particular. However, we firmly hold our position as market leader in this

items.statement: Management expects to maintain healthy above 20% growth for a long period of time
items.quote: We don't see any broad reduction on our growth prospects. We think that we can continue maintaining a healthy above 20% growth for a long period of time.

items.statement: Management targets around 20% net margin and 23% operating margin for the year
items.quote: Our endeavour is to maintain around 20% of net margin and 23%. And some quarters, it can be more in some years as a total.

items.statement: 90% of Q3 FY25 deal bookings expected to convert to revenue in FY26
items.quote: Yes. I think we should assume that 90% will flow in FY '26.

items.statement: $500 million revenue target in next three to four years remains intact
items.quote: We do think that our next three, four years are the timeframes where we think should be able to do things, so that we can be closer to that goal.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 profit after tax grew 30% YoY to INR89 crores; nine months PAT grew 41% to INR207 crores

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by revenue growth above budgeted 18-20% range

items.statement: Won RBI order for Regulatory Application Management System worth INR32 crores
items.quote: We have won an order from RBI for implementation and maintenance of the Regulatory Application Management System with an aggregate contract value of INR32 crores.

items.statement: Added 15 new logos in Q3 FY25 and 36 in nine months FY25
items.quote: In total, we have added 15 new logos in Q3. Over the nine months period, we have added 36 new logos.

items.statement: India banking demand shifting from Tier 1 to Tier 2 NBFCs with smaller but more numerous deals

items.statement: AI central to sales; ~50 person AI team to expand organically over 2-3 years

items.statement: CCS plant environmental clearance expected in next 4 weeks, then civil works to commence

items.statement: PLI income expected around INR9-10 crores for FY25, approval likely in Q1 or Q2 FY26

items.statement: MCC volume growth of 22.5% YoY for 9M FY25; Q4 historically strongest quarter for volumes
items.quote: Q4 is this thing -- highest turnover would be there, highest turnover and margins. And next Q2 and then Q3 and then Q1, if I give the ranking.

items.statement: Middle East subsidiary (Sigachi Arabia) currently loss-making; expected to turn positive in next 2 quarters as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Going forward, maybe in another 2 quarters, we hope we'll see a positive margin, positive figures there.

items.statement: Receivable days increased to 107 days due to customer credit terms and foreign currency issues; target to reduce to 90 days
items.quote: Receivables, now we have given little leverage to the customers. Recently, we have given instructions to our sales team to bring it down to 90 days. Now it is there around 107 days is there, the DSO days.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 25-30% YoY expected to continue sustainably
items.quote: And the existing growth rate will continue, means every year around we hope 25% to 30% growth it will continue.

items.statement: Raw material prices not a constraint; any increases can be passed on to customers

items.statement: CEP approvals for API exports expected by Q2 FY26, with regulated market sales potentially starting Q2 or Q3 FY26
items.quote: So possibly from Q2, we should be looking at having our -- in the Q2, we should be looking at having our CEP approvals. And possibly from Q2, if not from Q3, we should be having sales into the regulated markets as well.

items.quote: In both segments, both volume and pricing outlook in Q4 remains subdued given market condition and competitive intensity from low-cost imports with rising domestic competition.

items.quote: Even if you take 20% of what we are going to launch, that would be about INR1,000-odd crores at least that will come. That will help in reducing the net debt to us.

items.statement: Used vehicle supply constrained due to fewer new vehicles sold during COVID and BSIV to BSVI transition
items.quote: This shortage is due to fewer new vehicles that were sold during the COVID year, which means a number of vehicles, which are available for resale is also much lesser. Additionally, the industry shift from BSIV to BSVI emission norms further reduced the number of older vehicles in circulation.

items.statement: GNPA at 4.92% and Stage 3 at 2.72% for standalone ICF; credit cost at 2.6% for Q3 FY25
items.quote: This led to we continuing to report the GNPA number at about 4.92% and the Stage 3 saw a bit of an increase at about 2.72%. Our credit cost for Q3 FY '25 stood at 2.6%.

items.statement: Normalized credit cost expected at 2% to 2.5% over 4-year period; current year abnormal due to heat waves, elections, extended monsoon
items.quote: 2% to 2.5% will be the fair assessment. If it's a normal year we will be in the range of 2% to 2.5%.

items.statement: Allotted warrants to BCP Multiple Holdings for INR205 crores (80% of INR257 crores total subscription)
items.quote: During the quarter, the Board approved the allotment of warrants of the company on a preferential basis by way of a private placement to Brookfield Capital Partners, a promoter of the company. The total consideration received by ICF is INR205 crores, which is 80% of the total subscription amount of INR257 crores.

items.statement: Expanded branch network to 135 branches for Niwas Housing Finance as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: As a business strategy, we've decided to go further deep in our core geographies and hence have expanded our presence to 135 branches as on December 31.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew 64% YoY in Q3 FY25; AUM grew 32% to INR10,625 crores; disbursements up 17% to INR1,572 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, the management team delivered a consolidated PAT growth of 64% vis-à-vis Q3 FY '24, and AUM growth of 32% to INR10,625 crores and disbursements of INR1,572 crores, which is up 17% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management is optimistic to achieve FY25 guidance of INR750 crores plus revenues with increased profitability
items.quote: We are optimistic to achieve our financial year 2024-'25 guidance of INR750 crores plus revenues with increased profitability.

items.statement: Management is comfortably above the INR750 crores guidance based on current order book and confident of surpassing it
items.quote: So, we are comfortably above the guidance of INR750 crores as per our current order book. So we are very confident of achieving and surpassing that this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance upgraded from 20-22% to 23-25% for full financial year basis
items.quote: So, what guidance we had given earlier was, of course, 20% to 22% on our previous concalls and everything. So, now we are more confident of graduating more towards 23% to 25% of EBITDA margin on EBITDA level.

items.statement: Management expects margins to be sustainable with multiple unexhausted levers for improvement
items.quote: See, we already told you that there are multiple levers which are still unexhausted. So we are trying our best to keep on improving on the things.

items.statement: Five projects prioritized for next 2-5 years: two backward integration, three forward integration including cocoa butter alternative, industrial chocolates, palm mid-fraction, solvent extraction in Chhattisgarh, and Burkina Faso facility
items.quote: Today, we are evaluating multiple projects. Out of this, we are considering and prioritizing 4 to 5 projects for a timeline of next 2 to 3 years to 5 years perspective and to give you a broad idea, two of them will fall in backward integration and three in forward integration.

items.statement: Projects selected based on payback period of less than 3 years, to be executed over 3-5 years funded through internal accruals
items.quote: So, we have always considered a payback period, which gives us less than 3 years. So going forward, the projects what we have recently finalized or prioritized, so we have considered the projects, which will give us a payback period of less than 3 years.

items.statement: Management sees no demand fall for cocoa products despite lower European grindings, citing addiction to cocoa and CBE pricing stability
items.quote: The world is addicted to cocoa. So, this grindings and this all depends on various other factors, very human on us, especially in Europe, Latin America, America and Russia. They're addicted to cocoa since childhood. So , we don't anticipate any fall, the people will stop eat ing cocoa chocolates or cocoa products

items.statement: Value-added product mix (stearin and CBE) at 55% of production, CBE portion currently 15-20% targeting 30% for FY25
items.quote: Within that, we can say that a portion of CBE can be increased to maybe -- what we have guided earlier, it was around 30% that we will be doing the CBE portion for this current financial year. We are in line with what we are guided.

items.statement: New fractionation plant utilization at 50-60% currently, expected to reach 60-65% by end FY25 and 75-80% in FY26
items.quote: So, the utilization from our existing plant of 15,000 tons is 100%. And the new plant is giving us 50% capacity utilization as of now. So we expect it should be around 60% to 65% by the end of financial year 2025.

items.statement: Each project typically takes 12-15 months to commercialize after Board approval and execution start
items.quote: The projects what we have set up last year also, it usually takes 12 to 15 months, one project post what we have got the approval from our Board and we have started the execution.

items.statement: No competition anticipated in the business space as per management knowledge
items.quote: No, we don't -- as of now, we don't see any competition from our knowledge.

items.statement: Expansion funding to be decided after Board approval of detailed financial plans, healthy internal cash flows expected
items.quote: We mentioned that we will submit a detailed financial plan. Of course, the Company is going to have healthy cash flows. So we might see at that time the need of the capital, whether any debt dilution is required or not.

items.statement: Volume growth of 5-10% quarter-on-quarter, Q3 saw ~5% Q-o-Q volume growth
items.quote: Yes, we mentioned that in the call earlier also that there is a good volume growth also of around 5% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Inventory book value at INR580 crores including raw material and finished goods as of current date
items.quote: Inventory currently as on date total value is around INR580 crores, including raw material, what we have procured and as well as the finished goods.

items.statement: Secured book to be 40%+ of total loan book by year-end with ~50% YoY growth; individual loans to grow ~12% for full year; overall loan book growth 8-9%; credit cost guidance maintained at 2.3-2.5%; NIM for full year 8.6-8.8%; deposit growth
items.quote: As guidance, as my concluding remarks, I would like to state that our Secured book by the year end would be 40% plus , the Y -o-Y growth on the Secured book would be around 50%, the individual business growth should be around 12% for the entire year. Overall growth could be hovering between 8% and 9% on the overall book . Credit cost, we continue with our guidance of 2.3% -2.5%. Deposit growth wil

items.statement: Affordable Housing and micro mortgages book expected to reach Rs. 7,000 crores by March 31, 2025
items.quote: This book has reached Rs. 6,393 crores as of December '24, exhibiting a strong 11% Q-o-Q and 45% Y-o-Y growth expecting to close at Rs. 7,000 crores as of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Reduced interest rates on group loans by ~115 bps and individual loans by ~75 bps effective Jan 1, 2025; expects stable cost of funds and margin improvements from rate cuts plus growth in high-yield secured products to offset yield impact
items.quote: Bank took a call to reduce interest rates in group loans and individual loans by approximately 115 bps and 75 bps respectively, with effect from 1st January 2025. This will not have a major impact on profitability for a couple of factors, namely stable cost of funds with expected margin improvements due to rate cuts, strong growth expected in high yielding products like micro mortgages, vehicle lo

items.statement: NIM for Q3 was 8.6%; portfolio yield compressed to 18.2% from 18.9% due to growing secured book share; cost of funds rose 6 bps to 7.57%; management expects NIM to remain steady at current levels going forward
items.quote: On financials and margins, the NIM for the quarter is 8.6%. The compression and yields on the overall portfolio is down to 18.2% in Q3 versus 18.9% in Q2 due to growing contribution from Secured assets. The cost of funds moved up marginally by 6 basis points to 7.57% in Q3 versus 7.51% in Q2 largely attributed to the retirement of IBPC book.

items.statement: NIM expected to fall below 9% as secured mix increases, but high-yield products like Vehicle Finance, Gold Loans and Micro Mortgages will compensate for decline in unsecured portfolio yield
items.quote: Yes, the NIMs will fall below 9%, but what we have done is that our Secured assets book, we also have products like the Vehicle Finance, Gold Loans. All these are high yielding products. So, this should help us in compensating the decline in the unsecured portfolio. And we have micro mortgages, we have Vehicle Finance which are very high linked product. So, we should be able to maintain within aro

items.statement: Seeing improved disbursements in first three weeks of January vs any month since July 2024; demand bounce-back observed in majority of states after funding gap; some pockets in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha still stressed
items.quote: We have seen that after a gap of funding in the market, there is a bounce back which happens and we see this bounce back happening for the last four weeks. So, our January disbursement numbers that we have seen so far are better than what we have seen during this year so far.

items.statement: Secured book now 39% of total loans (up from 30% YoY); 46% of Q3 disbursements from secured products; Affordable Housing 21%, MSME 5%, FIG 7%, Vehicle Finance 1%, Gold Loans and Secured Agri growing rapidly; target 60-40 unsecured-secured m
items.quote: Our strategy to diversify the portfolio towards a more Secured Book has seen accelerated results, now contributing 39% to the total loan book by end of Q3, led by Affordable Housing, MSME and FIG. Our overall Secured book grew by 13% Q-o-Q, 33% YTD and 52% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Secured portfolio expected to reach 40-42% by FY25 end; medium-term target of 60% unsecured / 40% secured to be achieved earlier than FY26; newer lines (Gold, Vehicle, Secured Agri, Micro Mortgages) contributing well
items.quote: Currently, our Secured book stands at around 39% and this will see year-on-year growth. Our Secured portfolio in housing , MSME and the newer business lines like th e Gold , Vehicle Finance, Secured Agri, Micro Mortgages has started contributing well. We were supposed to hit the 60 -40 mark in FY26, but with the phase at which we are going with the Secured asset portfolio, we should be hitting tha

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 2.3-2.5% for FY25; 9M credit cost at 1.55% (Rs. 483 cr); Q4 credit cost guided at 0.8-0.9%; PCR to be maintained at 70-75%; ARC sale of Rs. 270 cr in Q3 with Rs. 26 cr loss; accelerated provision of Rs. 30
items.quote: We maintain our credit cost guidance at 2.3%-2.5% for the year. Bad debt recovery continued to be strong, collecting over Rs. 29 crores in the quarter.

items.statement: PAR numbers expected to stabilize and start declining in 2-3 months; incremental stress formation has peaked; bucket X collections at 99.2% in Q3; SMA resolution rates improved (SMA-0 ~30%, SMA-1 25-35%, SMA-2 21-25%); collection headcount
items.quote: We expect that this PAR numbers will stabilize here on and start to show a declining trend in the next maybe two or three months.

items.statement: Following 4-lender guardrail currently; implemented 3-lender guardrail for new-to-bank customers from Jan 1; 3-lender guardrail for all customers effective Apr 1; ~14% borrowers currently outside guardrails; confident customers will choose
items.quote: So, we are following 4 lender guardrails. The 3 lender guardrails would come into effect on 1st of April. However, the other guardrails of 2,00,000 indebtedness and funding to SMA customers, these were already following. What we have additionally done is for the new-to-Bank customers, we have implemented the 3 lender guardrails.

items.statement: Operating expenses ~Rs. 700 cr in Q3; cost-to-assets improved to 6.2% from 6.4%; cost-income ratio up due to investments in secured business (manpower, branches), universal banking license consultants (~Rs. 6 cr), branding (~Rs. 10 cr); abs
items.quote: Yes, it will be steady for some time to come. It may slowly come down also this quarter because there could be, we have to wait and see, but it will be more or less steady. That is what we see.

items.statement: Board approved application for voluntary transition to universal banking; will submit application to RBI shortly
items.quote: I am also delighted to announce that the Board has accorded approval to move the application for voluntary transition to universal banking in its meeting held today . We will be submitting the application to RBI shortly.

items.statement: Deposits grew 16% YoY to Rs. 34,494 cr; CASA up 15% YoY to Rs. 8,662 cr (25% of deposits); retail deposits 73% of total, up 24% YoY; digital current account launched in Q3; Ujjivan Pay UPI app testing, launch in Q4
items.quote: Bank's total deposits reached Rs. 34,494 crores, marking a 16% Y-o-Y growth. Notably, CASA deposit saw 15% Y-o-Y increase reaching Rs. 8,662 crores which is 25% of overall book. Retail deposits stood at Rs. 25,274 crores accounting for 73% of total deposits and demonstrating a 24% growth over December 23.

items.statement: Microfinance group loan disbursements Rs. 2,029 cr in Q3 (down 16% QoQ); repeat customer contribution rose to 73% from 61%; individual loans 15% of book, grew 21% YoY; digital self-service journey for IL repeat customers implemented
items.quote: Micro Group loans witnessed disbursement of Rs. 2,029 crores in Q3 marking a 16% Q-o-Q decline. As of December, ‘24, these loans constitute 45% of the total loan portfolio. Contribution Ujjivan Small Finance Ban January 23, 2025 of repeat customers to overall disbursement has risen from 61% -73% Q-on

items.statement: Blinkit absolute losses expected to increase in next one or two quarters due to accelerated store expansion
items.quote: directionally as we have mentioned in the letter, we do expect the investments in Blinkit to go up. And as a result, the losses on an absolute basis are expected go up in the next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Blinkit store expansion accelerated beyond earlier guidance of 1,000 stores by March-25; now targeting 2,000 stores
items.quote: we were able to add a lot more new stores than what we envisaged maybe a year ago when we gave the guidance of getting to 1,000 stores by March-25.

items.statement: Blinkit added almost 300 stores over last four to five months; more than half of expansion in top 8 cities
items.quote: we've added, I would say, almost 300 stores over the last four or five months.

items.statement: Customer delivery charges declined slightly due to competition; marketing costs increased but discounts remain near zero
items.quote: We have seen a slight decline there because of the market and the competition being where they are on the delivery fee. While the decline is not significant, but yes, it has partly contributed to the decline in take rate that you see.

items.statement: Food delivery growth slowed in Q3; management attributes to broad-based consumption slowdown, not competition
items.quote: I don't think any of this has had a material impact on Zomato restaurant aggregation food delivery business so far.

items.statement: Blinkit AOV increased to over INR 700 in Q3 driven by festival season and higher ASP categories like electronics; not a secular trend
items.quote: In OND, we see the festival impact on the AOVs, which with every passing year, is becoming a larger portion of the business whenever they come around, especially the Diwali season.

items.statement: Marketing costs expected to rise with increased competition; no loyalty programs or subsidies planned for retention
items.quote: We will see the impact of increased competition on the cost of presenting ourselves to the customer, which is primarily our digital marketing cost today. And because there will be more competition over there, we expect this number will go up.

items.statement: Food delivery margins expected to reach 5% in next few quarters driven by delivery cost optimization, consumer fee increases, and AOV growth
items.quote: we continue to drive confidence from the progress we are seeing across various parts of the business, including delivery costs, the consumer fee increasing, AOV going up, and so on.

items.statement: GOV market share in quick commerce unchanged meaningfully despite competition; order market share not tracked
items.quote: So far, we don't believe our GOV market share has changed meaningfully despite the competition, and that's an important metric for us.

items.statement: FY26 personal loan disbursement expected to be better than FY25 unless macro worsens
items.quote: we do expect that FY26 will be better than FY25. And especially given that we are going to have additional partners, going into FY26, we do expect an increase in this business and a rebound from the lows that we saw earlier this year.

items.statement: Merchant loan disbursement expected to grow steadily in FY26
items.quote: On the merchant loan side, we expect continuously steady growth. Currently we are already higher than where we were in January and we expect continuous steady growth

items.statement: Merchant loan penetration opportunity to reach north of 10% in 2-3 years
items.quote: over the next two, three years, we have an opportunity of taking this to north of 10%. And I think the long term opportunity is probably even higher than that.

items.statement: Capex not expected to return to FY24 levels; refurbishment supply for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we don't expect the capex to go back to FY24 levels, and, we think that the refurbishment, sort of savings on capex due to refurbishment, should generally be the case over the next two, three quarters

items.statement: DLG cost on blended basis significantly lower than 5% and stable QoQ
items.quote: On a blended basis, our DLG cost is significantly lower than the 5%, and it has broadly remained the same as last quarter.

items.statement: ECL range improved to 4.5%-5.0% from 4.75%-5.25% due to collection efficiencies
items.quote: the reason for improvement is generally collection efficiencies, obviously with a lag, it is also indicative that your underwriting is getting tighter.

items.statement: ~80% of merchant loans disbursed via DLG model in Q3 FY25
items.quote: That number is in the ballpark, Sachin. And, give or take a few percent, I think that's probably right.

items.statement: 5-6 lakh merchants have loans outstanding (4-5% of device base)
items.quote: It is broadly, five to six lakh merchants who have a loan outstanding. So, it is roughly 4-5% of our device base.

items.statement: Personal loan growth dependent on partner caution; measuring success by number of active partners
items.quote: it is very market dependent, if I had to be honest, because we absolutely respect the fact that our partners are being very cautious, through the cycle.

items.statement: International expansion focused on merchant acquiring in Middle East and Southeast Asia; up to ₹20 cr investment per market
items.quote: we are saying up to ₹20 crores of investment in each of these markets, which is also a bit of a placeholder number, we don't really think that we need large amounts of money in these countries.

items.statement: Rationalizing old One97 telecom subsidiaries in Africa/Middle East over next 3-6 months
items.quote: We are in the process of rationalizing these number of subsidiaries because some of these were set up many, many, many years ago, and we may have little or no business in some of these countries.

items.statement: RuPay on UPI provides MDR revenue unlike bank-linked UPI; small but fast-growing share
items.quote: we do make MDR, unlike bank linked UPI, but it is still a very small percentage growing fast, but it's still a very small percentage of the merchant transactions right now.

items.statement: Merchant acquiring drives consumer acquisition via QR presence; flywheel effect observed
items.quote: our acquiring will add it to the consumer acquisition is what our belief is and that is why we will aggressively expand on our merchant acquiring, because that gives us an edge in consumer also.

items.statement: Subscription waivers given as refunds for high-volume merchants, not activity-based
items.quote: We don't give waivers basis an activity. We give waivers basis, if you're doing a large amount of volume with us then we give that, which is what Vijay is referring to as a refund.

items.statement: Home loan/mortgage products not pursued due to low margins and high CAC
items.quote: No, they're very low margin. They increase the line expenditure on us and we have not been able to find a commercially logical reason.

items.statement: Capex expected to return to FY24 levels
items.quote: we don't expect the capex to go back to FY24 levels

items.statement: Depreciation reduction to accelerate next year as high FY24 capex rolls off
items.quote: as the high capex of FY24 relative to FY25, as that starts to, sort of, roll off, because these are two years depreciation for soundbox, then we should see a reduction in capex, sorry, reduction in depreciation.

items.statement: Contribution margin without UPI incentives at 50-55%, with UPI incentives at 55-60%
items.quote: we've talked about the contribution margin without UPI incentives is at 50 to 55%. So 50 to 55% and including UPI incentive for this to be 55 to 60%.

items.statement: Contribution margin expected to uptick as DLG costs plateau relative to disbursals
items.quote: as that number sort of plateaus a bit, relative to our overall disbursal, we should see an uptick in contribution margin, just based on that factor alone.

items.statement: Gross take rate on DLG MCA book over loan lifetime includes sourcing fee 3-4%, collection 1-2%, plus FLDG amount
items.quote: we used to talk about 3 to 4% on sourcing and 1 to 2% on collections, right. So, to that you can add the FLDG amount.

items.statement: Trailing gross take rate on DLG MCA book expected to reach 8-9%
items.quote: So, essentially we should reach 8-9% on a trailing basis, that is how the maths would eventually work.

items.statement: Non-lending revenue consistently 10-20% of financial services revenue over last 8-9 quarters
items.quote: broadly it has been 10 to 20% of our financial services revenue almost consistently over the last 8 or 9 quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA before ESOP profitability expected in next 1-2 quarters; PAT profitability to follow as gap narrows to zero in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we're going to get to PAT profitability, once EBITDA before ESOP is, is profitable either in, you know, maybe in the next 1 or 2 quarters, sequentially.

items.statement: Target double-digit EBITDA margin relatively soon, then substantial PAT
items.quote: the goal is to have, double digit EBITDA margin relatively soon and then have that translate into a substantial amount of PAT.

items.statement: Payment volumes in India growing 20-25% year-on-year relatively safely
items.quote: payment volumes in India are growing very meaningfully. So, maybe 20 - 25% year on year, relatively safely.

items.statement: Only 6 lakh merchants have taken a financial services product (<1% of base), generating ₹450+ crores revenue
items.quote: only about six lakh customers or merchants have taken a financial services product from us, last quarter and we're not even getting into product per customer, right.

items.statement: DLG book performing noticeably better than non-DLG book AUM; no concern on unit economics or credit losses
items.quote: our DLG book that we have done in the last five months has done, I would say, noticeably better than the non DLG book AUM that exists.

items.statement: Preference for distribution plus collection model over distribution only due to higher margins
items.quote: Distribution plus collection is the preference because it gets us more margin. Distribution only gets us larger money per ticket.

items.statement: Wallet business restart dependent on Paytm Bank final outcome; timeline uncertain
items.quote: We are waiting for Paytm Bank's final outcome and on the basis of that we'll take the next step.

items.statement: Paytm Money focus on mutual fund distribution (SIPs, customers); insurance embedded with health and auto as bottom-line contributors
items.quote: Paytm Money is something that where there is an attention on mutual fund distribution, because I think that mutual fund distribution is a great amount of, number of customers that we are able to sign up.

items.statement: UPI incentive eligible GMV growing 15-20%; Q4 incentive amount uncertain but in that range
items.quote: we do have about 15 to 20% growth in eligible GMV. And so, if you look at our last year number and going forward, and had to sort of take a ballpark guess at this number, this year's number, then it should be in that range.

items.statement: Asset growth 20% and liability growth 20% guidance for FY25 will be met; similar guidance will be given for FY26
items.quote: Our guidance on asset 20% - we will meet, our guidance on deposit growth of 20% - we will meet. If you give us the benefit of adding back accelerated provision, then we are meeting the ROAs, ROEs, etc. But we will come back with guidance for next year when we do March 25.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 maintained at 1.6%-1.7%
items.quote: First is we did say that our credit cost this year will be 1.6 % to 1.7%. And given where we are in Q3, we will end up with a 1.6%-1.7% cost.

items.statement: Secured book growth expected at 35% for full year FY25
items.quote: Our secured group is growing very strongly, and so we should be in the 35% range when the full year finishes on secured growth.

items.statement: Unsecured book to be stabilized or grown in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We would like to grow our unsecured book in Q4, at the minimum keep it stable.

items.statement: Accelerated provisioning to unwind over next 3-4 quarters; carry of Rs. 275-300 crores into next year
items.quote: So, certainly, because right now the total corpus of accelerated provision Rs. 208 crores. Let's say we take another 60, 70, 80 crores in quarter four. So, we will be closer to like Rs. 275 crores to Rs. 300 crores of accelerated provision we are carrying into next year.

items.statement: OPEX growth higher than 8-10% guidance due to collection staff and attrition; expected to normalize as unsecured book stabilizes
items.quote: So, the OPEX growth, I think it's in line with the AUM growth. So, what has happened is, if you see, Ajay covered it also in the slide earlier. So, the OPEX is growing in line with the AUM. So, we had given earlier guidance of 8% to 10% basis the scenario not considering any additional collection costs and additional marketing spend which would have been required during the year.

items.statement: CGTMSE and CGFMU guarantee programs cover 13.3% of unsecured portfolio; target 25-30% by March 2025
items.quote: We have initiated CGTMSE and CGFMU which covers about 13.3% of our Unsecured portfolio. And by March' 25, we hope to reach about 25 % to 30% of our Unsecured portfolio under both the guarantee programs.

items.statement: Secured book NIM holding at 8%; overall NIM decline driven by unsecured book de-growth; 50 bps NIM drop expected over 3 years as secured mix moves to 80%
items.quote: Three years, our model was that our NIMs would drop 50 basis points as we turn 80% secured. I want to tell you the point to point. So, we assumed 60% in March '24 we will get to 80. So, 20% change in secured, 50 basis point drop in NIM.

items.statement: CASA cost reduced from 4.8% to 4.44% in Q3 after pricing cut on Oct 3; CASA ratio at 18.43%
items.quote: Having done that, I have shared with you what was our cost of CASA as of September end. It was 4.8%. It has now fallen to 4.44% in a quarter alone, purely because we have taken away the upper end of CASA.

items.statement: Secured products growing strongly: affordable housing 25%, micro-LAP 14.3%, MSME 17.4%, two-wheeler 73.9%, gold loans 104.9% YoY for 9M FY25
items.quote: affordable housing for nine months with an average ticket size of 11.9 lakhs has grown at 25%. Our micro-LAP, which has the average ticket size of 6.4 lakhs has grown by 14.3%. Our MSME loans has grown 17.4%. Our Two-Wheeler by 73.9%. Our gold loans at 104.9

items.statement: MFI collection rate steady at 98.5-98.6% (B0); new book performing well; worst behind us
items.quote: I must tell you that reaching 99% by the 20th, 22nd of the month is still very hard. We kind of stay at 98.5, 98.6. That's a collection percentage of B0 I am talking of. I am not adding anything else except what is demand in B0 and what is collected in B0.

items.statement: Secured book at 68% (up from 60% at March 2024); target 80% secured / 20% unsecured
items.quote: We have seen a solid growth in secured loans, 36% year-on-year, and now our secured book stands at 68% from 60% in the March ending, 2024 financial year ending.

items.statement: Gross NPA additions Rs. 437 crores in Q3; recoveries and write-offs Rs. 434 crores (Rs. 109 crores technical write-off); expect lower additions in Q4
items.quote: We are hoping and we are working towards the addition, which is 437. We should bring down that a bit more in Q4. And we should end up with a closing GNPA number, which is flattish to lower than where it is right now.

items.statement: Slight GNPA uptick in micro-LAP and affordable housing in Odisha and West Bengal; actions taken; no spillover from MFI
items.quote: So, it's just, for us, very specifically two states are showing a bit of extra challenge. And I don't know whether this is industry-wide or Jana specific. One is in the state of Odisha. Secondly, we have seen slight pickup in West Bengal.

items.statement: Additional Rs. 730 crores refinancing from NHB and SIDBI (10-year and 5-year) taken for ALM management
items.quote: We have taken additional Rs. 730 crores of NHB and SIDBI money. This is 10-year and 5-year money at very good pricing. But we do it because it does help ALM getting long-term rates.

items.statement: Universal bank license application targeted for May 2025; requires gross NPA <3% and net NPA <1% for two consecutive years
items.quote: As we all know, to apply for a universal bank, you have to meet conditions of gross NPA below three, net NPA below one for two consecutive years. We met it last year, and to make sure that we meet it this year, we keep providing the accelerated provision.

items.statement: Steady-state ROA 1.8-2% and ROE 16-17% in 3 years with 80% secured book, 30% CASA, 30 bps NIM compression
items.quote: our ROA would be 1.8% to 2% range, and ROE between 16% to 17%. That is a steady-state model that we had imagined would happen.

items.statement: PAT around Rs 360 crore for 9M FY25, Q4 expected better than Q3, accelerated provision Rs 300 crore carried forward
items.quote: when you finish this year, we have right now PAT around Rs. 360 odd crores. We have one more quarter to go. You can take any reasonable addition to that, which is bet ter than Q3

items.statement: Accelerated provision unwind: Q1 FY25 portion (~Rs 60 cr) in Q1 FY26, Q3 FY25 portion (~Rs 93 cr) around Q2-Q3 FY26
items.quote: the Q3 provisioning will probably unwind around Q2, Q3 next year. What we provisioned about, I think around Rs. 60 crores in Q1, that is probably what will be available in Q1 next year.

items.statement: Applied for Universal Bank license in May, targeting net NPA <1%, gross NPA <3%
