items.statement: Smart meter bidding opportunity of 10 crore meters remaining in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, parts of Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: the smart metering bidding left out is about 10 crores meters and those are mainly from the state of Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, part of Andhra Pradesh and few other states.

items.statement: AEML debt reduced by Rs 400 crores in Q3; outstanding bonds $880M + $300M SLB = $1,120M
items.quote: Part of the proceeds have been used to repay the debt of the company about Rs 400 odd crores during last quarter. Currently at AEML, there is a reduction of the debt. We currently have around $ 880 million of bond outstanding and $ 300 million of SLB bond outstanding. So, $1,120 million of bond, which is outstanding at AEML level.

items.statement: Management expects Q4 revenue to surpass Q3's INR 65 crores and aims to double revenue over the next few years.
items.quote: We will definitely aim to surpass, like you said, the base numbers of around INR 65 crores. And while we look at Q4 more optimistically, while we have demonstrated a consistent base number, we will definitely look to surpass that in Q4.

items.statement: Management targets scaling rental units to 50,000 in the midterm and 1 lakh long-term.
items.quote: We would definitely look to scale it up to 50,000 units under management in the midterm, like we said. And in fact, our aspirations are quite larger, we would like to, in the longer terms, scale it up to 1 lakh rental units under management.

items.statement: SM-REIT AUM target of INR 2,000 crores over the next 2-3 years post-license approval.
items.quote: In the next 2 to 3 years, we would be looking to scale up to an AUM of around INR 2,000 odd crores to start with, and then we'll look to see based on how the acceptance of the product is in the market.

items.statement: Rights issue third tranche process to start in Q4 FY25 (JFM 2025).
items.quote: We are looking to start the process in this Q4 quarter and all for the rights money in next few months. But the process will be started in this quarter as we had committed earlier.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 24.7% in Q3 FY25 from 21.5% in previous quarter.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter, 24.7% compared to 21.5% in the previous quarter, improvement of 320 bps.

items.statement: Distribution segment achieved 18% net margin with 55% YoY growth for nine months ended Dec 2024.
items.quote: The restructured Distribution business, SaaS, services and noncore businesses demonstrated a 55% year-on-year growth for the period. This came at a significant net margin of 18%.

items.statement: IT hiring resumption and GCC growth in Bangalore and NCR driving rental demand.
items.quote: We are seeing a trend reversal with top IT firms resuming hiring, as indicated by their recent quarterly reports. This is a great positive for our core living business as it creates tremendous opportunity for us to expand supply and drive higher occupancy.

items.statement: NestAway Lite launched as transaction-only model to capture supply seeking only rental transactions without property management.
items.quote: NestAway Lite is a byproduct of our data analytics and why is that premium, where we saw that there was a lot of supply that was coming in as a request, which wanted to only do the rental transaction bit.

items.statement: No new capex guidance; depreciation of INR 59 crores for 9M FY25 largely from right-of-use assets under long-term leases (INR 42 crores).
items.quote: Out of, say, the total depreciation of INR 59 crores that you see for the nine months, around INR 42 crores comes on account of that. So that is not an asset, not a depreciation for the asset that we carry.

items.statement: Kota student living occupancy dropped to 57-60% from 85% due to regulatory changes and student welfare issues; 30% of team redeployed to Indore.
items.quote: The occupancy witnessed in this season with the present challenges is in the range of 57% to 60% in the city. So that is where the concern lies in, whereas just to underline or just to point out, in a good market, this city was operati ng at 85% kind of an occupancy

items.statement: SM-REIT license approval pending with SEBI; application submitted, awaiting response, no further queries expected.
items.quote: As of now, as we speak, we have submitted our information that was required by SEBI. We are awaiting their response. If no further queries, then it should be the last leg.

items.statement: ESOP-adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -2.4% (approx INR 1.8 crores on INR 70 crores revenue); management believes net profitability achievable at any point.
items.quote: We had now for last few quarters, we have started kind of declaring our ESOP adjusted EBITDA. And that has constantly improved to a point where it is now minus 2.4%, which means INR 70 crores revenue, it is INR 1.8 crores, approximately INR1.7 crores, not even INR1.8 crores.

items.statement: AI strategy focused on three prongs: increasing wallet share, improving team efficiency via automation, and enabling new models like C2C resale on NestAway.
items.quote: We feel AI and all the new-age AI practices are more of an enablers. And we have a clear 3-pronged strategy there is to, first, how do we use AI tool increase our top line by increasing wallet share of customers and consumers. Number two, how do we increase our bottom line by increasing the efficiency of our team structures, organizational structures, and automation of tasks.

items.statement: Raised subordinated debt of Rs 14 billion, strengthening solvency to 211.8% at December 31, 2024
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised subordinated debt of ` 14 billion, thereby strengthening our solvency to 211.8% at December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Focus is on growing absolute VNB; margin is an outcome of product mix
items.quote: Our focus has always been on growing absolute VNB and margins are primarily an outcome of the product mix.

items.statement: Medium-term VNB growth target is mid-teens; currently at 8.5% for 9M-FY2025
items.quote: The view that we want to take from a medium -term perspective is to work towards mid -teens.

items.statement: Investing in people, technology, and process improvements to deliver operating leverage in coming years
items.quote: We have been investing in our capabilities, i.e., people, technology and process improvements which will help us deliver an operating leverage into the coming years.

items.statement: VNB margin for 9M-FY2025 stood at 22.8%; movement primarily due to product mix shift
items.quote: The margin for 9M-FY2025 stood at 22.8%. The movement in margins is primarily on account of the shift in the underlying product mix.

items.statement: ULIP contribution increased to 50.8% of APE in 9M-FY2025 from 43.1% last year; non-linked savings excluding annuity declined to 17.5%
items.quote: Linked business grew by 49.8% year -on-year and its contribution to overall APE increased from 43.1% in 9M-FY2024 to 50.8% in 9M-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards ULIP products given the market buoyancy.

items.statement: Group Funds business grew 102.5% YoY, contribution increased to 6.0% of APE; considered lumpy but profitable
items.quote: Group Funds business grew by 102.5% year -on-year in 9M-FY2025. Contribution from Group Funds business increased from 3.7% last year to 6 .0% in 9M-FY2025. This business is typically lumpy in nature.

items.statement: Annuity APE grew 81.7% YoY in 9M-FY2025; regular pay annuity launched last year driving demand
items.quote: Annuity business grew by 50 .0% in Q3-FY2025 and 81% in 9M-FY2025 on a year-on-year basis. Its contribution increased from 6.2% in nine months last year to 8.9% of APE in nine months this year.

items.statement: Retail Protection APE grew 24.2% YoY in 9M-FY2025; Credit Life slowed due to MFI challenges, non-MFI doing well
items.quote: Retail Protection business grew by 40 .0% in Q3 -FY2025 and 24.2% in 9M-FY2025 on a year-on-year basis. In Credit Life business, we have witnessed some slowdown due to ongoing challenges in MFI industry. Non-MFI business continues to do well.

items.statement: Repriced non-par and annuity products effective October 1 in line with G-Sec yields; commission structures realigned with surrender value guidelines
items.quote: Yes, the pricing of non-par, annuity, all those products linked to G-Sec yields were all corrected effective 1st October, something that we could not do in Q2, it was corrected as we got into this quarter.

items.statement: No adverse surrender trends seen in zero surrender value annuity product launched three weeks ago; surrender expectations remain miniscule
items.quote: frankly we have not seen any adverse trends at this point, because again, our belief is that this product has been bought from the perspective that the customer wants to take an annuity.

items.statement: Agency advisor licensing grew 50%+ YoY; advisor activation 25-30% via digital enablement; IPru Edge app boosted value advisor productivity by 37%
items.quote: we have been able to see a growth on the new advisor licensing which is quite reasonable at 50% plus growth. And then as you know, apart from new advisor licensing, which anyways contributes little to the overall top line, it happens over a period of time. A lot of time has been spent in looking at building skill on the retail side of our advisors and very happy to state that more than 25% to 30%

items.statement: Approved investment up to Rs 100 million (not exceeding 10% share capital) in Bima Sugam India Federation
items.quote: Recently, the Company has approved the proposal to invest up to ` 100 million, not exceeding 10% of the share capital in Bima Sugam India Federation.

items.statement: Solvency strong at 211.8% at December 31, 2024 aided by sub debt raise; AUM at Rs 3.1 trillion
items.quote: Our assets under management stood at ` 3.1 trillion and our solvency continue d to be strong at 211.8% at December 31, 2024 aided by the ` 14 billion sub debt fund raise that we had done.

items.statement: Multiple levers in play for Q4; aim to continue alpha over market; no single big lever identified
items.quote: frankly, as we had mentioned to you last Q4, there are a series of multiple items that we have on the table and that of course is a natural consequence of the fact that we have got a very well diversified distribution network. So, there is not going to be one big lever that I can point.

items.statement: Order book at end of Q3 FY25 was INR2,681 crores
items.quote: The Q3 PAT was INR166 crores and the order book at the end of the Q3 was INR2,681 crores.

items.statement: Expect large tender-driven opportunities like BSNL expansion, 5G, Power, BharatNet to convert in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 contributing to FY26 business
items.quote: Some of the large tender-driven opportunities such as the BSNL expansion network, 5G, Power, BharatNet etc., are all live opportunities, which are maturing as we speak, and we expect them to convert in Q4 of FY'25 and Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Margins lower due to change in product mix, provisions for old inventory and higher R&D depreciation; expect improvement as international business picks up
items.quote: The margins or profitability are a bit lower than the previous quarter, and that's mainly on account of change in product mix. And also, there are certain provisions for old inventory and higher depreciation for certain R&D equipment that we've taken in this quarter.

items.statement: Initial 1 lakh site BSNL 4G order expected to complete this financial year with expansion and 5G upgrade opportunities following
items.quote: That's correct. I think this initial 1 lakh site order should get executed in this financial year. So what we expect to see is, again, an expansion of this 4G network because I think there is still some way to go for them to get coverage across the country wherever their plans are.

items.statement: Almost doubled floor space capacity for R&D and manufacturing in Bangalore; set up center of excellence for wireless communications
items.quote: We have significantly expanded our office and manufacturing facilities in Bangalore, in line with our business and headcount expansion and we have almost doubled our floor space capacity, both for our R&D as well as for manufacturing.

items.statement: India government business 3% of 9M revenue with 40% YoY decline; India business dominant driven by BSNL 4G shipments; international business 3%
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix, in the India government business has been 3% of our revenue, and there has been a year-over-year decline of 40%. And as you know, government business is tender-driven and lumpy.

items.statement: Tariff impact on US business unknown as nothing announced; regulatory compliance requires equipment certification before shipping
items.quote: Now as far as tariffs and all are concerned, it's still an open question. We really do not know. I mean nothing has been announced, so nothing has come up. So until that time it comes up, it's all pure speculation on this front.

items.statement: Headcount upwards of 2,350 people with more than 60% in R&D
items.quote: So as of today, we are upwards of 23 50 people, and more than 60% of them are in R&D, that is part of our engineering team.

items.statement: Expect significant order book refilling in FY26 if successful in BSNL 4G expansion, 5G, Kavach, BharatNet opportunities converting in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26
items.quote: So if we are successful in most of the se opportunities, it could lead to a significant bump or refilling of our order book

items.statement: Wireless POCs with domestic operators ongoing; expect success in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; international engagements in advanced technical discussions with band customization
items.quote: Yes. So as I mentioned that live POCs are going on for operators in India, and we think probably in this quarter or in Q1FY'26, we should be able to see some success in that in terms of additional orders and additional deployment.

items.statement: R&D investments will continue at absolute level despite revenue outlook; focus on optimizing overall spend
items.quote: While we would always look at optimizing and controlling the overall spend in general, but at an absolute level the investments in R&D will continue.

items.statement: Import content for active electronic components varies 40-65% by product; enclosures, cables, connectors, passive components localized; manufacturing and assembly fully localized in India
items.quote: The amount of it can vary between 40% to 65%, in terms of the active electronics that gets imported especially for the semiconductor chips. But a lot of the key ingredients in terms of enclosures, accessories, cables, connectors, mechanical items, Passive components, a lot of that has been localized in India.

items.statement: Sales teams in North America and LatAm grown over 50% YoY; added 6-7 people including system architects, senior sales, marketing, account executives
items.quote: Well, with respect to l ast financial year, we have grown our teams by more than 50% in those regions. In the US and LatAm, we've added at least 6-7 people, both in terms of system architects, senior sales, marketing people as well as account executives

items.statement: Targeting BEAD program, Rip and Replace, and network modernization in North America with dense circuit emulation solution seeing traction
items.quote: Besides BEAD and Rip and Replace, another significant opportunity that we are targeting in North America is network modernization. Most telecom networks in North America have been built over many, many years using old T DM technology which were optimized for voice

items.statement: Vodafone Idea 3-year contract for pan-India 4G/5G mobile backhaul using packet transport and optical DWDM equipment; supplies and deployment started
items.quote: For the wireline business, one of the highlights has been signing a 3-year contract with Vodafone Idea for supplying equipment for their pan-India 4G and 5G mobile backhaul network.

items.statement: Revenue from new CAPEX expected to start showing from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, the revenue should start showing up from Q2 of next year.

items.statement: Adding 30,000 tons ethoxylation capacity; commissioning phased in coming months and Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are adding about 30,000 tons of ethoxylation capacity. As I said, it will take us about 3 years or so for these capacities to get fully utilized.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 137 bps YoY; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 13.7% YoY due to growth investments
items.quote: Our gross margin improved by 137 bps YoY during the quarter, supported by a favorable product mix and operational efficiencies. However, higher expenses related to ongoing growth initiatives, capacity expansion, and certain businesses in their growth phases, such as our institutional cleaning vertical impacted the EBITDA margins, which stood at 12.6% compared to 13.7% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Expect similar EBITDA margin levels of 13% plus minus in first year of new capacities
items.quote: Currently, I think we would still be okay to, at least for the first year, to come up with similar kind of margin levels of 13% plus minus.

items.statement: Exports grew 21% YoY in Q3 and 28% YoY in nine months; domestic market challenging
items.quote: Our international business registered YoY growth of 21% during the quarter and 28% over the nine months, providing strong support to overall performance.

items.statement: YTD nine months volume growth 9%-10% across all segments; pricing contributed couple of percent
items.quote: I would say the volume would have grown about 9%-10% and a couple of percent increase would have come from pricing. And this has been across the three verticals.

items.statement: Textile focus shifting to finishing chemicals and pretreatment; backward integration into surfactants and silicon-based raw materials
items.quote: In the Textile business in the domestic market, we are focused very strongly on the product mix, especially the finishing chemicals. And this quarter and the next quarter, we will be paying additional attention to the pretreatment segment because of our backward integration into surfactants.

items.statement: Reliance EO capacity expansion delayed; no alternative EO source; clarity expected end of Q4 or early Q1
items.quote: We are waiting for newer EO capacity to come up in Reliance. Reliance is still not confirmed by when they will start giving. This may be a constraint till we have clarity from Reliance on the higher allocation of EO.

items.statement: If Reliance EO delayed 6 months, no other procurement option; must run underutilized plant
items.quote: We do not have any option because Reliance is the only supplier of EO and we cannot import or transport the EO.

items.statement: Bangladesh target Rs. 6-7 crore monthly sales intact but timeline extended; new leadership penetrating key accounts
items.quote: Our goal of Rs. 6 – Rs. 7 crore of monthly sales to Bangladesh is still there. I think it will take a little more time now given the current situation there.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning (Buzil Rossari) target Rs. 450-500 crore revenue in 2 years; EBITDA positive at that scale
items.quote: In 2 years, we want this business to be double of what it is today. Our two-year target, if you see, we should be closer to Rs. 450 – Rs. 500 crore kind of a revenue. And we expect that once it reaches that number, it will start contributing to the EBITDA.

items.statement: New office and two warehouses leased; one-time depreciation charge Rs. 1.5-1.6 crore in Q3; recurring Rs. 1.4 crore/quarter
items.quote: There is a onetime charge in depreciation of about Rs. 1.5 - Rs. 1.6 crore kind of a number which has come in this quarter. Going forward, the charge that will come in the depreciation will be about Rs. 1.4 crore kind of a number.

items.statement: Employee count up 190 YoY (120 in institutional cleaning); expense rate for Q3 expected to be quarterly run-rate going forward
items.quote: On an annualized basis, YoY, almost 190 people have been added. Now, most of these new additions have come up in our consumer or the Rossari institutional cleaning business.

items.statement: Export offices set up in Vietnam, Thailand, Turkey, UAE for HPPC and Textile growth
items.quote: We have already set up offices in Vietnam, in Thailand, and we are in the process of also setting up an office in Turkey. A lot of these initial costs and all will play into the P&L for a few quarters and then the leverage will start playing out. And also in Dubai, we have also set up in Dubai.

items.statement: Target debt-to-equity ratio of 8-9x going forward, down from current ~9x, as business mix shifts to higher-margin non-Railway assets
items.quote: And going forward, since we are looking forward to business outside Railways also, so we would like to be hovering around somewhere 8 to 9, this is the target right now.

items.statement: PAT expected to grow steeply quarter by quarter as higher-margin non-Railway business (3x-5x Railway margins) increases in mix, even if AUM growth moderates
items.quote: Rest assured, going ahead we are working very actively on ensuring that our bottom-line growth is bigger than what we have right now quarter by quarter.

items.statement: Non-Railway Railway-ecosystem margins are 3x to 5x the 35-40 bps Railway lease margin, i.e., ~105-200 bps
items.quote: Once we go out, the margins are quite higher. I am not quoting a number, but it hovers around somewhere between 3x to 5x of what I am getting in the Railways.

items.statement: Non-Railway business currently <1% of AUM; management aims to build sizeable non-Railway mix by FY28 to offset potential EBR slowdown
items.quote: Yes, right now yes, you are very right. It is just the beginning, for the first time in the history of the Company we are doing business outside Railway as a client.

items.statement: Aggressively tapping cheapest funds: 54EC bonds, zero-coupon bonds, domestic bonds, and monitoring ECB opportunities; most domestic bond issuance in last two months
items.quote: We are extremely aggressive in tapping the cheapest fund resources which are our raw materials. we are actively mobilizing more and more funds under 54EC bond market and exploring zero coupon bond market, and domestic bond market, apart from keeping an eye on any opportunity from various currencies in ECB market.

items.statement: Government EBR allocation (>Rs4.5 lakh cr) already in hand; any new budget allocation is 'icing on cake'; focus shifting to higher-margin Railway ecosystem projects (PPP, backward/forward linkages)
items.quote: If you have followed our conference call in the last quarter, we have made it very clear that our bags are full of what we needed from the government side, they are more than 4.5 lakh crores.

items.statement: NIM will improve as non-Railway mix rises; no specific number given but improvement expected every quarter
items.quote: Definitely, as our CMD has already told you, the mix of the business would definitely get changed and the non-Railway business will yield me a higher return, so definitely my NIM will improve.

items.statement: Rs10,000 cr non-Railway business equals Rs30,000-40,000 cr Railway EBR business in PAT impact; minimum target is to exceed last EBR of Rs33,000 cr equivalent
items.value: Rs10,000 cr non-Railway ≈ Rs30,000-40,000 cr Railway
items.quote: Suppose if I do Rs. 10,000 crores business outside Railway, it is akin to Rs. 30,000 crores to Rs. 40,000 crores of business that we do for the Railways.

items.statement: Tax-free status protected for next 4-5 years by >Rs6,000 cr unabsorbed depreciation cushion; no MAT liability foreseen
items.quote: As of now, I have a cushion of more than Rs. 6,000 crores in my balance sheet as unabsorbed depreciation. I think going forward for next four, five years, I do not foresee any tax liability on my balance sheet.

items.statement: Gati Shakti multimodal corridor (golden quadrilateral) and India-Middle East-Europe corridor offer decade-long pipeline; budget clarity awaited on funding split
items.quote: This dedicated freight corridor of eastern and western, they have covered only two lines. This country has got a golden quadrilateral, so four next lines of Gati Shakti are still on the pipeline and CAPEX should be huge.

items.statement: Refinancing existing Railway-allied projects funded at higher rates is a new opportunity; agreements will be announced via exchanges as finalized
items.quote: We never funded anything outside IR, but there are many alli ed projects which are already running, and they are being funded at a very high rate. So, now positioning ourselves as the main financing arm of the Railway ecosystem, we want to look at every business which is there on the platter

items.statement: Fluoro-intermediate site at Lote targeting 10% of peak revenues in Q4 FY25 and 40-60% in FY26
items.quote: And at our Fluoro-Intermediate site at Lote, thrilled to share that in quarter 4, as we have been really working very diligently towards it, is where we are seeking about 10% of the peak revenues. And in the course of the next financial year, that is FY '26, we target to have 40% to 60% of the peak revenues.

items.statement: Peak revenue from fluoro-intermediate asset base is INR 200 crores
items.quote: The second one is the peak revenues that we are achieving from that asset base is a peak revenue of INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Target to double sales from INR 2,800 crores in FY24 to FY28
items.quote: So, we are going to double our sales, correct, from INR 2,800 crores last year to FY '28.

items.statement: Total capex outlay INR 1,100 crores with INR 800 crores for Dahej, midpoint of expenditure in H1 FY26
items.value: INR 1,100 crores total, INR 800 crores Dahej
items.quote: So, the INR 1,100 crores, if you remember the conversations, INR 800 crores of that is allocated specifically to Dahej. And the midpoint of expenditure will happen in the first half of the next financial year.

items.statement: INR 220 crores capitalized at Lote fluoro project in Q3 FY25, balance INR 140 crores to be capitalized in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, we have capitalized INR 220 crores of the assets in Lote, as Rajan has alluded to. So that's the impact that is coming in depreciation sequentially.

items.statement: Specialty business EBITDA margin target 20-25%, Essentials business EBITDA 8-12% with asset turns 3x-5x
items.quote: And for Specialty is 1x to 2x asset turns; EBITDA 20% to 25%, which then enables us to get the ROCE what we are targeting.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 240 bps YoY in Q3 FY25 due to better product mix and operational excellence
items.quote: This has enabled in improving our gross margin by nearly 240 bps.

items.statement: Acetic acid prices moderated ~15% YoY from USD 450 to USD 380 range in Q3 FY25, expected to rise to USD 410 pre-Chinese New Year then moderate
items.quote: we say is basically now in this quarter, we are seeing -- quarter 3, we saw average prices sort of moderating to the normalized levels, closer to the USD 380 range. So, it was range bound to that extent. Moving into quarter 4, as a result of the Chinese New Year, which is expected by the end of January, we are seeing larger producers scaling down their operations. But most of it is done in a very

items.statement: Ethyl acetate revenue share to reduce from 60% in FY24 to 40% via new product launches and specialty growth
items.quote: With the strategy that we are envisaging, this number will come down to 40%.

items.statement: Freight costs grew ~100% YoY due to international issues, pulled back exports to Europe; seeing moderation signs in Q4
items.quote: Though we have still seen the challenges in our freight costs, which have grown year-on-year by nearly 100% due to international issues, but still, this is a resilient performance for us.

items.statement: No anticipated knee-jerk reaction from potential Trump tariffs as feedstock sourcing is primarily from Asia and acetic acid supply is long
items.quote: I think first is, where are we sourcing our feedstocks from, right? A lot of our sourcing strategy has been primarily coming in Asia. So that should, I would say, buffer any untoward element. Secondly, as I've called out in the past, also for the feedstocks, when you look at supply-demand dynamics, a lot of the key products tend to be long. So, for example, acetic acid. So I am not anticipating at

items.statement: Dahej project on track for regulatory approvals, timelines and budget; robust project tracking under CTO leadership
items.quote: We continue to remain on track to receive the pending regulatory approvals and the project remains in schedule on timelines and in budget.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA/stable/A1 positive by India Ratings and CRISIL; Together for Sustainability rating improved to 87% from 67%
items.quote: Also, I'm glad to share that in quarter 3, Laxmi Organic received a credit rating upgrade from India Rating and got rated by CRISIL. The company is now rated AA/stable/A1 positive. The recognition of our efforts on sustainability was validated with the rating on Together for sustainability at 87%, which was a big jump up.

items.statement: No investment in HF plant for backward integration; sufficient competitive capacity available externally
items.quote: Simple answer to that, no, Devang we will not be doing it. We are not a large consumer of HF, and we believe there is enough capacity out there to meet our demands competitively.

items.statement: Target to bring net debt below Rs. 4,000 crores by end of FY25 to support future investment
items.quote: The Company stays on course, with its objective to bring net debt below Rs. 4,000 crores to support our future investment.

items.statement: Vadraj acquisition bid amount Rs. 1,800 crores plus Rs. 900-1,200 crores capex over 18-24 months to operationalize
items.quote: we have a range of spend from Rs. 900 crores to Rs. 1,200 crores. So, which should be the money needed over a period of 18 to 24 months to make the assets fully operational.

items.statement: YTD capex Rs. 299 crores, Q4 FY25 expected Rs. 50-60 crores additional
items.quote: YTD CAPEX this year has been Rs. 299 crores, and I guess in Q4 we are looking at this Jajpur and a little bit of sustaining CAPEX which should be close to the tune of another Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Center has Rs. 5.97 lakh crore and States have Rs. 5.34 lakh crore pending capex as of November 2024
items.quote: As of November 2024, the Center has Rs. 5.97 lakh crore in pending CAPEX, while States have Rs. 5.34 lakh crore CAPEX spending to be executed.

items.statement: Project Bridge 2.0 delivering reduction upwards of Rs. 50 per tonne YTD, Q4 FY25 target Rs. 75 per tonne
items.quote: On cost efficiency program Project Bridge 2.0 is on track, delivering a reduction upwards of Rs. 50 per tonne YTD.

items.statement: Cement prices plummeted in Oct-Nov, improved mid-December; December exit realization 6% above quarter average
items.quote: December end realization was 6% of the quarter realization. So, we ended the quarter very strong.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per tonne reduced 6% QoQ to lowest in 13 quarters at Rs. 1.45 per million cal
items.quote: Power and fuel cost per tonne were reduced by 6% quarter-on-quarter. The Company has reached the lowest blended fuel cost in the last 13 quarters at Rs. 1.45 per million cal.

items.statement: Demand recovery observed in Q3 FY25 after challenging H1; optimistic on Q4 FY25 demand improvement
items.quote: I am pretty optimistic that Q4 overall demand should improve for industry, and certainly for our Company.

items.statement: Premium product percentage maintained at 39% despite 16% volume growth; trade share 71%
items.quote: And certainly we maintained our value strategy, our premium product percentage continue d to be at 39%.

items.statement: Vadraj NCLT approval carries business risk; deal could face hiccups but confident of overcoming
items.quote: But certainly, I think I cannot rule out any hiccup which may come on the way.

items.statement: Target 10% volume growth YoY for next 3-4 years: 21M tonnes FY26, 23M FY27, 25M FY28, 27M FY29
items.quote: I am looking at a 10% growth year-on-year. From next year we should have all the way to 21 million tonnes, 23 million tonnes, 25 million tonnes, 27 million tonnes.

items.statement: Routine maintenance capex ~Rs. 300 crores annually; Vadraj capex ~Rs. 1,200 crores over 2-2.5 years
items.quote: I had mentioned, Rs. 300-odd crores will be the kind of routine CAPEX for the Company.

items.statement: Management indicates Rs. 200 crores pretax profit achievable in Q4 FY25

items.statement: Nine redevelopment projects with Rs. 7,000 crores potential plus Rs. 2,500 crores unsold revenue from ongoing projects

items.value: 410 crores raised, 176 crores utilized, 234 crores balance

items.statement: Three new redevelopment projects added in Andheri East (1.29 lakh sq ft, Rs. 527 crores), Malad West (2.12 lakh sq ft, Rs. 750 crores), Borivali West (2.44 lakh sq ft, Rs. 865 crores) totaling 5.85 lakh sq ft, Rs. 2,150 crores

items.quote: As of now the plan is to deploy the funds that are raised. And if required, if we fall short an interim debt of say 20% debt to equity ratio is what we are comfortable with. items.quote: Yes. So, we save on the rentals, we have a faster turnaround, we have better IRR. The receivables come in faster and we save on the admin cost, salaries and rent als. And the money turning is faster, that gives us a better IRR. The overheads are lesser, the rentals are lesser

items.statement: R&D spend expected to be 8.5-9% of sales for full fiscal year
items.quote: The R&D spend was at 8% of sales and was higher by 25 basis points YoY and lower by 110 basis points on a QoQ basis. We expect the investment to be in the range of 8.5-9% for the full fiscal.

items.statement: Normalized effective tax rate expected around 25%
items.quote: We expect our normalized ETR to be around 25%.

items.statement: Capex cash outflow was Rs. 709 crores in Q3FY25

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin at 59%, up 19 bps YoY, down 91 bps QoQ

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 27.5%, down 176 bps YoY and 95 bps QoQ

items.statement: SG&A expected to stay around 28% of sales going forward
items.quote: Yeah, around this level.

items.quote: We said that we will grow. We will try and bring down the credit deposit ratio as quickly as possible over a 2- to 3-year timeframe. FY '25 will be lesser than the system. FY '26 will be in line with the system. FY '27 will be faster than the system.

items.statement: Expect loan growth step-up in FY26 and further step-up in FY27 as macro improves
items.quote: In FY'26, you would see a step-up. In FY'27, you will see a further step-up.

items.statement: NIMs range-bound and stable despite tight liquidity and CASA pressure
items.quote: NIMs have remained reasonably range-bound and stable despite the headwinds from tight liquidity, leading to a tight pricing environment.

items.statement: Urban demand moderating, rural demand picking up, government spending accelerating in H2
items.quote: We are in the midst of a very challenging macro environment, with tight liquidity conditions, signs of moderating urban demand, a tepid private capital expenditure programs, volatility and depreciation of the Indian rupee, capital outflows from equity and debt markets due to uncertainty around the new U.S. administration. However, we also see some drivers of growth or some positive signs as well.

items.statement: Deposit mix shifting to time deposits (22.7% growth) at expense of CASA; retail loan mix expected to rise over time
items.quote: We have a choice to make in terms of whether we want a holistic customer relationship that includes time deposit, which grew at 22.7% in this quarter, right? But then I think the business leaders did make the choice to say that we need to keep that customer relationship alive and growing

items.statement: Asset quality stable across all segments including unsecured, commercial, emerging corporate; agri slippages seasonal
items.quote: The quality of the overall book across segments continues to remain stable, which is the retail, the retail unsecured, secured or in the CRB book, the SME book or the SLI book or whatever or the wholesale book for that matter, pretty stable across all of those segments as we see.

items.statement: Agri NPA coverage lower due to secured nature and lower LGD; PCR ex-agri at 71%
items.quote: Excluding the seasonal agri, the slippages are flat period-to-period. And so, they are, since they are in the early buckets, the PCR, excluding agri, is at 71%, which is same as what it was in the prior quarter. That's the PCR.

items.statement: Borrowing cost fully loaded ~8%; investment yield on excess liquidity 6.5-7%; corporate spreads tightening 10-25 bps

That includes the cost of the hedges and so on, fully loaded cost, it comes to about 8% or so on the borrowing.

items.statement: Deposit growth 15% YoY average, outpacing system; loan growth 8% YoY AUM; CD ratio normalizing
items.quote: We have seen robust growth in our average deposits at about 15%, which continued to gain market share. And our AUM advances growth of 8% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Bought back INR44 billion of bonds this quarter to optimize borrowing costs
items.quote: For example, in this quarter, we did buy, call it, INR44 billion or INR4,400 crores of bonds and extinguished. That's part of the ongoing process, especially it manages and optimizes whatever is possible, and we mix and match and do these things.

items.statement: Contingent provision released INR3 billion on recovery from performing wholesale account
items.quote: Current quarter, there's a large wholesale account, which is performing wholesale account, which means they're not an NPA, performing account, which we had tagged that for contingent provision because our credit risk assessment showed that vulnerability. we provided -- and in this quarter, we received money, we collected cash, and so the contingent was not required. We recovered.

items.statement: PSL compliance at aggregate 40%+; ~1% shortfall in small/marginal farmer and weaker sections to be closed by Q4
items.quote: Our priority sector is last year or as we see now, at the aggregate level, we meet the target, 40-plus percent. The only area last year and as we speak now, we see is that small and marginal farmer and the weaker section. There are dual qualifications between them, but that's normally about a percentage points we always look for opportunities.

items.statement: Cost growth contained at ~7.5% YoY despite branch additions; cost-to-income stable at 40-41%
items.quote: On the cost to income, I want to add that we are at about 40.5% or so between 40%, 41%. It's been stable at that level. Two aspects to it. If you look at the rate of growth of cost, about 7.5% or so rate of growth of cost, right? The country's inflation is between 5% and 6% at an aggregate level and depending on the wage and so on and so forth, it's getting maintained at that level, sub 8%.

items.statement: TMD order book is 3,100 crores with 2,300 crores active orders; LMW Global order book is 280 crores; LMW China order book is 22 crores
items.quote: With respect to the order book, currently we hold an order book of 3,100 crores of which the active orders are around 2,300 crores.

items.quote: We are not looking at any price hikes because we have done a price hike in the month of May 2024. So at the moment we are not looking at any price hikes as far as the segment is concerned.

items.quote: The auto segment is now closer to 45% followed by General engineering, industrial machinery, pump and valve, tool room and electronics.

items.quote: With respect to order book, yes, the order book is pretty much the same range around 400 odd crores over the next two and a half years.

items.quote: We are talking about Bangladesh which has a foreign currency issue. Shipments are still happening; products are still getting shipped. But of course, they do have a foreign currency issue.

items.quote: Our focus Today is basically to be not in that segment because then what happens is we are investing a ton of time, ton of money and then it's going to take a long time for us to get back our investment.

items.quote: The total of first three quarters because fourth quarter is not likely to add much to the EBITDA. That is approximately what I said.

items.quote: For tech programs, while we've seen that hiring sentiment in tech is improving, actual hiring has not picked up as yet. This impacted our growth this quarter. items.quote: will remain in the 20 to 24 range as far as we are concerned

items.statement: Input prices expected to remain benign in Q4

items.statement: VAM consumption cost at $884/ton in Q3, expected similar in Q4

items.statement: Rural growth continues to be ahead of urban growth
items.quote: That is true. Even now, our rural is ahead of urban. As we go ahead, yes.

items.quote: Based on current visibility, we expect it to be around the 40 bps range going forward as well —40 to 45 bps as a range

items.quote: On MFI, there is definitely a high level of stress compared to what it has been across, mi rroring what the sector has been facing. Comparatively, we have a better asset quality is still holding on

items.quote: And I would say unsecured, these sensitive advances are still a small percentage of our balance is below 5%. And therefore, while there is stress on that, we have tapered our QoQ growth on these sensitive segments.

items.quote: SA averages grew by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter, CA averages increased by 1%, and overall, Average CASA grew by 2.3% this quarter.

items.quote: Wholesale term deposits — specifically those above ₹3 crore —have decreased from ₹37,821 crore to ₹33,848 crore, representing a drop of nearly ₹4,000 crore.

items.statement: Commercial Banking grew 5.65% QoQ and 24.5% YoY; Business Banking grew 13% YoY with record December disbursements
items.quote: Commercial Banking grew 5.65% quarter-on-quarter and 24.5% year-on-year, reflecting healthy momentum. Business Banking grew 13% year-on-year, with record disbursements in December.

items.statement: Expect low single-digit price growth in near term if commodity prices remain at current levels

items.statement: Expect to maintain EBITDA at lower end of 23-24% range amidst inflationary material prices

NMI turned positive last quarter, signifying net cost inflation for the business.

items.statement: Total FMCG volume growth slowed over last 6 months indicating subdued demand; urban growth moderating while gradual rural recovery sustained

items.quote: The business has scaled rapidly to cross an annual revenue run rate of INR500 crores in a short span of 4 years, while being one of the very few insurgent players that have stayed profitable since inception.

items.statement: Board approved scheme of arrangement to demerge Ice Cream business into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited; 1 equity share of new entity for every 1 share held in HUL
items.quote: Our Board of Directors has approved the scheme of arrangeme nt to demerge HUL's Ice Cream business into Kwality Walls ’s (India) Limited. Pursuant to the scheme, 1 equity share of the new entity will be allotted for every 1 equity share held in HUL.

items.statement: Expect full year ETR around 25.5% after prior period tax adjustments
items.quote: We expect our full year ETR to be around 25.5% after taking into consideration prior period tax adjustments.

items.statement: Year-to-date gross margin at 50.4% down 20 bps year-on-year; EBITDA maintained at 23.7%
items.quote: Gross margin at 50.4% was down 20 bps year-on-year. We continue to maintain EBITDA in a healthy range at 23.7%.

items.statement: Foods & Refreshment margin range of 19% to 20% is considered healthy for the business.
items.quote: And we believe that margin range of 19% to 20% is pretty healthy for our Foods business.

items.statement: Personal Care margin band of 17% to 18% is considered healthy; priority is sustained growth over margin expansion.
items.quote: Again, at a 17%, 18% margin band, I think, is a pretty healthy margin for the Personal Care business.

items.statement: Overall HUL margin improvement model is mix-led and leverage-led.
items.quote: And the totality of the margin outlook for Hindustan Unilever, the way we want to drive this improvement - mix led, and leverage led.

items.statement: Near-term FMCG demand moderation to continue; rural recovery gradual, urban demand compressed with small pack downtrading.
items.quote: And now having experienced one more quarter, we see of a similar view that the moderation that we have seen will be there in near term to continue.

items.statement: Small pack downtrading is transitory and should self-correct in a quarter or two.
items.quote: We do believe that this will be there for a quarter or 2 more. And -- but it is transitory in nature.

items.statement: Commodity inflation benign at aggregate level; palm oil down to ~INR 1,000 from INR 1,150-1,200; tea down 7% sequentially.
items.quote: In fact, palm oil, crude palm oil, it went up to INR1,150, INR1,200, and it has come down to more line INR1,000 as we speak in early part of January.

items.statement: Negative mix in Q3 due to Home Care outperformance and small pack shift; premium mix contribution up 100 bps YoY.
items.quote: And even in this quarter, our contribution of 120 index and above segment is 100 basis points more than last year's same period.

items.statement: Small pack negative mix impact expected to self-correct in a quarter; premium portfolio drive to continue building mix.
items.quote: I do believe and we do believe at this point in time that the impact of small pack negative mix should self-correct in a quarter or so, number one.

items.statement: Stratos formulation rollout risk assessed at 100% confidence after 6-9 months in market across WIMI clusters.
items.quote: Yes. So, answer is yes, and I would not say 80%, Manoj, I'll say 100. We are very confident that Stratos formulation is the right thing to do.

items.statement: Minimalist acquisition at pre-money INR 2,955 crores (5.9x sales); 90.5% acquired, balance 9.5% in 2 years.
items.quote: I quoted a number that on secondary buyouts that we have done pre- money at INR2,955 crores at 5.9 sales multiple.

items.statement: Minimalist integration model preserves founder agility ('speed boat') for at least 2 years while leveraging HUL scale.
items.quote: But in the next -- at least 2 years, we want them to operate like a speed boat. We will offer them whatever they need to become more successful.

items.statement: Horlicks focus on improving price-pack architecture to drive large pack usage and enhancing core product taste/stickiness.
items.quote: At this point, what we're trying to now do is to improve the price pack architecture to incentivize large pack usage because by driving more large packs, we know that those houses use more of the category compared to the ones that use small packs.

items.statement: Beauty & Wellbeing 6 big bets portfolio (~INR 2,000 cr) grew strong double digits in Q3 across organized trade and e-commerce.
items.quote: So yes, the INR2,000-odd crores portfolio that we have, Percy, at the 6 big bets we've spoken about, the growth trajectory of that portion of the business continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Beauty & Wellbeing margins to decline from healthy ~30% levels to fund portfolio premiumization (900 bps shift target) and innovation intensity.
items.quote: So, you will see more innovation intensity. You will see more launches as you already have seen this quarter. And also going forward in March quarter as well, it's a busy quarter for us in Beauty & Wellbeing.

items.statement: Organized trade (modern trade + e-commerce) grew double digits in Q3 but slowed vs previous quarter; small/large pack dynamic more pronounced in general trade.
items.quote: Overall, organized trade, if I look at modern trade e-commerce put together, they have grown in double digit. Overall, if I look at the segment and growth like everything else put together, even that has slowed down compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY25 sales volume expected around 5.5 million tonnes, similar to FY24
items.quote: For the full -year FY '25, we believe we will be able to achieve sales volume similar to FY '24 of around 5.5 million.

items.statement: FY26 volume target of 6.4 to 6.5 million tonnes
items.quote: Going to the next year, I think we are looking at anywhere between 6.4 million to 6.5 million as a number , which we should be able to comfortably achieve

items.statement: Prices stable in December, expect similar trend; limited upside until early Q1 FY26
items.quote: December exit all the way up to 10th and 20th prices fortunately remain very, very stable. They have been steady. There has not been an increase, nor there has been a decrease. We expect similar trend to continue with the hope that it further doesn't deteriorate.

items.statement: Current prices ₹2-3 per bag above Q3 average in South; similar in Odisha and MP
items.quote: I think it is safe to assume around ₹2 to ₹3 increase, not more, because in between, it went up, but it gradually s lipped, barring ₹2 to ₹3 in some of the markets.

items.statement: Operating leverage could add ₹200-300 EBITDA per tonne; internal target ~₹500+ EBITDA/tonne for FY26
items.quote: I think the operating leverage itself should add another ₹200 to ₹300 EBITDA per tonne kind of a number

items.statement: ₹88 crore spent in 9M FY25; ₹241 crore balance over next 1.5 years, bulk in Andhra
items.quote: The amount spent so far for FY '25 is ₹88 crore is what we have spent. The balance to be spent is ₹241 crore over the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Andhra plant pre-heater commissioning advanced to Oct-Nov 2025 (Dussehra) from March 2026
items.quote: We should, in all likelihood, be ready for this Dussehra which is in October, November, we should be ready to commission the Andhra plant, especially the pr e-heater.

items.statement: Demand recovery sharp in Q3; January strong despite festive week; Q4 momentum expected to continue
items.quote: January month in Andhra is almost , a week of it is usually a festivities because of Sankranti. The whole week would be lost. In spite of loss of week, I think it has been an extremely strong month. That only indicates that Q4 also is going very, very strong.

items.statement: Higher OPC share kept fuel cost at ₹1,466/tonne; expect similar trend
items.quote: It is ₹1,466 per ton of cement in spite of having higher OPC, the fuel cost is slightly higher. That is only purely on account of blended cement being lower . We expect similar thin gs to continue

items.statement: Industry volume focus unsustainable; supply additions gradual; prices need to rise to justify M&A
items.quote: It's true th at there is some amount of supply that is likely to happen, and that is likely to continue. We don't see any stoppage to supply coming into the market. Fortunately, that supply is likely to be in a gradual kind of a thing, not in a single burst.

items.statement: Vizag land sale: two of three approvals received; cabinet approval expected end Q4/early Q1; monetisation over 1.5 years post approval
items.quote: I think by middle of Q1 coming year, I think we should have got all the approvals. So, we are just waiting for cabinet approval to come, which is likely probably during end of Q4 to early part of Q1.

items.statement: Waste heat recovery at Gudipadu to save ₹50-75/tonne; Andhra upgrade to save ₹350-400/tonne at Andhra level
items.quote: The waste heat recovery at Gudipadu should save anywhere between ₹50 to ₹75 per ton, primarily because of electricity. But the Andhra upgrade should help us save anywhere between ₹ 350 to ₹400 per ton in terms of cost structure at Andhra level.

items.statement: Pet coke and coal prices expected to remain flat for next six months
items.quote: We believe that the next six months, the prices might remain more or less stable. With Trump coming in a significant way, people talk that the oil prices mig ht come down. That might put some influence on the pet coke prices going lower.

items.statement: Andhra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka growing strongly; Telangana lagging but low-cost housing push may help
items.quote: Andhra is growing very strongly, followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, then only Telangana because unfortunately, the real estate in Hyderabad also has taken a back seat.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue guidance: may miss by up to ~3%; EBITDA margin maintained at 24%
items.quote: Further, we find it necessary to revise our revenue guidance to reflect the impact of the current market uncertainties, slower growth in key sectors and geopolitical factors on our outlook for FY '25. On the consolidated level, we anticipate we may miss our revenue guidance by up to approximately 3% for FY '25. However, we remain confident in our ability to maintain EBITDA margins of 24% for the f

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR 684 cr as of Dec 31, 2024 vs INR 572 cr a year ago
items.quote: Despite the above challenges, we have a healthy order book of INR 684 crores as of December 31, 2024, as against INR 572 crores as of December 31, 2023, which will convert into revenue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Gear division order book INR 684 cr as of Dec 31, 2024; Q3 order intake INR 469 cr (+27.4% YoY)
items.quote: The order intake for the quarter was INR 469 crores, reflecting a healthy 27.4% year -on-year increase. As of 31st December 2024, our order book stood at INR 684 crores, positioning us for sustainable growth in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: MHE division open order book INR 421 cr as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: As of 31 December 2024, the open order book for MHE stood at INR 421 crores, reflecting strong demand and growth prospects.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 EBITDA margin 27% (+150 bps YoY); 9M EBITDA margin 24.3% stable
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR 143 crores, up from INR 120 crores in Q3 FY '24, representing a solid growth of 18.4%. Consequently, our EBITDA margin improved to 27% compared to 25.4% in Q3 FY '24. We have a 150 basis points improvement.

items.statement: MHE EBIT margin surged to 31.6% in Q3 from 18.6% YoY (+1,300 bps) due to favourable mix and aftermarket
items.quote: The EBIT for MHE stood at INR 35 crores compared to INR 12 crores in Q3 FY '24, reflecting a significant turnaround. EBIT margin surged to 31.6% in Q3 FY '25, up from 18.6% in Q3 FY '24, an increase of 1,300 basis points.

items.statement: MHE sustainable EBIT margin guided at 20-22% for next couple of quarters
items.quote: MHE margins will go through fluctuations, okay? Positive as well as negative. So, it is difficult to ascertain because they will depend on the type of product mix that we are able to market and sell depending upon the demand. However, we are reasonably confident that we should be able to maintain anywhere between 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Consolidated sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 23%
items.quote: In terms of the sustainable margin, I said, considered at the consol e level, we see 23% is my sustainable margin.

items.statement: Steel and sugar sectors delaying orders; power, marine, cement expected to drive FY26 growth
items.quote: Apart from this, next year, we are seeing a fairly positive requirement coming up in the marine sector as well as in the power sector. So these are the 2 areas where we feel that there is likely to be a healthy growth.

items.statement: Marine orders expected between Q1-Q3 FY26; order value INR 60-70 cr per order
items.quote: Order value will be ranging from INR 60 crores to INR 70 crores, somewhere. I don't have the exact figure at this point of a time, but we'll just circulate the same to you also.

items.statement: Gear division 9M product mix: 51% standard (CP), 49% engineered (EP)
items.quote: So for the 9 months now considering in this quarter, we had a better revenue from EP that is engineer product. So with this for 9 months, we are now CPs at 51% and EP that is engineered customers product it is 49%.

items.statement: OEM export revenue revised up to INR 50-60 cr for FY25 from earlier INR 25-30 cr
items.quote: But I think we are now at least expected it will reach to INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores at the optimum level itself for this year.

items.statement: Steel sector delaying capex due to Chinese dumping; sugar sector also muted
items.quote: As you might be aware about the steel sector, they are facing a challenge due to the dumping of steel from China and the steel sector, they are waiting for the support from the government. So that's the reason they are using the tactics to delay the ordering though they are ready with the capex plan, but they are delaying that raising the orders of this.

items.statement: Net free cash surplus INR 500+ cr as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our consolidated net free cash surplus stood at INR 500 crores plus as of 31 December 2024, providing us with significant financial flexibility to pursue growth opportunities and maintain operational resilience.

items.statement: After-sales/service share: 34% of 9M revenue (38% in Q3)
items.quote: Our total sales -- the composition between the product and the service, it is 34%. From 34% is the service and 66% is the product sales.

items.statement: Expects 50-75 bps gross margin improvement year on year; 80% gross margin seen as challenging
items.quote: I would expect a 50 to 75 bps gross margin improvement year on year.

items.statement: Targets blended EBITDA margin of 22-23% for FY25; first nine months in line with that target
items.quote: And a margin expansion this year, we have been guiding towards an overall blended EBITDA margin at between 22% and 23%. I think the first 9 months are in line with that.

items.statement: Cash balance expected to reach near INR 150 crores by end of FY25; operating cash generation of INR 15-18 crores per quarter
items.quote: So cash balance, I think we are well on track to get fairly close to the INR 150 crores mark, give or take INR 1 crores or INR 2 crores here and there. Because typically we generate between INR 15 crores to INR 18 crores of operating cash every quarter.

items.statement: Cash will be used for inorganic acquisitions fitting strategy and valuation; disciplined buyer, else cash returned to shareholders
items.quote: Utilization of cash, also nothing changes. I think I have been very categorical in my previous calls that this will be utilized for inorganic strategies. But any inorganic acquisition has to fit both our strategy and also pricing criteria.

items.statement: Growth drivers split roughly one-third each: volume 3-4%, price 3-5%, new products the rest
items.quote: We obviously would like our products to grow between 3% to 4% in terms of volumes, another 3% to 5% comes out of price and the rest comes out of new product launches.

items.statement: Divatrone market hyper-competitive; decline arrested, marginal growth from December; Indocap counterfeit issue resolved, now INR 50-crore brand
items.quote: Divatrone, the market environment hasn't changed much. It remains hyper-competitive. Having said that, while we have a fairly big drop compared to our performance last year, the new performance has stabilized. And in fact, we have started getting into a marginal growth territory starting from December.

items.statement: ESOP cost run-rate INR 17-18 million/quarter for next two quarters, then ~INR 10 million/quarter from September 2025
items.quote: Our current run rate ESOP cost, for next 2 quarters, would be in the region of INR 17 million to INR 18 million per quarter. And starting September '25, it will go down to about INR 10 million per quarter.

items.statement: Management will provide FY26 guidance in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Sahil we will be in condition of giving guidance in the first quarter. So, as a management will make sure we will be close to our guidance, so that's the reason we will give that in the first quarter.

items.statement: Targeting ~50% revenue growth in FY25 vs FY24
items.quote: Yes, more than that yes, in and around that.

items.statement: Leasing vertical annual CAPEX ~Rs 150 crore at Rs 50,000 per seat for 25,000 seats; 15-20% funded by company, rest by landlords
items.quote: Considering that, there's about per seat CAPEX of about Rs. 50,000, that is generally what is the thumb rule that we follow, and there about Rs. 10,000 we consider in terms of investments in deposits. So, if you consider it completely, then in that sense if we are looking at about total 150 crore odd amount of investment.

items.statement: Furniture vertical requires working capital for ~2 months at Rs 150 crore revenue target; no further plant CAPEX needed
items.quote: So, if we are expecting a business of about 150 crore next year in the Furniture vertical and at about two months minimum of the working capital deployment, that's the kind of investment that would be making in the Furniture vertical, there will be no further CAPEX which should be required in the Furniture vertical.

items.statement: Design & Build vertical needs 30-45 days working capital at Rs 225-250 crore revenue target
items.quote: Where, this year we are expecti ng to close , targeting to close this vertical at about 225 , 250 crore and the next year, we obviously would like to kind of continue the same trend of growth, if that we consider for about 30 to 45 days of working capital requirement, that's what would be the investment that would outlay that we would look for in the entire coming financial year

items.statement: Design & Build pipeline Rs 92 crore (Rs 32 crore under execution, Rs 60 crore in progress)
items.quote: The total project pipeline stands at 92 crores, with 32 crores worth of projects under execution and an additional 60 crores in progress.

items.statement: Furniture order pipeline Rs 8.57 crore for 30-day delivery, Rs 14.35 crore for 30-60 day delivery
items.quote: The order pipeline remains robust with projects worth 8.57 crores created for completion within 30 days, and an additional 14.35 crores within 30 to 60 days.

items.statement: Design & Build margins expected 17-18% blended, currently 20-22% due to high-margin contracts
items.quote: With regards to the D &B division, the margins we generally expect a margin range to be anything around 17%, 18% only but largely because of the certain contracts which we are receiving today, that is really contributing in us, enabling a higher margins and obviously, if tomorrow we get the blend, which is likely to happen in the coming quarter where we get the blend of this contract, the average

items.statement: Furniture vertical targets 30% EBITDA margin once at full capacity utilization
items.quote: We believe that 30% EBITDA is something which is really achievable. When we entered the market, based on the market report and the research, we have always been guided that anything between 35% to 40% is something achievable, but realistically speaking, considering the different product mix that one would come up with, achieving 30% margin in our mind is very much achievable, and would be achieved

items.statement: Leasing vertical net margin ~30% after deducting interest cost on owned properties
items.quote: Then you will see it will come out around 30% and that's the kind of margin that we have always guided to the investors that we are trying to achieve from our businesses.

items.statement: Leasing average rent per seat Rs 6,000-7,500, averaging Rs 6,250-6,500; newer seats achieving Rs 7,000+
items.quote: So, we have always maintained that we try to operate within this bracket, which is on an average it ranges from Rs.6000 to Rs.7000, Rs.7500, and an average out to around Rs.6250 to 500 and that's the range that we try to operate and that's how entire economics, also we plan.

items.statement: Office leasing demand growing from corporates and GCCs; furniture and turnkey solutions growing fast
items.quote: Secondly, the office industry is growing lot of corporate and GCC is coming in India so office furnishing and turnkey is growing a lot, so that will be a fast growing business and currently there is robust pipeline in D&B, Design and Build.

items.statement: Economic slowdown risk hedged via diversified verticals and sectors (education, healthcare, non-IT); all verticals real estate dependent but growth expected upward for 1-2 years
items.quote: Yes, the economic slowdown would have an overall impact, but as we can see right now primarily post -COVID the entire office market, and also the way the office premises are getting on a leasing model where the ultimate customers are looking at a solution which is more flexible for them, and more solution which is kind of less CAPEX oriented for them, but they are remaining to be an asset light Co

items.statement: SM REIT DRHP filing expected mid-to-late February 2025; IPO to follow SEBI approval
items.quote: We are expecting that roughly around in the month of February, we are expecting to file the DRHP, offer document with the SEBI, and then as per the approval receiving from the SEBI, immediately upon receiving of the approval we will definitely go for the IPO.

items.statement: SM REIT management fees from subsidiary EFC Investment Manager to add directly to bottom line; property operating expenses move to REIT books
items.quote: So, what in terms of revenue, which will come directly on our books, is the income for the services for management and operation of that entire SM REIT including managing their occupancy, including their marketing activity, administration and operationa l activity, all the activity that we would be carrying out , that would be charged in form of service fee, and that service we will directly add t

items.statement: Leasing seat capacity target 55,000 billable seats by end FY25; 62,000-65,000 total capacity
items.quote: Sir, by end of this financial year from billing perspective, we are trying to achieve total seats, anything around 55,000 seats that we are trying to bring it on a billing level and on a capacity level, obviously we are trying to achieve more than around 62,000 to 65,000 depending upon how the contracts getting closed for acquisition.

items.statement: FY25 revenue degrowth expected around 2.5-2.7% in constant currency
items.quote: There will be a degrowth. And if you look at the first three quarters revenue that does suggest that we will have a degrowth and the degrowth will be in the 2.5% or so range. We are being prudent and therefore we're saying 2.7%, but it will be about the 2.5% range.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 DET exit EBIT margin expected at 13.5% range
items.quote: And that's why we're saying Q4 exit margin will be 13.5% range, which will be what it will be for the year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue will grow quarter-on-quarter, not decline
items.quote: Firstly, I'll say, we will not decline under any circumstance in Q4. Q4 will be a growth quarter. I'll say it's not going to be a huge growth quarter, even as things stand, it is a growth quarter, we will see a b it of growth

items.statement: Target to reach 16% EBIT margin again in FY26, but subordinated to revenue growth
items.quote: What we said earlier was that we will hit 16% once again in FY26. And we are subordinating our margin goal for FY26 to revenue growth.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 order intake highest ever at USD 312 million, double Q2 and 50% above typical run rate
items.quote: The order intake is the highest ever at USD312 million. It's double of what it was in Q2. It's almost 50% higher than our typical quarterly run rate and 5% growth year-on-year despite all the macro challenges.

items.statement: Order backlog at all-time high; 13 large deals won with total contract potential of USD 234 million
items.quote: We have won 13 large deals, and the total contract potential of these deals is 234 million. So, I want to highlight that after some challenging times, order intake is at an all-time high, order backlog is at an all-time high.

items.statement: Annual contract value (ACV) now ~70% of order book vs historical 60%, due to shorter PO tenures
items.quote: The annual contract value will be a significant part of it. It will be about 70% of that is typically now in the ACV. Historically, it would have been lower. Historically, it would have been more in the 60% range.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 DET EBIT margin 13.5%, down 72 bps QoQ due to highest wage hike of FY25 and currency headwinds
items.quote: The Q3 FY25 DET EBIT margin stood at 13.5%, down by 72 bps quarter-on-quarter and this Q-on-Q movement was driven by wage hike impact, which was the highest we had for any quarter in FY25, along with currency headwinds.

items.statement: Transportation BU grew 3.7% QoQ CC on aerospace ramp-ups and steady demand from largest customer
items.quote: On transportation BU, we're seeing some good growth at 3.7% quarter-on-quarter. It is because of the ramp-up in new deals in aerospace in the last 1 year, combined with some good steady demand from existing customers, including our largest customer who is the aerospace customer.

items.statement: Connectivity BU grew 5.7% QoQ CC on strong execution and North America deal ramp-ups
items.quote: Connectivity is another sector where we're seeing very good growth. Quarter-on-quarter, we are seeing 5.7% growth on account of strong execution and ramp-up, especially in some of the North America deals.

items.statement: Sustainability BU down 1.3% QoQ CC as large projects end and new project wins delayed
items.quote: Where we do have a bit of a challenge is in the sustainability sector. This sector is down 1.3% quarter-on-quarter. And much of it is because of the project-based nature of work in this vertical. A couple of the large projects that we've been working on are at the end of their life cycle and some of the newer projects are yet to gain scale.

items.statement: Board approved exploring additional capital raise options for semiconductor subsidiary
items.quote: I'm delighted to announce that we have secured approval from our Board of Directors to explore additional capital raise options for our recently acquired semiconductor subsidiary.

items.statement: Management reaffirms 30% revenue growth and 30-35% PAT growth target for FY25
items.quote: As committed, I still feel 30% won't be a problem. We will grow 30% next year. And after that also I feel 30% is because there is a lot of many things are happening.

items.statement: 30% revenue and 30-35% PAT growth already achieved in 9M FY25, confident of full year target
items.quote: have already achieved for 9 months, Saket, and we will close 30% more up and even bottom line also 30%, 30% yes -between 30%, 35% PAT will also come

items.statement: Full year FY25 content cost expected at INR55-60 crores, below earlier INR70-80 crore target
items.quote: Ankush, it could be in that range of INR55 crores to INR60 crores for the full year. Depending on the releases, but let's say that would be the ballpark.

items.statement: Content investment to increase to 25-27% of revenue from next year onwards
items.quote: Next year onwards, you will see we are consuming around 25%, 27% will invest in content. It will happen.

items.statement: Exciting lineup of releases planned for 2025 as highlighted in investor presentation Slide 9
items.quote: We have a very exciting lineup of releases planned for '25, as highlighted in our investor presentation, Slide 9.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 71.6% for Q3 FY25, content cost at 18.7% of revenue
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margins were at 71.6% and PAT for the quarter stood at INR44.23 crores. That is a growth of 28%. Content cost for the quarter was INR14.55 crores.

items.statement: YouTube Shorts monetization via ads expected in 3-4 quarters, revenue split 55% to labels, 45% to platform
items.quote: Now, YouTube has given us a guaranteed floor which is minimum money, you will get this much money. And if they start up doing ads from those content, then same split happen. 55% for us, 45% for them.

items.statement: Short-form video (Reels, Shorts, TikTok) could become INR100 crore business for Tips in 3-5 years, currently 7-8% of YouTube plays
items.quote: What I see that, let's not talk only on TikTok, TikTok is not in India, and if TikTok comes in India then TikTok, Facebook, reels and that YouTube Shorts can be INR100 crores business for Tips for next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Subscription revenue growing ~40% YoY, Spotify leading growth, but still small portion of digital revenue
items.quote: If you compare year-on-year growth on subscription, it is growing about 40% every year. So, Spotify is doing a great job on that. But yes, it has to become a big number for all of us in the industry.

items.statement: No plans to change content cost accounting policy; full write-off in quarter of release continues
items.quote: We write-off our entire content cost in the quarter of music release even just Hoshiar Singh music, we have released just one song last week of December and we have written-off entire money towards that in this quarter

items.statement: Warner minimum guarantee not booked in accounts; revenue recognized only on actual sales
items.quote: We have got minimum guarantee, but we have not booked that minimum guarantee in our accounts. We have shown as an advance and whatever numbers they are actually selling; whatever business is happening; we are just booking that.

items.statement: Public performance revenue growing strongly driven by live events (Diljit, Coldplay shows featuring Tips songs)
items.quote: See, if you see Diljit shows or just yesterday, I was -- somebody has sent me this Coldplay. A big show of Coldplay. And in that show Jazzy B my artist is singing my song, Tips songs, Naag, Naag, there's a old song, he was singing.

items.statement: International publishing deal with Sony Music Publishing being negotiated for larger agreement
items.quote: Now they are talking to us for a bigger deal. We are discussing with them something, and we'll announce this soon as it happens.

items.statement: Catalogue analysis team formed to analyze revenue contribution by vintage; results in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: No, we are going to do that too. We have made that analysis team. In the next 3, 4 quarters, we will do that too.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance of 10% for FY25; already at 10.45% in 9M and confident of achieving 10.5%
items.quote: When we have grown the advances m ore than 10%, what we have given the guidance double digit at 10.45%, it was led by the RAM credit at 12.32% , a nd our Corporate has grown at 8.08

items.statement: CD ratio comfort level at 78%; currently at 76.65% globally and will not cross 78%

items.statement: Borrowings are largely floating rate; expect interest rate cycle to remain stable or fall, not rise.

items.quote: And as regards domestic NIM is concerned, last time our domestic NIM was at around 3.14%. This quarter it is at 2.98% which is a healthy number. And if I tell you the nine-month domestic NIM, it is at 3.19%.
