items.statement: Rural growth significantly ahead of urban; van program a big driver
items.quote: Our rural growths are significantly ahead of our urban growths, and van has been a big driver of that.

items.statement: Laundry, Air Fresheners, Sexual Wellness growing double-digit volumes; Fab gaining share
items.quote: Our Laundry, Air Fresheners and Sexual Wellness businesses continue to grow double-digit volumes.

items.statement: Incense Sticks share in high single digits; handler share close to 50%
items.quote: First, we should take Incense Sticks, our share now is in high single digits of the overall Incense Stick market and our share of handler is close to 50%.

items.statement: PFAD prices not falling in line with palm oil; margin pressure may persist in Q4
items.quote: PFAD has only dropped 7-8% from its peak. So I mean, at some point of time, these have to normalize.

items.statement: No significant capex or fund raise mentioned
items.quote: We have held our advertising spend at about 10% and delivered a consolidated EBITDA margin of about 20%.

items.statement: Indonesia: 6% volume growth, 9% revenue growth, 12% EBITDA growth in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Indonesia continues its solid performance with 6% volume growth, 9% revenue growth and 12% EBITDA growth.

items.statement: Africa: 9% EBITDA growth, revenue declined 8% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our Africa business continued its solid performance on bottom line, growing at 9% though revenues declined at 8%.

items.statement: Latin America: volume growth >25%, EBITDA margin in double digits
items.quote: Latin America continues to do extremely well with volume growth of greater than 25% and EBITDA margin now in double digits.

items.statement: Dow Jones Sustainability Index included GCPL as only Indian FMCG in Emerging Market and World Index leadership
items.quote: the Dow Jones Sustainability Index has included GCPL as the only FMCG company in India and one of the three worldwide to be part of the ir leadership of the Emerging Market Index and World Index

items.statement: Expect credit cost to anchor around 30 basis points to total assets
items.quote: We do believe that we might have a 10-15 basis points of uptick in the credit cost, but I think it should still be well below 50 basis points. I mean, our sense is about 30 basis points of range is that we should anchor our credit cost to.

items.statement: Target SR recovery of INR 1,200 crores per year and INR 3,000 crores plus total from portfolio
items.quote: But we would be definitely expecting a recovery of somewhere around INR 1,200 crores every year and overall ~INR 3,000 crores plus from this portfolio.

items.statement: Expect NIM improvement from new financial year as retail asset growth picks up
items.quote: And I think we are expecting that going forward especially the start of the new financial year, we would see the growth on the Retail Asset, which is going to help us in having the better Yields and the NIM expansion.

items.statement: Aim to reduce RIDF deposits below 5% of total assets over next 2 to 3 years
items.quote: As outlined earlier, going forward, while we may continue to see some RIDF related calls majorly for periods prior to FY24, but on net absolute basis, Bank looks to be well on course to reduce the same below 5% over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: On track to achieve INR 5,000 crores recovery and resolution guidance for FY25
items.quote: We are on track to achieve the guidance of INR 5,000 crores for FY25 and we would like to highlight that the SR portfolio would continue to contribute towards our recoveries and resolutions even after becoming NIL in terms of net carrying value on our Balance Sheet.

items.statement: Expect cost to income ratio to continue improving from current levels
items.quote: As guided earlier, with asset mix largely remaining stable between Wholesale and Retail, coupled with our on-going transformation exercise including right sizing initiatives and greater leverage of technology, productivity and process improvements, we expect our cost to income ratio to continue to further improve from here on.

items.statement: No equity raise needed as CET1 at 13.3% is adequate for growth requirements
items.quote: Currently we don't feel the need for raising any equity because our core equity is 13.3% is adequate to take care of our growth requirement.

items.statement: Blended savings account cost stable at 5.8%-5.9% over last 3-4 quarters despite rate hikes
items.quote: Our blended SA continues to be stable actually over the last almost 3 to 4 quarters and this is despite some of the rate actions that we took more than 12-months back on across different buckets where we actually took the headline rate higher for balances more than INR 10 lakhs. But despite that over the last one year, in fact our SA cost is largely anchored, I think it hovers around, let's say 5.

items.statement: Net interest margin flat at 2.4% sequentially and year-on-year
items.quote: In Quarter 3, our net interest margin came in at 2.4 %, flat both sequentially as well as same quarter last year.

items.statement: Outstanding security receipts with JCF at INR 2,400 crores; expect INR 3,000 crores recovery from pool
items.quote: So, currently the outstanding SRs with JCF is INR 2,400 crores around that. And I think if we go with the past track record, we would be seeing a recovery of almost INR 3,000 crores from this pool of Security Receipt.

items.statement: Retail advances flattish QoQ and down 3% YoY due to profitability recalibration; SME and Mid-Corporate growing 25%+ YoY
items.quote: On the other hand, our Retail Advances were flattish quarter-on-quarter and were down around 3% Y-o-Y due to ongoing recalibration aimed at profitability improvement. You can see the differential growth rate across the retail products on page 44 of our investor presentation. In the Corporate segment, we have maintained the growth momentum of last few quarters.

items.statement: Target retail-wholesale advances mix of 60:40 to remain stable over medium term
items.quote: At a headline level, there is no change in our overall strateg y and we would like our current advances mix between retail and wholesale, which is currently around 60 :40, to largely remain the same over the medium term

items.statement: New sourcing vintage curves for credit cards and personal loans showing better performance after tightening norms
items.quote: For both PL and Credit Cards, the sourcing quality of the recently acquired portfolio is definitely trending well because, like everybody in the market, there is a fair bit of tightening on the norms.

items.statement: Unsecured portfolio less than 25% of retail assets and less than 10% of total advances
items.quote: In any case, Jai, I think we should also keep in mind the fact that if you look at our Unsecured as a proportion to Retail Assets, and actually if you look at that as a proportion to Total Advances, I mean, we are talking about this portfolio adds up ~25% of our Retail Assets. So, that kind of gives you a good sense that we are not running like a... I'm sorry, at a Bank-wide level, my bad. So, it'

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio at ~71%; comfortable maintaining around 70%
items.quote: We are currently around ~71% on the provisioning coverage and we would like to see that our provision coverage would remain at the same level.

items.statement: Board approved capex of INR 1,100 crores across yarn and fabric verticals focusing on value addition and cost efficiencies
items.quote: To maintain our growth momentum, the Board of Directors have approved a significant capex plan of approximately INR 1,100 crores across the existing verticals, that is yarn and fabrics, mainly focusing on value addition and cost efficiencies.

items.statement: Capex funded by INR 800 crores debt and internal accruals, implementation over 24 months
items.quote: The expansion will be funded by approx INR800 crores of debt and remaining by internal accruals and will be implemented over the next 24 months.

items.statement: IRR on new capex expected in range of 14% to 15%
items.quote: As far as the IRR of the project is concerned, I think the IRR should be in the range of 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA levels of 20% plus for new integrated fiber-to-fabric project
items.quote: We are envisaging an EBITDA levels of 20% plus.

items.statement: New fabric capacity increasing revenue share from 25% to 33%+ should improve overall margin by 150-200 bps if conditions remain same
items.quote: Going forward, this should become nearly 1/3, 33% plus. So that should lead to the improvement in the margin by 150 to 200 basis points overall, if conditions remains as it is.

items.statement: Export recovery seen with India cotton yarn exports rising from 60,000 to 100,000 tons/month, domestic demand steady
items.quote: in the year 2023, our average exports of cotton yarn from the monthly average exports of cotton yarn was in the range of about 60,000 tons per month. I'm talking about the whole country. Now, this has recovered to about 100,000 tons at this point of time

items.statement: Expect similar revenue numbers in FY26 as FY25 assuming stable cotton prices, no formal guidance given
items.quote: We expect the raw cotton to remain at the similar level what it was there in this financial year. So expect similar kind of revenue numbers going forward as well.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread (delta) was ~INR 100/kg in Q3 (RM INR 161/kg, yarn INR 265-266/kg), expect similar or slightly higher delta in coming quarters
items.quote: In the last quarter, our raw material prices were about INR161 a kg and our yarn prices were about INR265, INR266 a kg. So delta was about INR100. We expect the similar delta or maybe a higher delta -- slightly higher delta to be maintained in the coming quarters.

items.statement: International cotton prices at lower end of cycle, downside limited to 5-7%, Indian cotton at MSP ~INR 54,000, expect stability
items.quote: We expect that the cotton prices should remain at this MSP levels of INR54,000 around.

items.statement: Fabric revenue currently ~25%, expected to reach one-third (33%+) of revenue after capex
items.quote: At the moment, our revenue is about 25%. And with this capex going forward, we are expecting that it will be one-third of our revenues, the expected revenues.

items.statement: 12-15% of India spinning capacity closed or closing due to uneconomical size, old technology, and capital constraints
items.quote: We have seen a lot of smaller capacities to the tune of -- if you talk about the total capacity, about 12% to 15% of the spinning capacity is already closed or on the verge of closures.

items.statement: Bangladesh political disruption may shift new garment orders to India, but short-term supply chain unchanged
items.quote: The new business which is supposed to come to Bangladesh is moving out of that country. They may able to hold to the quantity volumes which they are doing, but new business is definitely coming to India as well as to other competing countries.

items.statement: Total debt ~INR 1,250 crores as of Dec 2024 (term INR 850 cr + WC INR 400 cr), new project adds INR 800 cr term loan, ~INR 350 cr repayment over 2 years, total debt ~INR 1,900 cr by Mar 2027
items.quote: By March '27, we'll be close to about INR1,900 crores total debt.

items.statement: Knitting capacity utilization at 60% (28 tons/day capacity), weaving/finishing at 90%+, spinning at 95%+
items.quote: is in the Kgs and the tons. The knitting capacity is about 28 tons a day, that is 11,000 tons every year, and we are at about 60%, that is about 1,700 tons for this quarter

items.statement: Expect loan book of Rs. 5,800-6,000 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: So, we expect the book anywhere between Rs. 5,800 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores, that's where we would lend as far as this financial year is concerned.

items.statement: Target quarterly disbursements of Rs. 800-1,000 crores in FY26
items.quote: Going forward, we would seek to disburse on an average close to some Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 1,000 crores on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Target FY26 disbursements of Rs. 3,500-4,000 crores
items.quote: So, it would be anywhere Rs. 3,500 crores to Rs. 4,000 crores of disbursements for the next year.

items.statement: Expect Q4 disbursements to double first nine months total
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic that what disbursement we did in the first nine months, we will be able to double that in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Pipeline of proposals under evaluation at Rs. 500-600 crores
items.quote: We do have a significant pipeline in terms of the number of proposals that are currently under evaluation, which would be maybe in the range of at least Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 600 crores.

items.statement: Target interest spread of 2%-2.5%
items.quote: focus should be on our interest spread , where we are targeting to maintain in the range of 2% to 2.5% at least, which as of now it is standing at 1.85

items.statement: NIM expected to decline but stay above 3% over time
items.quote: Of course, it would be maintained in a certain range. It should be over 3% over a period of time.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to stabilize at 15% by end of FY26
items.quote: So, by the end of FY '26, this should be at 15%-odd, that's what it would stabilize at.

items.statement: NSL stay vacated in December; resolution expected by next quarter
items.quote: We are happy to state that in the month of December, the stay in Telangana High Court has been vacated. And then the ball has now shifted to the NCLT. We expect a resolution. So, this is a case which accounts for Rs. 125 crores.

items.statement: Vento resolution expected by March 31; full recovery by June quarter
items.quote: We expect to resolve this asset by the end of this quarter, by the end of March 31st, when we will have the winning bidder. And two, more importantly, the entire money would come to the organization before the end of the June quarter.

items.statement: Danu resolution expected by June
items.quote: We are progressing towards resolving this and we expect this to be resolved by June.

items.statement: Received in-principle approval for Rs. 500 crores lending line from financial institution
items.quote: I am happy to state that yesterday we received an in-principle approval from one financial institution for Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: CFO expected to join by end of March or early April; CCO by March 31
items.quote: We expect the Chief Financial Officer to join by the end of March or early April, that's what we expect. And as far as the Chief Compliance Officer is concerned, we have got some restructuring, by March 31st the Chief Compliance Officer will be in place.

items.statement: ESG roadmap to be fleshed out; details to be shared in April or July quarter
items.quote: we are developing a roadmap for ESG. So that apart from our financial performance, we are coming across as one of the key o r leading organizations in ESG. And as far as ESG is concerned, once the roadmap is fleshed out, in the subsequent, i.e., in the April or the July quarter, we will be able to share more

items.statement: Management stopped giving formal guidance but expects Q4 FY25 to be much better and aims for revenue closer to Rs 700 crore per quarter
items.quote: We have stopped giving guidance, but I think, we are looking for expecting better, much better next quarter. So, that's what, we would like to look at it. I mentioned to you Rs.700 Crs a quarter. I think we will be closer to that.

items.statement: Central 1 Credit Union deal adds Rs 200 crore ARR from 160 credit unions in Canada, expected to close in a couple of weeks
items.quote: So, I think it Rahul, you have to understand this like acquisition of business of Rs.200 crs as a revenue line. ARR business Rs.200 crs running it and upgrading it using our eMACH.ai technology.

items.statement: eMACH.ai chosen by 11 global customers in Q3 FY25 across key regions including US, Europe, Africa, Middle East, and Asia Pacific
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, eMACH.ai achieved significant milestones by being chosen by 11 global customers across key regions, showcasing its capability to address diverse and complex financial requirements.

items.statement: Year-to-date 34 deal wins and 37 go-lives across digital transformation projects globally
items.quote: For the year till date, we had 34 wins and we had gone live on 37 digital transformational projects

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 20% with EBITDA of Rs 121 crore on revenue of Rs 607 crore
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 121 crore, with a margin of 20%.

items.statement: License-linked revenue (Platform, License, AMC) contributed 48% of total revenue at Rs 292 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The License-linked revenue, comprising Platform, License, and AMC, stood at INR 292 crore, contributing nearly 48% of total revenue this quarter.

items.statement: LTM ARR reached Rs 700 crore as of Q3 FY25, underscoring platform stickiness
items.quote: The LTM ARR as of Q3 FY25 was INR 700 crore, underscoring the trust and stickiness of our platform-driven solutions.

items.statement: R&D capitalisation target of Rs 140 crore for FY25 will be met; absolute R&D spend to continue at current run rate
items.quote: As far as the R&D spends are concerned, we only look at the absolute numbers. So, Rs.140 crore is the target and that's the budget that we had put in the beginning of the year. And, we will be meeting that budget.

items.statement: Pipeline growing faster than revenue with 12-month sales cycle; Europe and Americas each potential Rs 1,000 crore markets in next four years
items.quote: We have a good pipeline. For the pipeline to closure, it says cycle time of 12 months. So, when we went to eMACH.ai marketplace, putting to Europe and Americas. So, now if you look at it, Europe and Americas, both market Americas will be Rs.600 Crs market as of now, Europe will be another Rs.600 Crs. So, we have a potential as both the market could be 1,000 Crs market in next four years.

items.statement: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) receivables delayed; no comment on resolution timeline
items.quote: No comment. Government is government. So, they are delaying the process right now. We have to look what we can do.

items.statement: Strategic investment of Rs 20 crore in DigiVation (GlobalLinker) to build interconnected commerce ecosystem for SMEs, corporates, and banks
items.quote: Our strategic investment of Rs.20 Cr in DigiVation Digital Solutions Pvt Ltd positions Intellect as a leader in corporate and government e-procurement, driving growth in trade and supply chain finance globally.

items.statement: Purple Fabric platform adopted by 20+ P&C insurance carriers after individual POCs and evaluations
items.quote: We have a significant presence amongst the P&C Insurance leaders with our Purple Fabric platform adopted by 20+ Carriers after individual POCs and evaluation.

items.statement: Targeting 20% year-on-year revenue growth trajectory; Q4 FY25 revenue expected close to Rs.700 Crs
items.quote: We are looking for 20% growth year on year. That trajectory, we want to keep it whether its 15%, 16%, 18%. Those are the number which we look at it as a trajectory.

items.statement: Aims to reach Rs.4,000 Crs revenue in next four years
items.quote: If you have somebody talk to me for next 4 years where we will be reaching, we are saying we can be Rs.4,000 Crs in next four years.

items.statement: Mature products yield 30%+ margins; portfolio target 30% operating margin in 4 years
items.quote: The mature product gives a margin of 30% plus. So, like, GTB has a business if you have a separate business that will give 30% plus margin.

items.statement: Targets Rs.1,000 Crs PAT margin in four years
items.quote: Rs.1, 000 Crs margin will be there after four years, definitely. If you want to put that in my mouth, we are also looking for 1,000 Crs margin in four years.

items.statement: Cost structure stable at Rs.475-485 Crs last four quarters; margin expansion expected as revenue crosses Rs.700 Crs
items.quote: If you look at the cost structure in last four quarters, it remains around Rs.475 to Rs.480 or Rs.485 Crs. And the revenue number is Rs.607 Crs number or you take Rs.625 Crs, the number will be different. As soon as it becomes Rs.700 Crs, the margin will look very different.

items.statement: Three Rs.1,000 Crs businesses planned: GTB (achieved), GCB (next year), AI (building)
items.quote: Now business 1 GTB has been Rs.1,000 Crs plus, business 2 is now GCB will be Rs.1,000 Crs next year. Now we are building AI business into this.

items.statement: Demand evident from pipeline; outlook supports billion-dollar revenue target in 3-4 years
items.quote: See, the demand is very much there and which is pretty evident from the pipeline that we have. And the outlook also we talked about in the next 3-4 years, Arun also talked about it to create a billion-dollar thing.

items.statement: Acquisition of Central 1 initially margin dilutive, targets accretive in 18-36 months via cross-sell
items.quote: We want to bring it to the value accretive in next 18-36 months period.

items.statement: Funnel value ~Rs.10,000 Crs in Q3 FY25; Purple Fabric adoption focus over revenue initially
items.quote: Almost Rs.10,000 Crs of the value of the funnel in Q3 FY 25.

items.statement: No quarterly guidance due to large deal volatility; 6-month pipeline-to-closure delay
items.quote: The guidance is big because these deals are very large values in enterprise space. If deal value is 5 million dollars, it switched the revenue, and so the last 12 months numbers are more projectable.

items.statement: Expect net marginal decline in general staffing headcount in Q4 FY25, primarily driven by BFSI sector weakness
items.quote: I think there will be a net decline of a small number that we do foresee for Q4. And I called that out in my narrative. While we will have BFSI contributing to a larger element of the decline.

items.statement: Expect normalization and positive outlook for general staffing headcount growth from Q1 FY26 onwards
items.quote: But I think post Q4 we do see normalization coming back and there are dialogues and feedbacks from companies about looking to add headcount thereafter and so on. So I think at this point, while we've seen it subdued for Q3 and Q4, I think Q1 onwards, it is the initial outlook from the sector and companies is quite positive.

items.statement: Not projecting any EBITDA contribution from Ikigai in Q4 FY25; meaningful contribution expected from FY26 onwards
items.quote: We are not projecting any EBITDA contribution from Ikigai in Q4 FY '25. However, FY '26 and thereon will have a meaningful contribution from this entity.

items.statement: EdTech business expected to maintain 6% to 7% EBITDA margin for full year FY25
items.quote: On a full year basis, EdTech can maintain 6% to 7% EBITDA this year.

items.statement: Inorganic contribution from TSR Darashaw and Crystal HR expected to be about INR1.1 crores in Q4 FY25 EBITDA
items.quote: Inorganic contribution by these two entities would be about INR1.1 crore s in Q4 FY '25 EBITDA of the TeamLease

items.statement: HR Services expected to turn positive in Q4 FY25 and for full year FY25
items.quote: HR Services, I think with the seasonality element of EdTech getting pushed is really why the loss is there. With the catch-up, we should turn positive back in Q4. Bhargav: No. So for the full year

items.quote: Last quarter, we announced the acquisition of 90% stake in TSR Darashaw HR services and 30% stake in Crystal HR. These two entities are currently at an annual run rate of INR22 crores in revenue and INR7.2 crores in profits.

items.statement: Invested in Ikigai partnership for specialized staffing expansion in Singapore and Middle East; breakeven business with INR20-odd crores annual revenue
items.quote: Our new IT staffing acquisition, Ikigai Enablers currently have an annual revenue of INR20-odd crores and breakeven at bottom line.

items.statement: Signed 34 new logo sign-ups in general staffing in Q3 FY25, 80% on variable markup model
items.quote: On a positive note, our sales effort brought in 34 new logo sign-ups, primarily in the consumer, retail and manufacturing segments, out of which 80% of the variable mark up.

items.statement: Signed 8 key clients in specialized staffing in Q3 FY25, including 3 very large strategic accounts
items.quote: On the sales front, we signed 8 key clients in the last quarter, including 3 very large strategic accounts.

items.statement: Specialized staffing achieved marginal improvement in year-on-year profitability in Q3 FY25 driven by wallet share expansion, cost savings, and one-time benefits
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, we achieved a small but positive net headcount growth for the first time in several quarters, along with increase in quarter-on-quarter revenue and a marginal improvement in year-on-year profitability, largely driven by expansion of wallet share within existing customers, cost-saving initiatives and onetime sourcing and absorption benefits.

items.statement: HCM vertical (including TSR Darashaw and Crystal HR) targeting 6% to 7% EBITDA margins after 12-month integration period
items.quote: With this contribution, we should be able to get to an EBITDA margins of 6% to 7% after a 12-month period in this vertical.

items.statement: BFSI sector remains stable with flat headcount due to tighter RBI norms; enforcement of KYC guidelines to continue impacting Q4 FY25
items.quote: As we had called out last quarter, the BFSI sector remains stable due to tighter norms around lending in micro finance, credit cards, personal loans and similar areas, resulting in a flat headcount by quarter end. Of course, on an ongoing basis, including for Q4, enforcement of some of the RBI guidelines around KYC will continue to impact us not just in Q3 but including in Q4 as well.

items.statement: Manufacturing and telecom saw low single-digit growth; mobile manufacturing experiencing slowdown due to weak smartphone demand
items.quote: Manufacturing and Telecom saw low single-digit growth, which while positive had limited impact on overall numbers. India's mobile manufacturing sector is currently experiencing a degree of slowdown due to weak demand for smartphones, particularly featured phones and entry-level devices in 4G, as highlighted in some of the media reports as well.

items.statement: Specialized staffing: GCCs contribute ~30% of headcount but 55-60% of net revenue; IT services decline not fully offset by GCC growth
items.quote: Currently, about one-third of our associate headcount is deployed with these GCCs, contributing to about 55% to 60% of our net revenue as of the last quarter. Beyond GCCs, we've also increased our focus on hiring for tech and specialized roles in the non-tech industry. While both GCCs and the non-tech sectors are expanding, their growth has not been sufficient to offset the decline in the IT servi

items.statement: Cost of funds expected at lower end of 7.10%-7.15% guided range for FY25
items.quote: Even with this increase, we expect to be at the lower end of our guided range of 7.10% to 7.15% for cost of funds for the year.

items.statement: Full-year credit cost guided at 1.55%-1.6% for FY25
items.quote: But I think we are expecting our credit cost overall, yearly basis at north of 6%. It might touch 7% too. That is why we have commented that our overall credit cost of the year would be in the range of 1.55-1.6%.

items.statement: ROA guidance of 1.6% for FY25, within striking range for Q4
items.quote: In terms of outlook for the next quarter, credit cost will stay elevated, driven by unsecured, but we expect to be within striking range of our ROA guidance of 1.6%.

items.statement: Full-year GLP growth expected around 20%, secured assets 23%-24%
items.quote: Overall, GLP growth is expected to be around 20%, with secured assets growing around 23% to 24% and continued degrowth in MFI and credit cards portfolio.

items.statement: Wheels book full-year growth expected more than 25%
items.quote: Growth for the full year is expected to be more than 25% and remains in the top tier of peer banks and NBFC.

items.statement: Mortgages: MBL low teens growth, home loans 20%-25% for full year
items.quote: For full year, MBL is expected to grow in low teens and home loans in a range of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Commercial banking full-year growth expected north of 30%
items.quote: Total GLP grew 22% year-to-date and 6.4% quarter-on-quarter and is expected to grow north of 30% for the full year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected 57%-58% for FY25, targeting sub-55% in next two years

items.statement: Plan to open 70-80 new branches next year, mostly in top cities

items.statement: Wheels distribution expansion to 250-300 new touchpoints by end of FY26
items.quote: By the end of FY26, we are expecting to expand to another 250 to 300 touch points, including UP and South India.

items.statement: Mortgages distribution expansion by 130-150 touchpoints in FY26
items.quote: In FY26, we would expand our presence by another 130 to 150 touchpoints.

items.statement: NIM declined 23 bps QoQ to 5.9% in Q3 due to investment book mix, loan mix, and interest reversal
items.quote: Net interest margin declined by 23 bps from 6.1% in Q2 to 5.9% in Q3. This was driven AU Small Finance Bank January 24, 2025 by higher mix of investment book on average during the quarter, which had an impact of 10 bps, adverse loan mix because of lower MFI and higher cost of funds, which had an impact of 9 bps, and interest reversal on NPAs, which had an impact of 4 bps

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds improved from 7.7% in FY24 to 7.4% YTD
items.quote: Notably, our incremental cost of funds has improved, declining from 7.7% in FY24 to 7.4% year-to-date.

items.statement: Savings and fixed deposit rates adjusted this week with 10 bps increase on peak FD rate and savings slabs widened to 7.25%
items.quote: This week, we adjusted our savings and fixed deposit rates to market condition, introducing 10 bps increase on our peak fixed deposit rate, and widening the slabs in savings accounts offering 7.25% interest rate.

items.statement: Economic slowdown post-October affected credit demand; rural consumption and govt capex showing signs of bounce back
items.quote: Post-October, however, there was a slowdown in economic activity on the ground. While there are some signs of bounce back in rural consumption and government CAPEX, overall momentum remains below expectation.

items.statement: FY25 asset growth guidance lowered to around 20% from 25%
items.quote: So, that remain intact and all put together is around 20% because it's still 20% is 2x of the industry average.

items.statement: FY25 deposit growth guidance of 23-24%
items.quote: FY25 we are saying 23%- 24% deposit growth, 20% asset growth.

items.statement: Cost of funds guidance revised to 7.07-7.08% for FY25

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 55% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: the hope is this that we might be, it should be lesser than the cost of income what we'll do this year, so that we remain on the path to become a 55% cost of income in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: ROA target of 2% linked to interest rate cuts
items.quote: the moment we start seeing the interest rate cut and our cost of money getting to a right level, you will see us reaching 2% ROA.

items.statement: MFI book expected to deliver 3% ROA sustainably with buffers
items.quote: I believe you can handle with maybe 5% to 8% kind of book in any balance sheet. You want to add, because Rajeev has handled it for last 12 years, it's good to hear his views.

items.statement: MFI industry over-leverage issue peaking; operating improvement seen from December
items.quote: Early green shoots, I would say, were in October, but we had more confidence that we derived from the December data. And by very logical nature of the product, the way we're building a new book, the way the industry is working together on this, I am reasonably confident January-February-March will be operating-wise better.

items.statement: MFI credit cost problem largely behind by Q2 FY26
items.quote: I think by Q2, we should largely be behind over-leveraged credit cost problem.

items.statement: Unsecured lending cap at 15% overall, currently ~11%; MFI at 7%
items.quote: Overall, the cap of unsecured lending is 15%, is around ~11%. We want to stick to that.

items.statement: Secured retail assets growing 20-24%, commercial banking growing 30%
items.quote: Other than that, secure retail asset is growing in the range of 20% to 24%. Commercial banking is growing in the range of 30%.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency improved to 98.7% in December from 98.5% in Q3
items.quote: The December number inched up to 98.7% (collection efficiency) and that was the second best number in the calendar year H2.

items.statement: MFI SMA and NPA recovery improving due to recovery team expansion to 1500 from 600
items.quote: we have increased our headcount from 600 that we had on the recovery vertical as of June, we have reached a number of about 1500 and higher trained and stabilized team. So, because of that, our efficiencies coming from the SMA book, coming from the NPA books has also started seeing improvements.

items.statement: PCR at 61% but adjusted for technical write-offs is north of 80%; target ~70%
items.quote: If you write back the technical write off in our PCR calculation, we are north of 80%. But we have very prudent write off policy also that so that we don't hang on the bad assets on the balance sheet. So, if you ask me and if you carefully see the internal calculation which is not available to you, our secured asset is around 60%, our unsecured asset is around 80%, even our MFI business is around

items.statement: Gold loan regulatory changes create level playing field; targeting faster delivery via Fincare expertise
items.quote: So, we are also thinking about it that how we can master ourselves now when there is a level playing field available now, right? And we have the advantage of cost, we have advantage of risk weight and we have the advantage of brand. I think now it's a level playing field and I think many banks would be doing this now in my opinion but being with Fincare, Fincare is doing this business for the last

items.statement: CGFMU guarantee cover on MFI portfolio increasing to ~90%; eliminates provisioning requirement
items.quote: Now from this financial year, we have covered our microfinance loan. So, first quarter it was lesser and now maybe going forward, maybe around 90% portfolio of microfinance will be covered in this guarantee program. Yes, cost is there, but if we see the overall benefit of coverage versus the cost, right, it is much, much beneficial. And then of course there is no provisioning requirement if we cov

items.statement: MFI lender cap reduced from 4 to 3 per borrower effective April; bank has already implemented
items.quote: We have started. We can't comment on the industry. We have started.

items.statement: Revenue guidance revised downwards; FY25 revenue now expected at Rs. 1,300-1,400 crores vs prior Rs. 1,400-1,500 crores
items.quote: we will not get to the Rs. 1,400 crores, Rs. 1,500 crores range, we will be more in the Rs. 1,300 crores, Rs. 1,400 crores range, which means that there is a drop in approximately Rs. 100 crores of revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance for full year maintained at Rs. 230-260 crores; Q4 EBITDA guidance reduced by Rs. 10 crores
items.quote: we are not changing the EBITDA guidance previously provided at Rs. 230 crores to Rs. 260 crores. And we expect Q4 is typically a high quarter for the pharma API industry, we expect that to be the case for Solara too. While we have obviously reduced our revenue guidance, we had to adjust our EBITDA guidance by about Rs. 10 crores for the quarter of Q4.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth target of low double digits over three-year horizon
items.quote: Low double digits would be a fair assumption.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin expanded 500 bps sequentially to 55%; driven by focus on profitable products, debottlenecking high-margin products, and cost improvement programs
items.quote: I am also pleased with the gross margin expansion of 500 basis points and that is a good start point for us to build a business from there.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reached 20% in Q3; target 20-23% over three years with consolidation strategy
items.quote: I do not think we can go much further from here. I think 20% to start off , and if we can have three or four consistent quarters at th ese percentage numbers, then we can start accelerating.

items.statement: Vizag facility has ~Rs. 500 crores invested; usable assets for CRAMS ~Rs. 250-300 crores; additional Rs. 100-150 crores capex needed over next three years
items.quote: We probably need to invest at least another Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 150 crores in the next three years to achieve the goals of what we want to be.

items.statement: CRAMS business currently ~Rs. 120 crores revenue; targets Rs. 500 crores in 3-4 years with 35-40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: I think we can triple or even quadruple our turnover from the current Rs. 120 crores. We do have a nice pipeline. And with a new arrangement that is being proposed, we think in about three to four years we can get to that Rs. 500-odd crores number.

items.statement: CRAMS demerger expected to take 12-15 months including NCLT process (9-12 months) and shareholder/regulatory approvals
items.quote: Consequent to all of this successfully getting completed and obviously subject to shareholder approvals and other regulatory approvals, which would take upwards of between 12 and 15 months.

items.statement: Plan to push down ~Rs. 200 crores of debt into new CRAMS entity; Solara retained business targets debt/EBITDA ~1x post demerger
items.quote: pushing down about Rs. 200 crores of debt into the new CRAMS business and also funding it separately as and when it's required. It just gives the ability for the Solara's retain business to be significantly asset balance sheet, I mean, a lighter balance sheet.

items.statement: 76% of business from regulated markets; ibuprofen ~34% of turnover; portfolio maximization via new geographies for existing products
items.quote: 76% of our business continues to be in the regulated market. So, they are very sticky businesses. There are long term partnerships where we would rather service those customers and increase the wallet share than trying to expand markets at price.

items.statement: Demand sustained for high-margin products that drove gross margin expansion; new market extensions and customer seeding to drive tepid top-line growth
items.quote: And we see a demand for these two products, which would sustain in the coming quarters.

items.statement: R&D team currently combined; plan to add 100+ scientists for CRAMS division in next 12 months post demerger
items.quote: We think that we will end up adding at least 100 new scientists for our CRAMS division in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Ibuprofen block at Vizag to be retrofitted for different segment; update announcement expected next quarter
items.quote: That ibuprofen block has to be retrofitted because we plan to convert that into a different segment, which we will shortly make certain update announcements in the next quarter.

items.statement: Carve-out of Vizag facility will not impact core catalog capacity for 2-3 years; current utilization ~65%
items.quote: The carving out of the Vizag facility will not impact on our capacity for the next at least foreseeable two to three years, in our core catalog business, as we currently operate the business at around 65% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Other expenses reduced to Rs. 56 crores in Q3 via site mothballing (Vizag, Mysore) and cost reduction measures; trend sustained over last four quarters
items.quote: See, over the last four quarters our OPEX has been coming down, it's mainly because of mothballing of sites we have worked on Vizag and Mysore sites. Plus, we have also taken some cost reduction measures in other sites which have brought down this cost.

items.statement: Debt reduced significantly; currently sub 2.5x debt/EBITDA vs 6x six quarters ago; target under 1.5x in 12-14 months post carve-out
items.quote: If you look at our debt book, we are now sub 2 times debt to EBITDA, I mean, 2.5 times debt to EBITDA, compared to almost 6 times when we started this reset journey about six quarters ago. And we expect the debt to be under 1 time, 1.5 times in the next 12, 14 months, after the carve out is complete.

items.statement: Overall market demand remains subdued but early signs of improvement are visible; industry appears to have begun recovery path.
items.quote: Overall, the market situation continues to remain subdued in terms of demand but we are beginning to see a faint sense of improvement in the market.

items.statement: Finished goods pricing has almost stabilized with no further downward revision; some key raw materials showing uptick.
items.quote: On the pricing, not fairly but I would say almost stabilized. So now we are not seeing any kind of downward revision to pricing.

items.statement: Gross profit margin expected to stabilize around 45% as new agro products with higher raw material consumption replace higher-margin PTC and SDA volumes.
items.quote: Roughly in the range of 45%.

items.statement: New plant at Dahej site for agro intermediates expected to be ready for production in Q4 FY2026.
items.quote: We expect the plant to be ready for production in Q4 of FY 2026.

items.statement: Four new MNC customers onboarded for SDAs in 2024; two ready to begin commercial supplies from April 2025, two already ramping volumes.
items.quote: The other two large customers with whom we got approved in 2024 for various applications are now ready to begin actual commercial supplies from us from April 2025.

items.statement: Two new MNC customers onboarded for PTCs in recyclable plastic application; shipments commenced, business to ramp over 6-8 months.
items.quote: We have successfully onboarded two new MNC customers. The commercial business with both these customers have begun as on date.

items.statement: All four agro intermediates under approval to commercialize in CY2025; two largest products to see regular shipments from April/May 2025.
items.quote: All 4 agro products definitely getting into full-scale commercialization from this year 2025.

items.statement: Electrolyte salt demand gaining momentum; qualification with key hybrid car battery customer progressing, pilot scale-up expected by April 2025.
items.quote: we expect to run the scale up at pilot level by the month of April.

items.statement: Monoglyme trials at 100kg catalyst level to begin; 1000kg equipment delivery expected by end FY25, commercialization by June 2025.
items.quote: Installation and commercialization are projected to be completed by June 2025, marking a key milestone in our operational expansion.

items.statement: First commercial supply of flame retardant to begin in current quarter; full commercialization only when pricing conditions improve.
items.quote: We are set to begin the first commercial supply to the customer in the current quarter.

items.statement: Distillation plant started in January, expected to free 12-15% reactor capacity for major products and new agro product distillation.
items.quote: I would not have the exact number, but I think it should give us at least 12% to 15% of free space in the plant.

items.statement: Existing plant expected to be almost fully occupied by June/July 2025; combined with new plant, revenue potential exceeds INR 900 crores.
items.quote: we definitely have the chances to cross our revenue of more than INR900 crores with the existing and upcoming capacities.

items.statement: Semiconductor-grade TMAH purity at 38-60 PPB vs required <1 PPB; targeting qualification in 4-6 months, would be first Indian company to achieve this.
items.quote: So as of today, if you ask me, honestly, we are still in the range of about 38 to 60 PPB when it comes to the final product.

items.statement: SDA demand recovery driven by end-market pickup in IC/hybrid engines and gradual China ramp-up; customers advising preparation for volume surge.
items.quote: We are seeing very encouraging signs coming in from the end-use customers, seeing demand uptick in terms of IC engines and hybrid engines.

items.statement: Electrolyte salt sales to smoothen out from April as customer production lines stabilized and regular consistent demand expected.
items.quote: It will smoothen out from April. So dispatch is beginning from April, it will definitely smoothen out in terms of consistent sales that is happening.

items.statement: US policy shift away from EVs seen as potentially positive for SDA business (hybrid vehicles), not negative for electrolyte salts.
items.quote: It might indirectly benefit us in some way but still time will tell what will happen. So it's not going to be a negative impact for the business.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Price increases implemented across 5 products covering ~65% of retail health portfolio; blended impact 8-9% targeting 10-12% annualized yield per product
items.quote: We have had to align our product pricing strategy to match the market reality. Up to Jan 25, we have implemented price increase across 5 products which is approximately 65% of our retail health portfolio.

items.statement: Targeting 18% growth to double top line from FY24 by FY28 under IFRS path
items.quote: More than anything, I think we should be focusing more on the IFRS path towards Financial Year '28 and whether we can keep growing at the rate which we have envisaged, which is 18%-odd, reaching and doubling our top line from Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Agency force 761,000 agents (+19,000 net in Q3); 66,000 recruited in 9M; 69 banca partners added Bajaj Finance and NeoGrowth
items.quote: Our agency strength has increased to 7,61,000 agents with net addition of 19,000 agents in the December quarter. The agent recruitment number has now reached 66,000 in the first nine months of this financial year.

items.statement: Reinsurance ceded ~6.3% steady state; RI commission deferred under 1/N accounting; no treaty change
items.quote: The reinsurance ceded is about 6.3% or so. Will this be the steady state going ahead? Nilesh Kambli: Yes, it will be in the similar range going forward

items.statement: Q4 largest premium quarter; pricing interventions in Dec/Jan to improve financials going ahead
items.quote: We are excited about Quarter 4, which is the largest quarter in terms of the premium for us. With the pricing intervention taken in December and Jan '25, the financials will continue to improve going ahead.

items.statement: Group business 4% of portfolio; SME/mid-corporate focus unchanged despite elevated loss ratios; corrective pricing/selection underway
items.quote: On the Group side, I had mentioned in my opening remarks is a small business that's 4% of our portfolio, focusing largely on SME and mid -corporates but yes, there has been a d eterioration in the loss ratios on the Group side for industry and as well as for Star Health

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% maintained; long-term goal to double revenue to INR1,000 crores by FY27
items.quote: We remain confident in achieving our revenue growth guidance of 20% while maintaining strong margins. Our long -term goal of doubling revenue to INR1,000 crores by financial year '27 remains firmly on track

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 34% to 36% for FY25
items.quote: for the full financial year, we would like to guide an EBITDA margin of 34% to 36%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 capex expected to close around INR120 crores to INR130 crores
items.quote: For the full year, we expect capex to close around INR120 crores to INR130 crores, primarily directed towards the refurbishment of block A, B and C at our Lote facility and development at Ambernath plant.

items.statement: Exports contributed 85% of revenue in Q3 FY25, up from 74% a year ago; regulated markets share ~45%
items.quote: This quarter, exports contributed 85% of our total revenue, up from 74% in the -- same period last year, reflecting our increasing penetration into regulated markets that command premium pricing.

items.statement: LATAM revenue share grew to 21% in Q3 FY25 from 8% a year ago; full LATAM potential seen at INR200 crores over 2-3 years
items.quote: LATAM region, in particular, has demonstrated remarkable growth, contributing 21% of the revenue this quarter compared to 8% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Backward integrated products contribute 77% of revenue; target is fully backward integrated basket
items.quote: Today, backward integrated products are almost contributing to 77% of our total revenue, and we intend to keep that trend upwards. We want to grow that trend. And we would like to have a fully backward integrated basket.

items.statement: Module E block commissioned adding 335 KLPD, total capacity over 1,000 KLPD; INR125 crores invested, peak revenue by FY27
items.quote: We have invested a total of INR125 crores in the newly inaugurated Module E manufacturing block, which is expected to achieve its peak revenue contribution by FY '27.

items.statement: CMO/CDMO opportunities at negotiation stage; revenue impact expected from FY27; CMO to contribute ~20% of revenue by FY27
items.quote: On the whole as CMO, including the current opportunities what we have and the new opportunities which are there in our pipeline, we expect in FY '27, CMO to contribute closer to 20% of the total revenue.

items.statement: New product launches: at least 4 annually; Q4 FY25 launches include 2 new products; contrast media first launch Q2 FY26; Ambernath formulation site revenue from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our strategy includes launching at least 4 new products annually, ensuring we remain at the forefront of innovation of API manufacturing.

items.statement: No gross margin guidance provided; management refuses product-level pricing disclosure
items.quote: So Aditya, we never guide on gross margin. So I will not be able to give any guidance even today on gross margin.

items.statement: North America currently 4-5% of revenue; expected to grow to ~10% in next 3-4 years; Europe and LATAM to remain larger markets
items.quote: We are expecting it to grow to almost 10% in the next 3 to 4 years. But like I said, Europe and LATAM will continue to be the larger markets for us.

items.statement: DSM-Firmenich project: first commercial supply 5-10 MT in Q4 FY25; firm forecast of 25-30 MT for FY26; full potential by FY27
items.quote: We have got about 25, 30 metric ton of forecast from them. So the project is moving really well. And we are on target of taking it to full potential by FY '27.

items.statement: API pricing erosion minimal due to backward integration; growth driven by volumes and regulated market penetration
items.quote: Although, overall, yes, there is some erosion happening in the API prices because we have a very strong backward integrated model in place, for our set of products, we are not seeing that kind of erosion.

items.statement: Confident to touch INR1,000 crore monthly SIP book by March 2025
items.quote: We have added INR280 crores to our SIP book in last 12 months, and we are confident to touch the mark of INR1,000 crores by March 2025.

items.statement: January SIP numbers expected higher than November and December
items.quote: Probably January business would be higher than what we did in the month of November, December.

items.statement: January net sales expected higher than November
items.quote: We are very, very confident that net sales also will be higher than what we did in November.

items.statement: Opex growth expected at 12% to 14% for next year
items.quote: Overall, we expect that the next year growth -- looking at the current year base, then 12% to 14% should be the range for operating expenditure, which include the employee costs also.

items.statement: Added almost 16 branches in current fiscal, incremental opex from rent, electricity, conveyance
items.quote: So actually the opex also, if you look at the current fiscal we added almost 16 branches. Incremental cost is visible on the opex side, mainly because of rent, electricity, conveyance because this is all related to branch expansion.

items.statement: Payout ratio increased from 63.4% to 64.6% due to additional trail provision of INR3 crore in Q3
items.quote: Sequentially, the payout ratio has increased from 63.4% to 64.6%, so let me just try and address this also. So by end of second quarter, that is the end of September quarter, we rolled out a scheme of additional trail for our partners based on the net sales did by them in the current financial year.

items.statement: Additional INR6 crore provision for trail over two quarters, INR3 crore in Q3 and balance in Q4
items.quote: Hence, we need to provide additional 6 crore towards this. And out of the 6 crore, we have done an extra provision of 3 crore in this quarter. And balance, we will be providing based on the actual number in the March quarter.

items.statement: Percentage margins sustainable, absolute margin may decline as scheme size grows
items.quote: Obviously, percentage margins, we'll be able to maintain. Absolute margin might come down because as the size of the scheme grows, the receivable comes down.

items.statement: Retail sentiment intact, net sales in first 9 months 50% higher than full FY24, redemption ratio 44% vs 60% historic average
items.quote: Our net sales in first 9 months is 50% higher than what we did in last full fiscal of 2024. The redemption ratio at 44% within the last quarter is much lower than the 30-quarter historic average of 60%.

items.statement: Monthly SIP run rate of INR20 crore continuing in current month
items.quote: Our monthly run rate of adding 20 crores SIPs is still continuing, and we are continuing to add the same number in the current month also.

items.statement: P2P distribution stopped from August due to RBI regulations, revenue dropped from INR2.56 crore in Q2 to INR43 lakh in Q3
items.quote: In FY '24, we earned a gross revenue of INR13 crores from P2P distribution. And in first 9 months of the current fiscal, our revenue stands at INR6.6 crores. If you look at the bifurcation of first 9 months, the last quarter alone, which is the quarter period previous to this quarter, that means September quarter alone, we earned INR2.56 crores. And the December quarter, we earned INR43 lakhs only

items.statement: PMS/AIF average AUM doubled to INR1,060 crore in 9M FY25 from INR605 crore in FY24, closing AUM INR1,270 crore
items.quote: Our average AUM PMS, AIF in first 9 months of the current fiscal has doubled to INR1,060 crores from full year average of INR605 crores of last year. Our closing AUM in the PMS, AIF segment as on 31st December was INR1,270 crore.

items.statement: Few AMCs cut commissions on historical assets, impact already absorbed, gross margins maintained
items.quote: So today, if you see, I think hardly four, five AMCs have cut the commission on the historical assets and that too on -- not on all schemes. So only time will say that I think which all AMCs and which all schemes they cut the commission, but till now whatever they have cut is already absorbed in the system. And you can see that, I think, we could be able to maintain the margins on the gross side.

items.statement: Life insurance volumes lower than exceptional FY23, but January better than previous quarter
items.quote: We might not be able to see the numbers what we did in 2023, but compared to the last quarter, definitely we have done the better number till now in the month of January. And we are hoping to continue similar kind of number in the next 2, 3 months.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 23-24%
items.quote: The target is to stay around 23-24% EBITDA margins and any increase in revenue will immediately add to the EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Target utilization of 85%
items.quote: Actually the target is 85%. So, uh, we are working to constantly towards that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved YoY despite appraisal costs
items.quote: Note that our approval cycle hit in October, and therefore, this quarter has the impact of increasing payroll cost across the company. And despite that, we've been able to have a better margin as compared to December 23.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin ~18.5% on revenue of 97 crores
items.quote: Even though the revenue is not growing as fast, the margins are growing faster. So that is good news in a sense that yes, we are going in the right direction.

items.statement: US environment better than six months ago but no animal spirits
items.quote: I think the cautious, my mood is still cautious in my mind. Customers are de ﬁnitely looking positive because Trump has always been pro-corporates. So their environment is de ﬁnitely there. I don't think it is animal spirits anywhere to be seen at this point in time. But regardless of that, the environment is better as compared to what it was six months ago

items.statement: Revenue stuck in 95-100 crore range for ~10 quarters
items.quote: We have been trying multiple things and there have been one or the other clients moving away which is causing this pain. But at the same time, we've been able to get new clients who are able to ﬁll the gap. However, the end result remains the same we are in that 95 to 100 crore range

items.statement: Europe and UAE share increasing, US share slightly reduced
items.quote: Interestingly, Europe is, you know, increasing the pie, the size of its pie. Usually, a year ago, I would say 80% was US, 10% was Europe, and 10% was UAE plus India. Today, both UAE and Europe are increasing their share in the pie, and US is slightly reduced.

items.statement: German revenue nearly doubled YoY via Materna/Agenio partnership
items.quote: And you can see the European market, which is German revenue is almost doubled from what it used to be a year ago. So yes, good progress in that sense.

items.statement: Investing heavily in sales across US, Germany, Middle East
items.quote: we have hired Harmeet as the CRO and we will have more salespeople coming and joining us. So that will impact the margin deﬁnitely for that quarter, but if I were to look at a longer period, at least 12 to 18 months, we will be able to recover everything that we have spent in the initial quarters in order to grow the business

items.statement: Six new clients onboarded, starting at $100K-$200K each
items.quote: See we are a services company and typically any new client that starts with us will start with a small project. And these projects, typically when I look at all these six clients, we probably are looking at 100K to 200K worth of work to begin with.

items.statement: Revenue dip in December quarter due to holiday billing hours
items.quote: December quarters are usually lower quarters in terms of the billing availability and the number of billing hours available for the month or the quarter, because of Dussehra, Diwali, holidays in India, and then Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays in the U.S.

items.statement: No active M&A pipeline currently
items.quote: Nothing worth mentioning right now, therefore we did not put anything this time. There is nothing that is going on.

items.statement: Net headcount reduced by 43 for cost optimization
items.quote: Yeah, so we reduced our net count by 43 people to be precise. We have done a bit of a cost optimization here.

items.statement: Current utilization at 79%
items.quote: So we are at 79%. We are striving to improve it further.

items.statement: Passing on cost increases to customers gradually
items.quote: Now in that environment, obviously you cannot maintain the same margin just o ǣ the bat. It has to, I mean we are passing on the cost to the customers slowly and gradually and the results have to be seen in the last three quarters, the margins have started to show improvements

items.statement: EBITDA margins will remain in the range of 40% to 45%
items.quote: And overall, the EBITDA margins will remain in the range of 40% to 45% that we have been maintaining.

items.statement: Capex of INR 60-70 crores planned for coming year
items.quote: So cash flows vis-a-vis capex, we are looking to be bringing in another INR60 crores to INR70 crores in the coming year.

items.statement: Nine international contracts signed but not yet transitioned; revenue to clock in subsequent quarters
items.quote: There are close to about nine asset management companies, which are in transition of delivery. We have announced them in Q2 and some in Q1 and of course, some of them now. As I've said, it takes roughly about 2 to 3 quarters depending upon the size and complexity of the contract for us to be able to transition it. And hence, the revenue for these 9 contracts is yet to be clocked and goes well, hop

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 44.1% for Q3 FY25, down 10 bps sequentially due to seasonality
items.quote: EBITDA margins, as I talked about, have seen a sequential dip of 10 bps, but that's more to do with some bit of seasonality that we have seen. Otherwise, in terms of the overall results, they are still 44.1%.

items.statement: International deal sizes increased from ~INR 1 crore to INR 3-3.5 crores per annum; pipeline deals near $1 million each
items.quote: On an average, the deal sizes earlier used to be anywhere about INR1 crores or so per annum recurring right annuity. That deal size now, if I average out the last 6 deals that we have signed, has now expanded to over nearly about INR3 crores to INR3.5 crores, right? And the deals that we are now in the pipeline are closer to $1 million in terms of each deal that we are looking to work with.

items.statement: Mutual fund net flows 20% higher in Q3 vs Q2, offsetting 4-4.5% mark-to-market correction
items.quote: And however, that got compensated by higher net flows. The net flows in Q3 were 20% higher as compared to Q2 of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Non-mutual fund revenue target raised to 50% of total book over 3-5 years from current ~35%
items.quote: We continue to track to the trajectory of getting the non-mutual fund businesses to be near about 50-odd percent over the next 3 to 5-year horizon.

items.statement: Revenue sensitivity: 4-5% sequential decline if markets drop with no net flow offset; 65% revenue still equity-linked
items.quote: Clearly, if there is a significant drop with no offset happening in the form of net flows, we will have probably adverse impact anywhere between 4% to 5% decline in revenue sequentially, so to speak.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents of INR 570 crores available for business expansion, M&A, and dividends per Board policy
items.quote: We remain cash positive. We have a dry powder of almost INR570 crores sitting in cash and cash equivalents, which we will utilize as per the Board policy for business expansion, M&A and the Board policy at the year-end in terms of looking at dividend payout if the Board considers that.

items.statement: BlackRock Aladdin partnership signed; 108 funds and ~$10 trillion addressable opportunity; go-to-market strategy under discussion
items.quote: One of the biggest accomplishments we've had in the previous quarter was to sign with BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager to be in their list of marquee fund administrator, only eight, and we are the ninth one across the globe for implementation of Aladdin.

items.statement: Wealth platform mPower Wealth launched; 5 large contracts signed in 3 months including Tata Capital, Aditya Birla Wealth; revenue to start next quarter
items.quote: Wealth revenue will start coming in from next quarter, I mean, in JFM.

items.statement: Hexagram revenue grew 60% YoY to INR 9.5 crores for 9 months ended December
items.quote: Hexagram had a revenue of about INR9.5 crores for 9 months ended December versus about INR6 crores for the same period last year. So it's a 60% plus growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Pension business grew 35% vs industry 12%; reached breakeven; market share near 10%
items.quote: Industry has grown at about 12%. We've grown about 35%. And this quarter also marks the breakeven in this line of business, which means into the coming quarters as the number of pensioners expand.

items.statement: Alternatives AUM grew 55% YoY to over INR 1.4 trillion; market share ~37% by fund count; win rate >60% domestic, ~75% GIFT City
items.quote: The AUM growth has been substantive at about close to 55% year-on-year, bringing our total assets under management to over INR1.4 trillion.

items.statement: Corporate registry added 366 clients in Q3, ~1,000 in 9 months; folio count up 8 million; revenue growing 24%+ YoY, 20% CAGR over 3-4 years
items.quote: We have added close to 366 clients in the last quarter. In the 9 months of this year, that's roughly about 1,000-odd new client contracts we have added. The total folio count has expanded by about 8 million.

items.statement: International client base at 70, contracts at 90; signed 2 full-service tier deals in Philippines, 1 large deal in Malaysia, 2 LOIs in Malaysia
items.quote: In the quarter that had gone by, we have signed two full service tier deals from a large asset management company and the trust, and these are based out of Philippines. We have also signed a large -- another large deal in Malaysia, and we have received two letters of intent, which are being in the process of being converted into letter of awards in the coming weeks from a significant sized custodi

items.statement: Highest ever EBITDA margin of 12.5% in Q3 FY25, up 180 bps YoY; 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 12.2%, up 205 bps YoY
items.quote: I am glad that we have delivered the highest ever EBITDA margin of 12.5% in Q3 FY25, which is 180 basis points higher than Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Aim to sustain current EBITDA margin level and improve gradually in subsequent quarters depending on two-wheeler industry growth
items.quote: Our aim is to sustain this level of EBITDA margins and improve gradually in the subsequent quarters depending upon the growth of the two-wheeler industry.

items.statement: Invested Rs. 475 crore in Karoli plant to date and continuously investing up to Rs. 200 crore in 18th manufacturing facility in Bangalore
items.quote: We invested Rs. 475 crore in the Karoli plant till date and we are continuously investing up to Rs. 200 crore in the 18th manufacturing facility in Bangalore.

items.statement: Invested Rs. 600 crore total which will see through next 18 months; will invest more when opportunities arise
items.quote: We have invested Rs. 600 crore and this will see us through for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Export order of Rs. 100 crore for Ford Motor under testing, expected to start beginning of next financial year
items.quote: We have got an export order of Rs. 100 crore for Ford Motor, but that is under testing. We have already given the samples and once the approvals come, and then that will start hopefully in the beginning of the next financial year.

items.statement: EV component content 30-50% higher than ICE; EV share of business 5% of total vehicle production
items.quote: The EV component because we are into very critical lightweighting and thermal management products. In EV, the component is higher, it's 30% to 50% higher in EV.

items.statement: ICE contribution 76% of business, EV contribution about 5% in current quarter
items.quote: So, the ICE contribution is 76% in our business and the EV contribution is about 5%.

items.statement: Exports may not grow this year as European customers consume pipeline inventories; Q4 exports trying to be better than Q3 and Q2
items.quote: In spite of such good results, we would like to tell the investors that our exports may not grow this particular year because the customers, very prominent customers, they are first consuming the vast inventories in the pipeline.

items.statement: Expect to outperform industry growth in subsequent quarter of FY25; anticipate two-wheeler growth momentum to continue for remaining part of year
items.quote: As we go forward, we are hopeful of maintaining trend of outperforming industry growth in the subsequent quarter of FY25. We anticipate the growth momentum in two-wheeler sector to continue for the remaining part of the year with prevailing positive market sentiments.

items.statement: Bengaluru 18th manufacturing facility commercialized on 14th January 2025; QAV expected to finish by March, good stream level from next financial year
items.quote: Our 18 th manufacturing facility at Bengaluru, incidentally that is our third plant in southern India, in Bengaluru. It has commercialized on 14th January 2025

items.statement: Solar power plant of 9.9 MW in Sirsa, Haryana started trial production on 27th January 2025 for captive consumption
items.quote: Solar power plant of 9.9 megawatt in Sirsa, Haryana for captive consumption started trial production on 27th January 2025 and will start supply of power soon.

items.statement: Rajasthan plant subsidy of Rs. 6.65 crore received in Q3 FY25; similar figure of around Rs. 7 crore to continue in forthcoming quarters
items.quote: is about Rs. 6.65 crore subsidy from the Karoli plant in the Q3. Joseph George: Understood. Kuldip Singh Rathee: Now onwards, a similar figure of around Rs. 7 crore will continue in the forthcoming quarters also

items.statement: Karoli plant utilization between 45% and 50%; asset turnover target of 2x
items.quote: So, the utilization percentage is similar, between 45% and 50%. But now the capacities are further ahead, and we expect that the coming years growth shall be very much taken care of from there.

items.statement: AISIN JV aftermarket launch planned for Q1 FY26; targeting breakeven in first year
items.quote: We are in the process of appointing dealers all over the country and we hope to launch the operations in Q1 FY26 as we had always told before.

items.statement: Debt-equity closed at 0.42 last year; likely to close at 0.38 this year despite heavy investment; target 0.3 next year
items.quote: I am happy to share that last year we closed at a debt equity of 0.42. And in spite of such a heavy investment, we will be most likely closing at a debt equity of 0.38. Further next year our target is 0.3.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance: 24-26% AUM growth, Opex to net total income 14-15%, GNPA 40-60 bps, credit cost 20-25 bps, provisioning coverage 40-50%, ROA 2-2.2%, leverage 7-8x, ROE 13-15%
items.value: 24-26% AUM growth; Opex/NII 14-15%; GNPA 40-60 bps; credit cost 20-25 bps; coverage 40-50%; ROA 2-2.2%; leverage 7-8x; ROE 13-15%
items.quote: We estimate in the medium term 24% to 26% AUM growth, Opex to net total income to go down to 14 % to 15% from in the current quarter it came to 19.8%, GNPA at 40 bps to 60 bps. Credit cost remaining sideways between 20 to 25 bps. Provisioning coverage at 40 % to 50%. ROA is of a 2% to 2.2% with leverage of 7 to 8 times. Thus ROE of 13% to 15% in the medium term horizon.

items.statement: No dedicated branches for affordable vertical; will use existing branches where present and set up new BHFL branches in new geographies for all products
items.quote: The geographies where we are commonly present with the other segments, it will be the same branches, but where geographies, there will be geographies which we are going to cover through this segment where we are not existingly operating, we will set up the branches for those markets for this particular.

items.statement: Developer finance AUM grew 59% YoY to under Rs 13,000 crore across 738 active projects; management expects mix to rise from 12% to 12-15% of portfolio
items.quote: Our book which we had mentioned has grown at a faster pace, but at absolute level we are still less than Rs. 13,000 crore kind of a book, which is across 738 active projects.

items.statement: Gross spread stable at 1.9%; NIM dipped to 4% from 4.1% sequentially and YoY; medium-term spread corridor 1.7-2.2%
items.quote: Gross spread remains constant at 1.9%. NIM dropped slightly to 4% against a 4.1% on a sequential basis and also on a YOY basis.

items.statement: Cost of funds peaked at 7.9% and stable QoQ; full pass-through achieved; 30% of total liabilities linked to external benchmark, 13% to MCLR
items.quote: Cost of funds was stable at 7.9% from the last quarter indicating that the cost of funds have peaked out and the pass-through of all cost of funds has been there in the balance sheet.

items.statement: Residential real estate saw slowness in growth and lower launches in first 9M FY25; sales drop attributed to fewer launches, not demand weakness at launch counters
items.quote: the first nine months of F Y25 residential real estate has witnessed slowness in growth versus last year. So I'll say slowness in growth versus last year and there is an overall sale drop also as what has been reported by few agencies Bajaj Housing Finance January 27, 2025 but in terms of a market sizing and in terms of their the launches have been

items.statement: Portfolio mix stable: HL 57%, LRD 19%, DF 12%, LAP 10%; affordable/near-prime vertical started May-Jun 2024, expected meaningful AUM contribution from FY26-27; affordable to remain 5-10% of HL book, not 5% of total book
items.quote: Broadly, overall, portfolio mix remains stable with slight movement between the products. HL at 57%, LAP at 10%, LRD at 19%, and DF at 12%.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 29 bps, NNPA 13 bps; Stage 2 at 37 bps (regulatory 31-90 DPD only 8 bps); only 2 DCCO extensions ever, 1 closed, 1 NPA; no DCCO extension in last year; construction finance risk managed via granularity (738 projects), sweep f
items.quote: GNPA stood at 29 bps as against 25 bps on Q3 FY24 and 29 bps of preceding quarter. NNPA at 13 bps against 10 bps of Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.15% net of Rs 10 cr overlay release (0.20% gross); overlay fully released; balance transfer out stable at ~12% annualized
items.quote: Overall credit cost gross of overlay release in this quarter was 0.20% which is because there's a Rs. 10 crore overlay release because 0.15% is net of overlay release.
